<hr data-start="2459" data-end="2462">
<h2 data-start="2464" data-end="2491">What to commit vs ignore</h2>
<p data-start="2492" data-end="2499">Commit:</p>
<ul data-start="2500" data-end="2643">
<li data-start="2500" data-end="2518">
<p data-start="2502" data-end="2518"><code data-start="2502" data-end="2518">pyproject.toml</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2519" data-end="2606">
<p data-start="2521" data-end="2606"><code data-start="2521" data-end="2530">uv.lock</code> (this is your reproducibility anchor) <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 63px;"><a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 63px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Astral Docs</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2607" data-end="2643">
<p data-start="2609" data-end="2643">your notebooks, <code data-start="2625" data-end="2631">src/</code>, docs, etc.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2645" data-end="2652">Ignore:</p>
<ul data-start="2653" data-end="2751">
<li data-start="2653" data-end="2683">
<p data-start="2655" data-end="2683"><code data-start="2655" data-end="2663">.venv/</code> (local environment)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2684" data-end="2751">
<p data-start="2686" data-end="2751">big local data files (unless the course requires them in the zip)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2753" data-end="2914"><code data-start="2753" data-end="2757">uv</code>’s docs are explicit that <code data-start="2783" data-end="2790">.venv</code> is the isolated env folder and <code data-start="2822" data-end="2831">uv.lock</code> is the lockfile meant for version control. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 63px;"><a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 63px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Astral Docs</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<hr data-start="2916" data-end="2919">
<h2 data-start="2921" data-end="2971">If the course/grader expects <code data-start="2953" data-end="2971">requirements.txt</code></h2>
<p data-start="2972" data-end="3070">You <em data-start="2976" data-end="2981">can</em> generate one from <code data-start="3000" data-end="3009">uv.lock</code> using <strong data-start="3016" data-end="3029">uv export</strong>: <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 77px;"><a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/export/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/export/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 77px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Astral Docs</span><span class="-me-1 flex h-full items-center rounded-full px-1 text-[#8F8F8F]">+1</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="3071" data-end="3149"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>uv </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">export</span></span><span> --format requirements.txt --output-file requirements.txt
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="3151" data-end="3345">Astral notes they generally <strong data-start="3179" data-end="3215">don’t recommend maintaining both</strong> <code data-start="3216" data-end="3225">uv.lock</code> and <code data-start="3230" data-end="3248">requirements.txt</code> long-term, but exporting is exactly what it’s there for. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 63px;"><a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/export/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/export/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 63px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Astral Docs</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<hr data-start="3347" data-end="3350">
<h2 data-start="3352" data-end="3404">The useful <code data-start="3366" data-end="3371">.md</code> files (lightweight but high-ROI)</h2>
<p data-start="3405" data-end="3487">For this course (and your “shadow leadership” reality), these pay off immediately:</p>
<ul data-start="3489" data-end="3820">
<li data-start="3489" data-end="3569">
<p data-start="3491" data-end="3569"><code data-start="3491" data-end="3502">README.md</code> — how to run + repo map (this is your “show your work” front door)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3570" data-end="3660">
<p data-start="3572" data-end="3660"><code data-start="3572" data-end="3590">PROCESS_DIARY.md</code> — 3 entries required; keep it running instead of reconstructing later</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3661" data-end="3725">
<p data-start="3663" data-end="3725"><code data-start="3663" data-end="3677">DECISIONS.md</code> — why you chose model X, dropped option C, etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3726" data-end="3820">
<p data-start="3728" data-end="3820"><code data-start="3728" data-end="3743">DATA_NOTES.md</code> (or <code data-start="3748" data-end="3768">DATA_DICTIONARY.md</code>) — what each field means, known quirks, assumptions</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3822" data-end="4054">If you want, paste your current repo tree (or tell me what you’ve already created), and I’ll give you a <strong data-start="3926" data-end="3989">tight CRISP-DM-aligned folder structure + starter templates</strong> for those markdown files that match the assignment deliverables.</p>

whole SSH setup:</p>
<ul data-start="62" data-end="199">
<li data-start="62" data-end="81">
<p data-start="64" data-end="81">Key generated ✅</p>
</li>
<li data-start="82" data-end="106">
<p data-start="84" data-end="106">Added to ssh-agent ✅</p>
</li>
<li data-start="107" data-end="130">
<p data-start="109" data-end="130">Public key copied ✅</p>
</li>
<li data-start="131" data-end="199">
<p data-start="133" data-end="199"><code data-start="133" data-end="156">ssh -T git@github.com</code> returns <em data-start="165" data-end="195">“successfully authenticated”</em> ✅</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="201" data-end="240">That means Git over SSH is ready to go.</p>
<p data-start="242" data-end="375">Now let’s finish the setup cleanly on Pop!_OS: repo + structure + (optional) <code data-start="319" data-end="323">uv</code> env + the <code data-start="334" data-end="339">.md</code> docs that make the course painless.</p>
<hr data-start="377" data-end="380">
<h2 data-start="382" data-end="430">1) (If you haven’t yet) add the key to GitHub</h2>
<p data-start="431" data-end="610">You already copied the public key output. If you haven’t pasted it into GitHub yet:<br>
GitHub → <strong data-start="524" data-end="569">Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key</strong> → paste the full <code data-start="587" data-end="604">ssh-ed25519 ...</code> line.</p>
<p data-start="612" data-end="667">(Your <code data-start="618" data-end="626">ssh -T</code> success implies you likely already did.)</p>
<hr data-start="669" data-end="672">
<h2 data-start="674" data-end="725">2) Create your course repo on GitHub (fast path)</h2>
<h3 data-start="726" data-end="775">Option A: Create on GitHub website (simplest)</h3>
<ol data-start="776" data-end="988">
<li data-start="776" data-end="821">
<p data-start="779" data-end="821">Create a new repo: <code data-start="798" data-end="821">case-studies-capstone</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="822" data-end="850">
<p data-start="825" data-end="850">Choose <strong data-start="832" data-end="843">Private</strong> (fine)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="851" data-end="903">
<p data-start="854" data-end="903">Don’t add README or .gitignore (we’ll do locally)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="904" data-end="988">
<p data-start="907" data-end="988">Copy the SSH URL (looks like <code data-start="936" data-end="987">git@github.com:USERNAME/case-studies-capstone.git</code>)</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="990" data-end="995">Then:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="997" data-end="1127"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">mkdir</span></span><span> -p ~/projects
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span></span><span> ~/projects
git </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">clone</span></span><span> git@github.com:USERNAME/case-studies-capstone.git
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span></span><span> case-studies-capstone
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<h3 data-start="1129" data-end="1165">Option B: If you want CLI (<code data-start="1160" data-end="1164">gh</code>)</h3>
<p data-start="1166" data-end="1199">Only if you already installed it:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1200" data-end="1291"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>gh repo create case-studies-capstone --private --</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">clone</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">cd</span></span><span> case-studies-capstone
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<hr data-start="1293" data-end="1296">
<h2 data-start="1298" data-end="1365">3) Drop in the “Show Your Work” repo skeleton (course-optimized)</h2>
<p data-start="1366" data-end="1387">From inside the repo:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1389" data-end="1881"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">mkdir</span></span><span> -p data/{raw,interim,processed} notebooks src outputs/{figures,tables,models} docs reports references
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">touch</span></span><span> README.md .gitignore
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">touch</span></span><span> docs/00_master_tracker.md docs/01_process_diary.md docs/02_decision_log.md docs/03_assumptions_risks.md
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">touch</span></span><span> reports/M05_assignment1.md reports/M09_assignment2.md reports/M13_assignment3.md
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">touch</span></span><span> data/raw/.gitkeep data/interim/.gitkeep data/processed/.gitkeep
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">touch</span></span><span> outputs/figures/.gitkeep outputs/tables/.gitkeep outputs/models/.gitkeep
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<hr data-start="1883" data-end="1886">
<h2 data-start="1888" data-end="1926">4) Add <code data-start="1898" data-end="1910">.gitignore</code> (safe defaults)</h2>
<p data-start="1927" data-end="1956">Paste this into <code data-start="1943" data-end="1955">.gitignore</code>:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1958" data-end="2308"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">gitignore</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-gitignore"><span># Python
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
.env

# Jupyter
.ipynb_checkpoints/

# Editors/OS
.vscode/
.idea/
.DS_Store

# Large outputs (rebuildable)
outputs/models/
outputs/figures/
outputs/tables/

# Data (keep out of git; still include in Coursera ZIP if needed)
data/raw/
data/interim/
data/processed/

# Keep placeholder files
!.gitkeep
</span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="2310" data-end="2445"><strong data-start="2310" data-end="2331">Why this is good:</strong> you keep Git clean, but you can still include datasets in the ZIP submission separately if the course expects it.</p>
<hr data-start="2447" data-end="2450">
<h2 data-start="2452" data-end="2495">5) Use <code data-start="2462" data-end="2466">uv</code> for Python env (recommended)</h2>
<h3 data-start="2496" data-end="2529">Install <code data-start="2508" data-end="2512">uv</code> (if not already)</h3>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="2530" data-end="2589"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="2591" data-end="2675">Restart terminal (or <code data-start="2612" data-end="2630">source ~/.bashrc</code> / <code data-start="2633" data-end="2643">~/.zshrc</code> depending on your shell), then:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="2677" data-end="2701"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>uv --version
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<h3 data-start="2703" data-end="2736">Initialize project + add deps</h3>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="2737" data-end="2854"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>uv init --bare
uv add numpy pandas matplotlib scikit-learn jupyterlab scipy statsmodels seaborn ipykernel
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="2856" data-end="2879">Run Jupyter through uv:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="2880" data-end="2910"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>uv run jupyter lab
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="2912" data-end="2935"><strong data-start="2912" data-end="2935">Commit these files:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2936" data-end="2966">
<li data-start="2936" data-end="2954">
<p data-start="2938" data-end="2954"><code data-start="2938" data-end="2954">pyproject.toml</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2955" data-end="2966">
<p data-start="2957" data-end="2966"><code data-start="2957" data-end="2966">uv.lock</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2968" data-end="2995">Do <strong data-start="2971" data-end="2978">not</strong> commit <code data-start="2986" data-end="2994">.venv/</code>.</p>
<p data-start="2997" data-end="3049">If the graders want <code data-start="3017" data-end="3035">requirements.txt</code>, generate it:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="3050" data-end="3128"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>uv </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">export</span></span><span> --format requirements.txt --output-file requirements.txt
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<hr data-start="3130" data-end="3133">
<h2 data-start="3135" data-end="3191">6) Fill the key <code data-start="3154" data-end="3159">.md</code> docs (minimum viable templates)</h2>
<h3 data-start="3193" data-end="3224"><code data-start="3197" data-end="3224">docs/00_master_tracker.md</code></h3>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="3225" data-end="3701"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">md</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-md"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Master Tracker</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M9 (Assignment 2 due)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M10
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M11
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M12
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M13 (Assignment 3 + slides due)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> [ ] M14

This repository contains my end-to-end case study work for the University of Pittsburgh MDS capstone course.  
Projects are structured using the </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**CRISP-DM**</span></span><span> methodology (Business Understanding → Data Understanding → Data Preparation → Modeling → Evaluation → Deployment) and include stakeholder-ready reports plus the supporting analytical work.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## What’s in here</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Major deliverables</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 1 (Module 5):**</span></span><span> Business &amp; Data Understanding Report  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Problem framing, success criteria, EDA, data quality assessment
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 2 (Module 9):**</span></span><span> Data Preparation &amp; Modeling Report  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Cleaning, feature engineering, multiple models, model selection + evaluation
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 3 (Module 13):**</span></span><span> Final Report + Executive Slides  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Business impact interpretation, deployment feasibility, risks, recommendations, reflection

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### “Show your work” (evidence)</span></span><span>
Each report is backed by:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> notebooks that run top-to-bottom
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> figures/tables produced from analysis
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> a lightweight decision + assumptions trail (docs/)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Repository structure</span></span><span>

</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1361" data-end="1531">notebooks/          # Jupyter notebooks (EDA → prep → modeling → evaluation)<br>

tables/           # Exported tables used in reports<br>

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; Note: Large data files may be excluded from Git for size/privacy reasons, but will be included in the course submission ZIP when required.</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## How to run this project</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Option A — Using `uv` (recommended)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> Install </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`uv`</span></span><span> (if needed):  
   </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> From the repo root:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">   -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`uv sync`</span></span><span> (creates/updates </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`.venv`</span></span><span>)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">   -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`uv run jupyter lab`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Option B — Using venv + pip</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`python3 -m venv .venv`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`source .venv/bin/activate`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`pip install -r requirements.txt`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`jupyter lab`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Notebooks (suggested flow)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`01_data_inventory.ipynb`</span></span><span> — dataset overview + grain + keys + joins
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`02_eda.ipynb`</span></span><span> — distributions, missingness, anomalies, initial hypotheses
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`03_cleaning.ipynb`</span></span><span> — cleaning logic + exclusions + data quality fixes
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`04_feature_engineering.ipynb`</span></span><span> — features + leakage checks
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`05_modeling_baselines.ipynb`</span></span><span> — simple baselines for comparison
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`06_modeling_candidates.ipynb`</span></span><span> — candidate models + tuning
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`07_eval_interpretation.ipynb`</span></span><span> — metrics + error analysis + interpretation

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Documentation (CRISP-DM process instance)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`docs/02_decision_log.md`</span></span><span> — major decisions + tradeoffs
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`docs/03_assumptions_risks.md`</span></span><span> — assumptions, risks, mitigations

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="189">That’s
 a smart play. A public, non-PHI capstone repo is basically the 
“clean-room” version of your real work: it proves you can do end-to-end 
analytics without touching HIPAA/EHR landmines.</p>
<p data-start="191" data-end="291">Here’s how I’d set it up so it’s portfolio-ready later (but still works for course submissions now).</p>
<hr data-start="293" data-end="296">
<h2 data-start="298" data-end="348">1) Make it “public later” friendly from day one</h2>
<h3 data-start="350" data-end="382">Don’t commit data by default</h3>
<p data-start="383" data-end="536">Keep <code data-start="388" data-end="395">data/</code> ignored in Git (like we set up), and treat datasets as <strong data-start="451" data-end="461">inputs</strong> that a reviewer can download separately. This avoids licensing issues too.</p>
<p data-start="538" data-end="552">Add to README:</p>
<ul data-start="553" data-end="693">
<li data-start="553" data-end="602">
<p data-start="555" data-end="602">where the dataset came from (Coursera/provided)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="603" data-end="648">
<p data-start="605" data-end="648">whether it can be redistributed (often: no)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="649" data-end="693">
<p data-start="651" data-end="693">instructions to place files in <code data-start="682" data-end="693">data/raw/</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="695" data-end="727">Keep outputs that prove work</h3>
<p data-start="728" data-end="797">For a portfolio, you want <strong data-start="754" data-end="766">evidence</strong> without shipping the raw data:</p>
<ul data-start="798" data-end="947">
<li data-start="798" data-end="837">
<p data-start="800" data-end="837">exported figures (<code data-start="818" data-end="836">outputs/figures/</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="838" data-end="875">
<p data-start="840" data-end="875">exported tables (<code data-start="857" data-end="874">outputs/tables/</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="876" data-end="912">
<p data-start="878" data-end="912">report PDFs/markdown in <code data-start="902" data-end="912">reports/</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="913" data-end="947">

<h2 data-start="263" data-end="314">The game plan for this course (how we’ll run it)</h2>
<p data-start="315" data-end="354">For each module we’ll do the same loop:</p>
<ol data-start="356" data-end="745">
<li data-start="356" data-end="450">
<p data-start="359" data-end="450"><strong data-start="359" data-end="370">Capture</strong>: a short set of bullets from the lecture/readings (what matters, what’s fluff).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="451" data-end="552">
<p data-start="454" data-end="552"><strong data-start="454" data-end="467">Translate</strong>: “What does this mean for <em data-start="494" data-end="498">my</em> case study?” (choices, risks, assumptions, politics).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="553" data-end="651">
<p data-start="556" data-end="651"><strong data-start="556" data-end="565">Write</strong>: add/update 1–2 living files in the repo (so the report is basically writing itself).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="652" data-end="745">
<p data-start="655" data-end="745"><strong data-start="655" data-end="665">Decide</strong>: log decisions + alternatives you <em data-start="700" data-end="708">didn’t</em> pick (so you can defend them later).</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="747" data-end="1227">That lines up with what the course is asking for: <strong data-start="797" data-end="821">professional reports</strong> + <strong data-start="824" data-end="859">evidence of process in the repo</strong> (not perfect code, but clear work). The “Show Your Work” ZIP specifically wants all notebooks/code, a <code data-start="962" data-end="973">README.md</code>, a dependency file (<code data-start="994" data-end="1010">pyproject.toml</code> or <code data-start="1014" data-end="1032">requirements.txt</code>),
 the provided + derived data, and outputs that support your writeups. 
It’s pass/fail and they care about organization + evidence you actually 
did the work. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="relative inline-flex items-center"><button class="ms-1 flex h-[25px] text-[10px] leading-[13px] rounded-xl corner-superellipse/1.1 items-center justify-center gap-1 px-2 relative text-token-text-secondary! hover:text-token-text-primary! hover:bg-token-bg-secondary dark:bg-token-main-surface-secondary dark:hover:bg-token-bg-secondary bg-[#f4f4f4] "><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="h-[16px] w-[16px] object-contain text-token-text-primary! flex-none icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#554074" fill="currentColor"></use></svg><p class="not-prose mt-0! mb-0! flex-auto truncate">Show Your Work-1</p></button></span></span></p>

<p data-start="2188" data-end="2203">Why this works:</p>

</li>

<hr data-start="2683" data-end="2686">
<h2 data-start="2688" data-end="2763">The “living .md files” I want you to keep (these are your secret weapon)</h2>
<p data-start="2764" data-end="2859">These are the files that make the reports fast and keep you from losing decisions in your head:</p>

This document provides some opinionated guidance for setting up your data science workspace, including:

    Installing Python

    Setting up a development environment

    Managing Python packages and virtual environments

    Organizing your project repository

    Creating effective documentation

Installing Python

You have three main options for managing Python on your computer:

Option 1: The Official Python Interpreter This includes the Python interpreter and the standard library. You'll need to install necessary libraries for your data science project separately. Choose this if you want full control over your Python environment.

    Visit https://www.python.org/downloads/

     to download Python for your system.

Option 2: The Anaconda Python Distribution Anaconda includes Python plus a large collection of pre-installed data science libraries. This is a good option for getting started quickly and easily.

    Visit https://www.anaconda.com/download/success

     to download Anaconda for your system.

Option 3: Managing Python with UV UV is a modern Python package and project manager that can also handle Python installations.

    Visit https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/install-python/

     to learn more about managing Python with UV.

Dr. Burton's Recommendation: For beginners, I recommend either option 1 or option 2. While UV can manage Python installations, it's more advanced. UV will automatically find Python installed via options 1 or 2, so you can still use UV for package management (highly recommended) regardless of how you install Python.
Development Environment

When choosing your development environment, consider whether you'll primarily work with Jupyter Notebooks, Python scripts, or both. Most data science projects use a combination - notebooks for exploration and scripts for the pipeline.

Jupyter Lab A web-based IDE ideal for Jupyter Notebooks. It runs in your browser and provides file management capabilities. Included with Anaconda.

    Visit https://jupyter.org/install

     for installation information.

Visual Studio Code The most popular IDE among developers and data scientists. Excellent support for both Python scripts and Jupyter Notebooks.

    Visit https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/overview

     for data science features.

DataSpell JetBrains' IDE specifically designed for data science work, with specialized features for data exploration and visualization.

    Visit https://www.jetbrains.com/dataspell/

 for more information.

Free for students: https://www.jetbrains.com/academy/student-pack/

Other Options:

    Spyder

 - A Scientific IDE with a plugin to support Jupyter Notebooks. Not hugely popular, but specifically designed for data science.

Positron

 - This is a new Data Science IDE from the creators of R Studio. It’s a fork of VS Code, but with a lot of customization specifically for data science.

Marimo

     - Marimo is a new Python notebook environment that re-envisions the experience of authoring Python notebooks. It is an alternative to Jupyter and is still under development. It supports reactive execution, which means that if you execute a cell any other cells that refer to the variables will be automatically executed. 

Dr. Burton’s recommendation: 

If you haven’t tried it, I recommend using VS Code since that is the most popular IDE out in the world and has a lot of support for Jupyter-based data science work. It is good for editing Notebooks and Python scripts. The integrated terminal is useful for quickly managing your virtual environments and Python package installation (with UV).

You should also keep an eye on Marimo. Marimo resolves a lot of pain points people experience with Jupyter notebooks

, but the reactive execution model sometimes hurts my brain. I am personally using Marimo a lot more in my own work. I would only recommend Marimo if you feel very confident working with code and the command line. Also Marimo plays super nice with UV.
Managing Python Packages
Chaotic flowchart of conflicting Python versions and paths, captioned: “My Python setup is so bad it’s a Superfund site.”

Image Source: XKCD 1987 https://xkcd.com/1987/

 

There are a bunch of ways to manage Python Packages and most of them aren’t great. Python package management has always been a challenge, but it has gotten easier in the past year. 

Pip The standard Python package installer. Use pip to install packages from the Python Package Index

.

    Visit https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/getting-started/

     for documentation.

Conda The package manager for Anaconda distributions. Can install both Python and non-Python dependencies.

    Visit https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/stable/

     for documentation.

UV A modern, extremely fast package and project manager that simplifies Python development.

    Visit https://docs.astral.sh/uv/

     for documentation.

Dr. Burton's Recommendation:Just use UV. It eliminates most Python package management pain points and has quickly become invaluable for both academic and industry data scientists. The time invested in learning UV pays off quickly through improved productivity and fewer environment issues.
Virtual Environments

Virtual environments create isolated Python installations for each project, ensuring reproducibility and preventing package conflicts. While not required, they're strongly recommended for any serious work.

UV makes virtual environment management seamless:

    Visit https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/

     for UV project management.

Tracking Dependencies

Your project should include a file that lists all required packages:

    If using UV: pyproject.toml (automatically managed)

    If using pip: requirements.txt (create with pip freeze &gt; requirements.txt)

    If using conda: environment.yml (create with conda env export &gt; environment.yml)

Project Repository Organization

A well-organized repository helps both you and others understand your work. Here's our recommended structure:

project_name/
│
├── README.md       # Project overview and navigation guide
├── pyproject.toml  # Python packages you used (requirements.txt)
│
├── data/
│   ├── raw/        # Original data files (READ ONLY)
│   ├── processed/  # Cleaned datasets you created
│   └── CONTEXT.md  # The CONTEXT information for your project
│
├── notebooks/               # Your analysis notebooks
│   ├── 01-exploration.ipynb    # Data exploration and understanding
│   ├── 02-preparation.ipynb    # Data cleaning and preparation  
│   ├── 03-modeling.ipynb       # Model building and evaluation
│   └── [other notebooks]
│
├── results/
│   ├── figures/             # Charts and visualizations
│   ├── models/              # Saved models (if applicable)
│   └── [other outputs]
│
├── src/ # Python scripts (if any)
│
└── [other folders as needed]

This structure is a suggestion, not a requirement. Organize your work in whatever way makes sense for your project, but make sure your README.md explains how everything is organized.

Key Principles:

    Keep raw data separate and untouched

    Use clear, numbered naming for notebooks to show workflow

    Separate code, data, and results

    Include documentation at multiple levels

Documentation Best Practices
README.md

Every project needs a README.md file in the root directory. This is the first thing people see when viewing your repository. The readme should focus on documenting the contents of the project directory and discuss how to execute the code.

Essential Sections for your README.md:

# Project Title

## Overview

Brief description of your project. 

## Repository Structure

Explain what's in each folder and key files.

## Setup and Dependencies

How to recreate your environment (reference pyproject.toml or requirements.txt).

## How to Run

Basic instructions for reproducing your analysis.
Code Comments

Include comments that explain:

    What complex code sections do

    Why you made specific analytical choices

    Any assumptions or limitations

    Data transformations and their purpose

Example:

# Remove outliers beyond 3 standard deviations

# This prevents extreme values from skewing the model
df_clean = df[np.abs(stats.zscore(df['sales'])) &lt; 3]
External Resources
Video Tutorials 

Here are some YouTube tutorials that walk you through setting up a Python data science environment with VS Code and UV on Mac or Windows.

    Windows setup: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uxgkWssqkAU

MacOS setup: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0wj8F_oBYEE

Project Organization

Some opinionated guides to project organization and best practices around scientific computing and using Jupyter Notebooks.

    Cookiecutter Data Science: A logical, flexible, and reasonably standardized project structure for doing and sharing data science work.

        Visit https://cookiecutter-data-science.drivendata.org/

The Turing Way: A handbook to reproducible, ethical and collaborative data science.

    Visit https://book.the-turing-way.org/

Good Enough Practices in Scientific Computing: Best practices for organizing and documenting computational research. 

    Visit https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510

Ten simple rules for writing and sharing computational analyses in Jupyter Notebooks: Practical tips for authoring Jupyter Notebooks.

    Visit https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007007

UV Resources

Some blog posts about what is possible with the UV package manager.

    Data science workflow with UV: https://samedwardes.com/blog/2024-08-28-data-science-projects-with-uv/

UV unified packaging: https://astral.sh/blog/uv-unified-python-packaging

Remember: Tools and best practices evolve constantly. Stay curious and keep learning!

The data science landscape changes rapidly—new programming libraries emerge, cloud platforms add features, and analytical techniques evolve based on research breakthroughs. What's cutting-edge today may be standard practice next year. Successful data scientists cultivate a habit of continuous learning by following industry blogs, experimenting with new tools, and focusing on understanding core principles rather than memorizing specific syntax. The tools will change throughout your career, but strong analytical thinking and adaptability will always be valuable.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
Describe the goals, scope, and significance of the project. Explain what the project aims to achieve, any specific areas or processes it targets, and its overall importance.

### Best Practice:
- Clearly state the purpose and objectives.
- Mention the specific data or domains involved.
- Highlight the expected impact or outcome.

### Example:
"The project aims to analyze the potential operational and clinical improvements observed during specific overnight shifts in the Emergency Department that had overnight radiology coverage. The purpose is to identify improvements in efficiency and patient outcomes for future planning."

## Data:
Detail the datasets used, their sources, and any preprocessing done. Mention any limitations or noteworthy aspects of the data.

### Best Practice:
- Describe the source and nature of the data.
- Explain any preprocessing steps taken.
- Acknowledge any data limitations or exclusions.

### Example:
"The data used is from the Emergency Department and radiology department, covering operational and clinical metrics like time to decision and ED throughput. The data has been pre-processed to include relevant subsets, with no missing data in the final dataset."

## Analysis:
Explain the analytical methods and processes used in the project. Include any specific models, statistical tests, or tools applied.

### Best Practice:
- Outline the analysis methods clearly.
- Mention any specific software or libraries used.
- Describe the rationale behind choosing these methods.

### Example:
"The analysis involved exploratory data analysis (EDA) and logistic regression to estimate the odds ratios for each independent variable, using R packages like ggplot2, dplyr, and glm."

## Code:
Provide information on where to find the code, any dependencies required, and instructions for running it.

### Best Practice:
- List the programming languages and major libraries used.
- Include instructions for setting up the environment and running the code.
- If code cannot be shared publicly, explain how it can be accessed.

### Example:
"The R code for the project requires ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, readr, lubridate, and glm. It can be run by sourcing the main script, with file paths specified for input data and output files."

## Results:
Summarize the key findings and conclusions from the project. Highlight any significant results and their implications.

### Best Practice:
- Clearly state the main findings.
- Explain the significance of these results.
- Include references to detailed results or reports for further reading.

### Example:
"The presence of overnight radiology coverage was associated with shorter time to decision and overall ED length of stay, indicating a potential area for operational improvement."

## Contributions:
List the project contributors and their roles or contributions.

### Best Practice:
- Acknowledge all contributors and their roles.
- Include contact information if appropriate.

### Example:
"Main contributors: Dr. Daniel Chow (Associate Professor-in-Residence) and Luis Gonzalez (Business Intelligence Specialist III), focusing on data analysis and project coordination."

## Future Work:
Discuss any planned future research or unanswered questions that the project has raised.

### Best Practice:
- Mention specific areas for further investigation.
- Suggest how the project's findings could be expanded or applied.

### Example:
"Future work could explore other subsets of ED patients and additional factors impacting efficiency and outcomes, potentially integrating more comprehensive data sources."

## References:
Cite any references or external sources used in the project.

### Best Practice:
- Include full citations for any referenced works.
- If no external references were used, state this clearly.

### Example:
"No external references were used in the project."

## Contact Information:
Provide contact information for the project lead or main contact point.

### Best Practice:
- Include name, affiliation, and email address.

### Example:
"Luis Gonzalez: lgonzal1@hs.uci.edu"

<h3 data-start="305" data-end="339">Cookiecutter, in plain English</h3>
<p data-start="340" data-end="445"><strong data-start="340" data-end="369">Cookiecutter Data Science</strong> isn’t magic automation of your workflows; it’s <strong data-start="417" data-end="444">a scaffolding generator</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="446" data-end="548">
<li data-start="446" data-end="464">
<p data-start="448" data-end="464">you run it once,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="465" data-end="525">
<p data-start="467" data-end="525">it creates a standardized folder structure + starter docs,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="526" data-end="548">
<p data-start="528" data-end="548">then you fill it in.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="550" data-end="733">So: <em data-start="554" data-end="582">it’s a repo bootstrap tool</em>,
 not an orchestration/automation tool. You already built “the bones,” so
 cookiecutter is optional now — you’ve basically done the useful part 
already.</p>
<hr data-start="735" data-end="738">
<h2 data-start="740" data-end="802">What I recommend for <em data-start="764" data-end="770">this</em> course repo (minimal, high ROI)</h2>
<h3 data-start="804" data-end="861">1) Keep your README shorter than your “work template”</h3>
<p data-start="862" data-end="931">Your template is great internally, but for GitHub + graders you want:</p>
<ul data-start="932" data-end="1013">
<li data-start="932" data-end="946">
<p data-start="934" data-end="946">what this is</p>
</li>
<li data-start="947" data-end="962">
<p data-start="949" data-end="962">how to run it</p>
</li>
<li data-start="963" data-end="988">
<p data-start="965" data-end="988">where the artifacts are</p>
</li>
<li data-start="989" data-end="1013">
<p data-start="991" data-end="1013">what’s in/out of scope</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1015" data-end="1098"><strong data-start="1015" data-end="1056">Move the long-form stuff into <code data-start="1047" data-end="1054">docs/</code></strong>, and keep the README as the “front door.”</p>
<h3 data-start="1100" data-end="1137">2) Add a <code data-start="1113" data-end="1131">SCOPE_OF_WORK.md</code> (yes)</h3>

<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1409" data-end="2927"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">md</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-md"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Case Studies in Data Science — Capstone (CRISP-DM)</span></span><span>

This repository contains a single end-to-end case study for my University of Pittsburgh MDS capstone course.
Work is organized using the CRISP-DM lifecycle: Business Understanding → Data Understanding → Data Preparation → Modeling → Evaluation → Deployment.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Portfolio note:**</span></span><span> This project uses non-sensitive coursework data (no PHI/EHR/HIPAA data).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Start here</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Assignment 1 report (M5): </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`reports/M05_assignment1.md`</span></span><span> (exported PDF later)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Assignment 2 report (M9): </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`reports/M09_assignment2.md`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Assignment 3 final report + slides (M13): </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`reports/M13_assignment3.md`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Repository structure</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`data/raw/`</span></span><span> — provided dataset (unchanged; may not be committed to Git)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`data/processed/`</span></span><span> — modeling-ready datasets created during prep
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`notebooks/`</span></span><span> — analysis notebooks (numbered in workflow order)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`outputs/`</span></span><span> — figures/tables/models referenced in reports
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`docs/`</span></span><span> — scope, decisions, assumptions/risks, process diary
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`reports/`</span></span><span> — written reports aligned to course assignments

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## How to run</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Using uv (recommended)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`uv sync`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`uv run jupyter lab`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Using venv + pip (fallback)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`python3 -m venv .venv &amp;&amp; source .venv/bin/activate`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`pip install -r requirements.txt`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`jupyter lab`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Data note</span></span><span>
The dataset may be provided through coursework and may not be licensed for public redistribution.
Raw data is kept in </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`data/raw/`</span></span><span> and may be excluded from Git. If needed for course submission, it will be included in the submission ZIP.
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>

 fair — for this class, the “scope” is mostly dictated by the case

<p data-start="161" data-end="333">A <strong data-start="163" data-end="189"><code data-start="165" data-end="187">00_master_tracker.md</code></strong>,

<p data-start="4933" data-end="5011">For a real org, scope is negotiated and political, so SOW is protective armor.</p>
<p data-start="5013" data-end="5029">For this course:</p>
<ul data-start="5030" data-end="5210">
<li data-start="5030" data-end="5084">

</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="5212" data-end="5279">So: ✅ tracker yes, ✅ decision log yes, ✅ diary yes, ❌ SOW optional.</p>

"""CONTEXT+DATASET Overview

In this lesson you'll review several CONTEXT+DATASETS—these are your project options for the course. Each represents a  scenario where data science can make a meaningful impact to solve a problem or discover new knowledge. You'll choose one of these projects (or propose your own) and work with it through all three major assignments.
Understanding CONTEXT+DATASETS

The CONTEXT+DATASETS aren't just descriptions of data—they're complete project scenarios that situate you in a realistic professional role. When reading them, pay attention to:

    Who you'll be: Your professional role shapes how you approach the analysis

    Who you're serving: Different stakeholders have different needs and technical sophistication

    What problem you're solving: Some investigate "what's happening?" while others determine "what should we do?"

    What success looks like: Each project defines specific, measurable outcomes

The datasets themselves are real (or realistically complex), but more importantly, they exist within authentic organizational or societal contexts. This means your analysis must balance technical rigor with practical communication and real-world constraints.
Your Project Options
ICU Patient Care Analysis

Setting: Regional Medical Center's intensive care unit
Your role: Healthcare data analyst on the quality improvement team
The challenge: Help the hospital understand factors influencing patient outcomes to improve care quality and resource allocation
The data: Comprehensive electronic health records from 100 ICU patients
Why it matters: Your insights could directly impact how critically ill patients receive care

Best for students interested in healthcare analytics, clinical decision support, or public health applications of data science.
COVID Drivers: Pennsylvania Traffic Safety

Setting: Digital news organization investigating public safety
Your role: Data journalist uncovering truth behind public perceptions
The challenge: Determine if Pennsylvanians are actually driving worse post-COVID or if it's just perception
The data: 20 years of detailed crash data from PennDOT
Why it matters: Your investigation will inform public discourse about traffic safety with evidence rather than anecdote

Best for students interested in journalism, public policy, social science research, or telling data-driven stories.
Consumer Product Safety Analysis

Setting: Consumer Safety Research Institute (nonprofit)
Your role: Senior research analyst preparing the annual safety report
The challenge: Identify which products pose the greatest risk of severe injury, not just frequent injury
The data: National injury surveillance data from emergency departments
Why it matters: Your analysis guides consumer safety recommendations and policy priorities

Best for students interested in consumer advocacy, public health, risk analysis, or nonprofit research.
POGOH Bike Share Growth Analysis

Setting: Pittsburgh's nonprofit bike share system
Your role: Data analyst intern working with operations leadership
The challenge: Understand growth patterns to identify expansion opportunities
The data: Complete trip records since system relaunch in 2022
Why it matters: Your recommendations will shape how the system grows to serve more Pittsburgh residents

Best for students interested in urban planning, sustainable transportation, operations analysis, or local civic technology.
Bring Your Own Data (BYOD)

If you have access to data from your work, research, or personal interests, you may propose your own project. However, BYOD requires creating your own complete CONTEXT+DATASET specification. This means:

    You need more than data—you need a problem situated in a realistic social context (it doesn’t have to be real, you can provide fictionalized details)

    You must identify stakeholders who would care about your results

    You take responsibility for scoping a project that's neither too simple nor too ambitious

    You'll need proper permissions and must address ethical considerations

The BYOD option works best when you're genuinely excited about a problem and have domain knowledge that enriches your analysis.

IMPORTANT NOTE: BYOD projects require you to submit a CONTEXT+DATASET Proposal and receive approval from the instructional team. See the BYOD Reading Item for more details on proposing your own project.
Check out the Data

As you review each CONTEXT+DATASET specification, take time to read through the full project description carefully—understanding the context is essential for making an informed choice. However, don't stop there. Each project includes a link to download a ZIP file containing the actual datasets you'll be working with. We encourage you to download these files and do some preliminary exploration: check the file sizes, peek at the data structure, get a sense of the variables, and consider what kinds of analysis might be possible. This combination of reading the context and examining the actual data will give you the clearest picture of what each project entails. Remember, you'll be working with this data for an entire semester, so it's worth investing time upfront to ensure you're choosing a project that offers both interesting context and data you're excited to analyze."""
