Download a zip repository of the data here: 
Background

Regional Medical Center (RMC) is a 400-bed academic medical center serving a diverse metropolitan population. The hospital's 36-bed intensive care unit (ICU) treats critically ill patients requiring continuous monitoring and specialized care. Like many hospitals nationwide, RMC faces pressure to improve patient outcomes while managing costs and resource utilization effectively.

The ICU medical director has noted that patient outcomes vary significantly, and the hospital wants to better understand the factors that influence patient care and recovery. While the medical staff has extensive clinical experience, they recognize that systematic analysis of patient data could reveal patterns and insights that aren't apparent from individual case experience alone.
Motivation

ICU patients represent the most critically ill individuals in the hospital, with complex medical conditions requiring intensive resources and careful monitoring. Understanding what factors contribute to successful patient outcomes is crucial for improving care quality and resource allocation.

The hospital has access to comprehensive electronic health records that capture detailed information about patient demographics, medical history, treatments, monitoring data, and outcomes. However, this wealth of data has not been systematically analyzed to identify patterns that could inform clinical practice and operational decisions.

Healthcare organizations increasingly recognize the value of data-driven insights for improving patient care, optimizing resource utilization, and supporting clinical decision-making. RMC sees this as an opportunity to leverage their data assets to enhance care quality and operational efficiency.
Objective

Conduct a comprehensive analysis of ICU patient data to identify patterns and factors associated with patient outcomes and care delivery. The analysis should generate actionable insights that could inform clinical practice, quality improvement initiatives, or operational decisions.

The hospital is particularly interested in understanding patient characteristics, treatment patterns, and care processes that influence outcomes such as length of stay, resource utilization, and patient recovery. The goal is to develop evidence-based insights that could support clinical staff in providing optimal patient care.
Success Criteria

Success will be measured by the analysis team's ability to generate meaningful, evidence-based insights from the patient data that could realistically inform healthcare improvement efforts. The analysis should demonstrate sound methodology, appropriate interpretation of healthcare data, and practical relevance to hospital operations and patient care.
Deliverable

A comprehensive healthcare analytics report that includes clinical insights, data-driven recommendations, and clear documentation of methodology suitable for hospital leadership and clinical staff review.
Role

You are a healthcare data analyst working with the hospital's quality improvement team. Your analysis will contribute to the hospital's ongoing efforts to understand and improve patient care through evidence-based insights. You should approach the work with appropriate sensitivity to the healthcare context while maintaining analytical rigor.
Stakeholders

ICU Medical Director: Seeks evidence-based insights to improve clinical protocols and patient care quality; requires rigorous analysis with clear clinical relevance and practical recommendations that can be implemented in daily practice

Hospital Administration: Concerned with operational performance, resource utilization, and quality metrics; needs executive-level summaries showing potential impact on hospital efficiency, costs, and measurable outcomes
Datasets

Data Source Description

The MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo contains comprehensive electronic health records for 100 intensive care patients from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. The dataset spans multiple years of patient care and includes 26 interconnected tables organized into hospital-wide data (hosp module) and ICU-specific data (icu module). Data includes patient demographics, vital signs, laboratory results, medications, procedures, diagnoses, and hospital transfers. The dataset contains approximately 50,000+ individual records across all tables, representing real clinical complexity while maintaining manageable scope for analysis. This data provides sufficient detail to analyze patient characteristics, care patterns, outcomes, and resource utilization in intensive care settings.

Note, the demo dataset contains a open-access subset of the full dataset.

Provenance

Data was originally collected during routine clinical care at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center as part of standard hospital operations. Electronic health record systems automatically captured patient information during admission, treatment, and monitoring processes. The data was later extracted and processed by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology as part of the MIMIC project to create a research resource for healthcare analytics. The demo version was created by randomly selecting 100 patients from the full database while preserving all data relationships and temporal patterns. No additional sampling or filtering was applied beyond patient selection.

Data Source

The links below provide comprehensive information about the MIMIC-IV dataset.

Articles about MIMIC-IV on the PhysioNet website:

    MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo

 - Description of the open-access demo dataset that is a subset of the full dataset. This is the source of the provided data files.

MIMIC-IV Clinical Database

     - Description of the full MIMIC-IV Clinical Database. This dataset is not openly accessible and requires an extensive credentialing process for full access. This link provides broader context about the collection and contents of the MIMIC-IV Database.

Access: Publicly available under Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0

Data Dictionary

MIMIC-IV documentation:

    MIMIC Project Website

 - This website provides comprehensive information about the MIMIC project and databases as a whole.MIMIC-IV Core Concepts

 - Important concepts for understanding the structure and how to use the MIMIC-IV data.

MIMIC-IV Documentation
 - Provides detailed information on the MIMIC-IV data tables. The demo dataset contains the hosp
 and icu

 data tables.

MIMIC-IV Video Tutorials

     - The MIMIC project site links to several long (30mins to 1hr) videos that provide extensive information about the database.

Data Quality Notes

Several data characteristics result from the deidentification and extraction process:

    Patient identifiers are synthetic random numbers, not sequential

    All dates have been consistently shifted by patient-specific random offsets while preserving intervals

    Patients over 89 years appear with shifted ages for privacy protection

    Free-text clinical notes are excluded from the demo version

    Some tables may be empty or sparse due to the 100-patient subset

    Clinical measurements reflect real-world variability including missing values, measurement errors, and irregular timing typical of actual healthcare delivery

Ethical Considerations

The dataset has undergone rigorous deidentification following HIPAA Safe Harbor provisions, with all protected health information removed or transformed. However, students should:

    Treat the data as confidential research material despite deidentification

    Avoid attempting to re-identify patients or make connections to individuals

    Consider potential biases in healthcare data including socioeconomic, racial, and geographic disparities

    Recognize that clinical decisions and outcomes may reflect broader healthcare access issues

    Frame analysis conclusions appropriately, acknowledging that patterns may reflect systemic healthcare inequities rather than purely clinical factors

    Ensure any recommendations consider potential impacts on different patient populations""" this is the dataset readme """===============================
MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo
===============================

The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV&nbsp;database is comprised
of&nbsp;deidentified electronic health records for patients admitted to the Beth Israel
Deaconess Medical Center. Access to MIMIC-IV is limited to credentialed users.
Here, we have provided an openly-available demo of MIMIC-IV containing&nbsp;a subset
of&nbsp;100 patients. The dataset includes similar content to MIMIC-IV, but excludes
free-text clinical notes. The demo may be useful for running workshops&nbsp;and for
assessing whether the MIMIC-IV is appropriate for a study before making an access
request.

For details on the data, see the MIMIC-IV project on PhysioNet:
https://doi.org/10.13026/07hj-2a80

The contents of this project also contain an additional file:
demo_subject_id.csv

This is a CSV file containing the subject_id used to filter MIMIC-IV. Only
these subject_id are available in the demo."""  CONTETEXT """# CONTEXT+DATASET: ICU Patient Care Analysis

## **Background**

Regional Medical Center (RMC) is a 400-bed academic medical center serving a diverse metropolitan population. The hospital's 36-bed intensive care unit (ICU) treats critically ill patients requiring continuous monitoring and specialized care. Like many hospitals nationwide, RMC faces pressure to improve patient outcomes while managing costs and resource utilization effectively.

The ICU medical director has noted that patient outcomes vary significantly, and the hospital wants to better understand the factors that influence patient care and recovery. While the medical staff has extensive clinical experience, they recognize that systematic analysis of patient data could reveal patterns and insights that aren't apparent from individual case experience alone.

## **Motivation**

ICU patients represent the most critically ill individuals in the hospital, with complex medical conditions requiring intensive resources and careful monitoring. Understanding what factors contribute to successful patient outcomes is crucial for improving care quality and resource allocation. 

The hospital has access to comprehensive electronic health records that capture detailed information about patient demographics, medical history, treatments, monitoring data, and outcomes. However, this wealth of data has not been systematically analyzed to identify patterns that could inform clinical practice and operational decisions.

Healthcare organizations increasingly recognize the value of data-driven insights for improving patient care, optimizing resource utilization, and supporting clinical decision-making. RMC sees this as an opportunity to leverage their data assets to enhance care quality and operational efficiency.

## **Objective**

Conduct a comprehensive analysis of ICU patient data to identify patterns and factors associated with patient outcomes and care delivery. The analysis should generate actionable insights that could inform clinical practice, quality improvement initiatives, or operational decisions.

The hospital is particularly interested in understanding patient characteristics, treatment patterns, and care processes that influence outcomes such as length of stay, resource utilization, and patient recovery. The goal is to develop evidence-based insights that could support clinical staff in providing optimal patient care.

## **Success Criteria**

Success will be measured by the analysis team's ability to generate meaningful, evidence-based insights from the patient data that could realistically inform healthcare improvement efforts. The analysis should demonstrate sound methodology, appropriate interpretation of healthcare data, and practical relevance to hospital operations and patient care.

## **Deliverable**

A comprehensive healthcare analytics report that includes clinical insights, data-driven recommendations, and clear documentation of methodology suitable for hospital leadership and clinical staff review.

## **Role**

You are a healthcare data analyst working with the hospital's quality improvement team. Your analysis will contribute to the hospital's ongoing efforts to understand and improve patient care through evidence-based insights. You should approach the work with appropriate sensitivity to the healthcare context while maintaining analytical rigor.

## **Stakeholders**

**ICU Medical Director**: Seeks evidence-based insights to improve clinical protocols and patient care quality; requires rigorous analysis with clear clinical relevance and practical recommendations that can be implemented in daily practice

**Hospital Administration**: Concerned with operational performance, resource utilization, and quality metrics; needs executive-level summaries showing potential impact on hospital efficiency, costs, and measurable outcomes


## Datasets

### Data Source Description
The MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo contains comprehensive electronic health records for 100 intensive care patients from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. The dataset spans multiple years of patient care and includes 26 interconnected tables organized into hospital-wide data (hosp module) and ICU-specific data (icu module). Data includes patient demographics, vital signs, laboratory results, medications, procedures, diagnoses, and hospital transfers. The dataset contains approximately 50,000+ individual records across all tables, representing real clinical complexity while maintaining manageable scope for analysis. This data provides sufficient detail to analyze patient characteristics, care patterns, outcomes, and resource utilization in intensive care settings.

Note, the *demo* dataset contains a open-access subset of the full dataset.

### Provenance
Data was originally collected during routine clinical care at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center as part of standard hospital operations. Electronic health record systems automatically captured patient information during admission, treatment, and monitoring processes. The data was later extracted and processed by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology as part of the MIMIC project to create a research resource for healthcare analytics. The demo version was created by randomly selecting 100 patients from the full database while preserving all data relationships and temporal patterns. No additional sampling or filtering was applied beyond patient selection.

**Data Source**

The links below provide comprehensive information about the MIMIC-IV dataset.

Articles about MIMIC-IV on the PhysioNet website:
- [MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/2.2/) - Description of the open-access demo dataset that is a subset of the full dataset. This is the source of the provided data files.
- [MIMIC-IV Clinical Database](https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/3.1/) - Description of the full MIMIC-IV Clinical Database. This dataset is not openly accessible and requires an extensive credentialing process for full access. This link provides broader context about the collection and contents of the MIMIC-IV Database.

Access: Publicly available under [Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/view-license/2.2/)

**Data Dictionary**

MIMIC-IV documentation:
- [MIMIC Project Website](https://mimic.mit.edu/) - This website provides comprehensive information about the MIMIC project and databases as a whole.
- [MIMIC-IV Core Concepts](https://mimic.mit.edu/docs/iv/about/concepts/) - Important concepts for understanding the structure and how to use the MIMIC-IV data.
- [MIMIC-IV Documentation](https://mimic.mit.edu/docs/iv/) - Provides detailed information on the MIMIC-IV data tables. The demo dataset contains the [<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">hosp</code>](https://mimic.mit.edu/docs/iv/modules/hosp) and [<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">icu</code>](https://mimic.mit.edu/docs/iv/modules/icu) data tables.
- [MIMIC-IV Video Tutorials](https://mimic.mit.edu/docs/iv/tutorials/video/) - The MIMIC project site links to several long (30mins to 1hr) videos that provide extensive information about the database.

**Data Quality Notes**

Several data characteristics result from the deidentification and extraction process:

- Patient identifiers are synthetic random numbers, not sequential
- All dates have been consistently shifted by patient-specific random offsets while preserving intervals
- Patients over 89 years appear with shifted ages for privacy protection
- Free-text clinical notes are excluded from the demo version
- Some tables may be empty or sparse due to the 100-patient subset
- Clinical measurements reflect real-world variability including missing values, measurement errors, and irregular timing typical of actual healthcare delivery

**Ethical Considerations**

The dataset has undergone rigorous deidentification following HIPAA Safe Harbor provisions, with all protected health information removed or transformed. However, students should:

- Treat the data as confidential research material despite deidentification
- Avoid attempting to re-identify patients or make connections to individuals
- Consider potential biases in healthcare data including socioeconomic, racial, and geographic disparities
- Recognize that clinical decisions and outcomes may reflect broader healthcare access issues
- Frame analysis conclusions appropriately, acknowledging that patterns may reflect systemic healthcare inequities rather than purely clinical factors
- Ensure any recommendations consider potential impacts on different patient populations""" based on the video overview this data is from 2000.  they wanted to replicated doctors.. lol For <strong data-start="33" data-end="40">.gz</strong>, you don’t “unzip” with <code data-start="65" data-end="72">unzip</code>; you <strong data-start="78" data-end="88">gunzip</strong> them (or <code data-start="98" data-end="107">gzip -d</code>). And you can do it recursively without touching the folder structure.</p>
<p data-start="180" data-end="224">Below are a couple safe, copy/paste options.</p>
<hr data-start="226" data-end="229">
<h2 data-start="231" data-end="279">0) First: see how many <code data-start="257" data-end="262">.gz</code> files you’ve got</h2>
<p data-start="280" data-end="328">From the repo root (or wherever the data lives):</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="330" data-end="377"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find . -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">wc</span></span><span> -l
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="379" data-end="427">If your raw data is under <code data-start="405" data-end="416">data/raw/</code>, scope it:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="429" data-end="483"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">wc</span></span><span> -l
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<hr data-start="485" data-end="488">
<h2 data-start="490" data-end="567">1) Recommended: decompress all <code data-start="524" data-end="529">.gz</code> files in-place (and remove the <code data-start="561" data-end="566">.gz</code>)</h2>
<p data-start="568" data-end="678">This keeps directories exactly the same and deletes the compressed files after expanding (what you asked for):</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="680" data-end="755"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> -print0 | xargs -0 gunzip -v
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<ul data-start="757" data-end="850">
<li data-start="757" data-end="780">
<p data-start="759" data-end="780"><code data-start="759" data-end="763">-v</code> = shows progress</p>
</li>
<li data-start="781" data-end="850">
<p data-start="783" data-end="850">This will turn <code data-start="798" data-end="810">foo.csv.gz</code> into <code data-start="816" data-end="825">foo.csv</code> and delete <code data-start="837" data-end="849">foo.csv.gz</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="852" data-end="917">If you’re not using <code data-start="876" data-end="887">data/raw/</code>, replace it with your folder:</h3>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="918" data-end="986"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find . -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> -print0 | xargs -0 gunzip -v
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<hr data-start="988" data-end="991">
<h2 data-start="993" data-end="1049">2) “Safety mode”: keep the <code data-start="1023" data-end="1028">.gz</code> too (uses more disk)</h2>
<p data-start="1050" data-end="1095">If you decide you want to preserve originals:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1097" data-end="1173"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> -print0 | xargs -0 gunzip -vk
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<ul data-start="1175" data-end="1236">
<li data-start="1175" data-end="1236">
<p data-start="1177" data-end="1236"><code data-start="1177" data-end="1181">-k</code> keeps the <code data-start="1192" data-end="1197">.gz</code> and also writes the decompressed file.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="1238" data-end="1241">
<h2 data-start="1243" data-end="1297">3) Faster option if you have <code data-start="1275" data-end="1281">pigz</code> (parallel gzip)</h2>
<p data-start="1298" data-end="1329">Pop!_OS often has it available:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1331" data-end="1391"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">sudo</span></span><span> apt-get update
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">sudo</span></span><span> apt-get install -y pigz
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1393" data-end="1398">Then:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1400" data-end="1476"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> -print0 | xargs -0 pigz -d -v
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1478" data-end="1527">Same effect as gunzip, just faster on multi-core.</p>
<hr data-start="1529" data-end="1532">
<h2 data-start="1534" data-end="1558">4) Verify you’re done</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1559" data-end="1613"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f -name </span><span><span class="hljs-string">"*.gz"</span></span><span> | </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">wc</span></span><span> -l
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1615" data-end="1633">Should return <code data-start="1629" data-end="1632">0</code>.</p>
<hr data-start="1635" data-end="1638">
<h2 data-start="1640" data-end="1674">Common gotchas (quick heads-up)</h2>
<ul data-start="1675" data-end="1881">
<li data-start="1675" data-end="1734">
<p data-start="1677" data-end="1734">If you see <code data-start="1688" data-end="1694">.zip</code> files: those use <code data-start="1712" data-end="1719">unzip</code>, not <code data-start="1725" data-end="1733">gunzip</code>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1735" data-end="1881">
<p data-start="1737" data-end="1881">If you see <code data-start="1748" data-end="1757">.tar.gz</code>: that’s a tarball (use <code data-start="1781" data-end="1803">tar -xzf file.tar.gz</code>). MIMIC demo is usually individual <code data-start="1839" data-end="1848">.csv.gz</code>, so you probably won’t hit this.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="1883" data-end="1886">
<p data-start="1888" data-end="1915">If you paste the output of:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1916" data-end="1974"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>find data/raw -maxdepth 3 -</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">type</span></span><span> f | </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">head</span></span><span> -n 30
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1975" data-end="2077">…I can tell you if your folder path is exactly what we should target (without changing any structure).</p>

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="182">Yep — MIMIC looks “opaque” at first because it’s <strong data-start="49" data-end="66">26 flat files</strong>, but it’s actually a pretty clean relational model once you internalize the <strong data-start="143" data-end="157">3 core IDs</strong> and the <strong data-start="166" data-end="181">two modules</strong>.</p>
<h2 data-start="184" data-end="228">The 3 IDs that make everything make sense</h2>
<p data-start="230" data-end="271">Think of MIMIC-IV as three nested levels:</p>
<ol data-start="273" data-end="427">
<li data-start="273" data-end="304">
<p data-start="276" data-end="304"><strong data-start="276" data-end="302"><code data-start="278" data-end="290">subject_id</code> = patient</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="305" data-end="356">
<p data-start="308" data-end="356"><strong data-start="308" data-end="354"><code data-start="310" data-end="319">hadm_id</code> = hospital admission (encounter)</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="357" data-end="427">
<p data-start="360" data-end="427"><strong data-start="360" data-end="384"><code data-start="362" data-end="371">stay_id</code> = ICU stay</strong> (a slice of time inside a hospitalization)</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="429" data-end="548">MIMIC-IV is explicitly modular, and those identifiers are the glue across tables. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<p data-start="550" data-end="826"><strong data-start="550" data-end="608">Important correction on your “data from 2000” thought:</strong><br data-start="608" data-end="611">
That “2000” you saw is a <em data-start="636" data-end="658">PhysioNet/PhysioBank</em> citation, not the clinical data’s timeframe. The <strong data-start="708" data-end="716">demo</strong> cohort is selected from <code data-start="741" data-end="760">anchor_year_group</code> <strong data-start="761" data-end="787">2011–2013 or 2014–2016</strong>. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 57px;"><a href="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 57px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PhysioNet</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<hr data-start="828" data-end="831">
<h2 data-start="833" data-end="881">The two modules you care about (for the demo)</h2>
<h3 data-start="883" data-end="951">1) <code data-start="890" data-end="896">hosp</code> module (hospital-wide / ADT / orders / labs / billing)</h3>
<p data-start="952" data-end="974">This is where you get:</p>
<ul data-start="975" data-end="1099">
<li data-start="975" data-end="1010">
<p data-start="977" data-end="1010">demographics + admissions context</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1011" data-end="1031">
<p data-start="1013" data-end="1031">labs, microbiology</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1032" data-end="1062">
<p data-start="1034" data-end="1062">meds (orders + admin tables)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1063" data-end="1099">
<p data-start="1065" data-end="1099">billing-coded diagnoses/procedures</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1101" data-end="1237">The <code data-start="1105" data-end="1111">hosp</code> module includes ADT records plus labs, meds, and administrative/billing-derived tables. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<p data-start="1239" data-end="1302">A key line from the documentation/paper that matters for joins:</p>
<ul data-start="1303" data-end="1625">
<li data-start="1303" data-end="1367">
<p data-start="1305" data-end="1367"><strong data-start="1305" data-end="1346"><code data-start="1307" data-end="1319">subject_id</code> is present in all tables</strong> (link to <code data-start="1356" data-end="1366">patients</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1368" data-end="1492">
<p data-start="1370" data-end="1492"><strong data-start="1370" data-end="1419"><code data-start="1372" data-end="1381">hadm_id</code> represents a single hospitalization</strong> (some rows may not have <code data-start="1444" data-end="1453">hadm_id</code> if not tied to an inpatient encounter)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1493" data-end="1625">
<p data-start="1495" data-end="1625"><strong data-start="1495" data-end="1560">tables with <code data-start="1509" data-end="1517">itemid</code> must be linked to <code data-start="1536" data-end="1541">d_*</code> dimension tables</strong> for human-readable meaning <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1627" data-end="1685">2) <code data-start="1634" data-end="1639">icu</code> module (bedside charting during the ICU stay)</h3>
<p data-start="1686" data-end="1737">This is the “high-frequency / messy-reality” stuff:</p>
<ul data-start="1738" data-end="1955">
<li data-start="1738" data-end="1785">
<p data-start="1740" data-end="1785">vitals &amp; bedside observations (<code data-start="1771" data-end="1784">chartevents</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1786" data-end="1813">
<p data-start="1788" data-end="1813">infusions (<code data-start="1799" data-end="1812">inputevents</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1814" data-end="1840">
<p data-start="1816" data-end="1840">outputs (<code data-start="1825" data-end="1839">outputevents</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1841" data-end="1883">
<p data-start="1843" data-end="1883">procedures/therapies (<code data-start="1865" data-end="1882">procedureevents</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1884" data-end="1922">
<p data-start="1886" data-end="1922">time-typed events (<code data-start="1905" data-end="1921">datetimeevents</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1923" data-end="1955">
<p data-start="1925" data-end="1955">plus the key table: <code data-start="1945" data-end="1955">icustays</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1957" data-end="2007">The ICU module is documented as a <strong data-start="1991" data-end="2006">star schema</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="2008" data-end="2142">
<li data-start="2008" data-end="2061">
<p data-start="2010" data-end="2061">event tables reference <strong data-start="2033" data-end="2061"><code data-start="2035" data-end="2045">icustays</code> via <code data-start="2050" data-end="2059">stay_id</code></strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2062" data-end="2142">
<p data-start="2064" data-end="2142">and reference <strong data-start="2078" data-end="2104"><code data-start="2080" data-end="2089">d_items</code> via <code data-start="2094" data-end="2102">itemid</code></strong> <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 58px;"><a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 58px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Nature</span><span class="-me-1 flex h-full items-center rounded-full px-1 text-[#8F8F8F]">+1</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2144" data-end="2147">
<h2 data-start="2149" data-end="2190">The join map (the “one over” you want)</h2>
<p data-start="2192" data-end="2231">Here’s the mental ERD in plain English:</p>
<h3 data-start="2233" data-end="2252">Backbone tables</h3>
<ul data-start="2253" data-end="2776">
<li data-start="2253" data-end="2325">
<p data-start="2255" data-end="2325"><code data-start="2255" data-end="2265">patients</code> (<strong data-start="2267" data-end="2281">subject_id</strong>)<br data-start="2282" data-end="2285">
↳ 1 patient → many hospital admissions</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2327" data-end="2433">
<p data-start="2329" data-end="2433"><code data-start="2329" data-end="2341">admissions</code> (<strong data-start="2343" data-end="2354">hadm_id</strong>, subject_id)<br data-start="2367" data-end="2370">
↳ 1 admission → many transfers, labs, orders, diagnoses, etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2435" data-end="2547">
<p data-start="2437" data-end="2547"><code data-start="2437" data-end="2448">transfers</code> (subject_id, hadm_id, times, locations)<br data-start="2488" data-end="2491">
↳ this movement log is what ICU stays are derived from</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2549" data-end="2776">
<p data-start="2551" data-end="2776"><code data-start="2551" data-end="2561">icustays</code> (<strong data-start="2563" data-end="2574">stay_id</strong>, subject_id, hadm_id, <code data-start="2597" data-end="2605">intime</code>, <code data-start="2607" data-end="2616">outtime</code>)<br data-start="2617" data-end="2620">
↳ ICU stays are <strong data-start="2638" data-end="2666">derived from <code data-start="2653" data-end="2664">transfers</code></strong> and consecutive ICU-location transfers can be merged into one <code data-start="2729" data-end="2738">stay_id</code> <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 58px;"><a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 58px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Nature</span><span class="-me-1 flex h-full items-center rounded-full px-1 text-[#8F8F8F]">+1</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="2778" data-end="2816">“Facts” you usually join in (hosp)</h3>
<ul data-start="2817" data-end="3460">
<li data-start="2817" data-end="2905">
<p data-start="2819" data-end="2905"><code data-start="2819" data-end="2830">labevents</code> + <code data-start="2833" data-end="2845">d_labitems</code> (lab concepts/labels) <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2906" data-end="3001">
<p data-start="2908" data-end="3001"><code data-start="2908" data-end="2928">microbiologyevents</code> (cultures; more complex hierarchy) <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3002" data-end="3146">
<p data-start="3004" data-end="3146"><code data-start="3004" data-end="3019">prescriptions</code> + <code data-start="3022" data-end="3032">pharmacy</code> (order + compound detail), and <code data-start="3064" data-end="3070">emar</code> + <code data-start="3073" data-end="3086">emar_detail</code> (admin record detail) <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3147" data-end="3210">
<p data-start="3149" data-end="3210"><code data-start="3149" data-end="3164">diagnoses_icd</code> + <code data-start="3167" data-end="3184">d_icd_diagnoses</code> (billing-coded diagnoses)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3211" data-end="3250">
<p data-start="3213" data-end="3250"><code data-start="3213" data-end="3229">procedures_icd</code> + <code data-start="3232" data-end="3250">d_icd_procedures</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3251" data-end="3362">
<p data-start="3253" data-end="3362"><code data-start="3253" data-end="3263">drgcodes</code>, <code data-start="3265" data-end="3278">hcpcsevents</code> (+ <code data-start="3282" data-end="3297">d_hcpcsevents</code>) for billing/service codes <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3363" data-end="3460">
<p data-start="3365" data-end="3460"><code data-start="3365" data-end="3370">poe</code> + <code data-start="3373" data-end="3385">poe_detail</code> for orders (imaging/consults/etc.) <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 37px;"><a href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9810617/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 37px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PMC</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3462" data-end="3499">“Facts” you usually join in (icu)</h3>
<p data-start="3500" data-end="3527">All of these are basically:</p>
<ul data-start="3528" data-end="3648">
<li data-start="3528" data-end="3648">
<p data-start="3530" data-end="3648"><strong data-start="3530" data-end="3568">(stay_id + itemid + time + value…)</strong><br>
…and you decode <strong data-start="3585" data-end="3607"><code data-start="3587" data-end="3605">itemid → d_items</code></strong>. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 58px;"><a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01899-x" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 58px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">Nature</span><span class="-me-1 flex h-full items-center rounded-full px-1 text-[#8F8F8F]">+1</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3650" data-end="3653">
<h2 data-start="3655" data-end="3703">Practical advice for <em data-start="3679" data-end="3685">your</em> analysis workflow</h2>
<h3 data-start="3705" data-end="3754">Pick your “grain” early (this prevents chaos)</h3>
<p data-start="3755" data-end="3807">For this course, you’ll usually choose one of these:</p>
<ul data-start="3809" data-end="4118">
<li data-start="3809" data-end="3955">
<p data-start="3811" data-end="3955"><strong data-start="3811" data-end="3838">ICU-stay-level modeling</strong> (one row per <code data-start="3852" data-end="3861">stay_id</code>)<br data-start="3862" data-end="3865">
Best for: predicting ICU LOS, ventilation, mortality proxy outcomes, resource intensity.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3957" data-end="4118">
<p data-start="3959" data-end="4118"><strong data-start="3959" data-end="3996">Hospital-admission-level modeling</strong> (one row per <code data-start="4010" data-end="4019">hadm_id</code>)<br data-start="4020" data-end="4023">
Best for: total hospital LOS, discharge disposition (if available), admission-level outcomes.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4120" data-end="4183">Then you aggregate everything “below” that grain into features.</p>
<h3 data-start="4185" data-end="4251">The 2 views that make everything easier (even before modeling)</h3>
<p data-start="4252" data-end="4300">When you load into Postgres, create these early:</p>
<ol data-start="4302" data-end="4482">
<li data-start="4302" data-end="4365">
<p data-start="4305" data-end="4365"><strong data-start="4305" data-end="4322"><code data-start="4307" data-end="4320">vw_backbone</code></strong> = <code data-start="4325" data-end="4335">patients</code> + <code data-start="4338" data-end="4350">admissions</code> + <code data-start="4353" data-end="4363">icustays</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="4366" data-end="4482">
<p data-start="4369" data-end="4482"><strong data-start="4369" data-end="4397"><code data-start="4371" data-end="4395">vw_icu_events_first24h</code></strong> = join ICU event tables filtered to <code data-start="4434" data-end="4458">[intime, intime + 24h]</code>, decoded with <code data-start="4473" data-end="4482">d_items</code></p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="4484" data-end="4551">That gets you from “26 files” → “I can actually reason about this.”</p>
<hr data-start="4553" data-end="4556">
<h2 data-start="4558" data-end="4596">Re: “I should put this in Postgres”</h2>
<p data-start="4597" data-end="4939">100% reasonable. MIMIC-IV is designed as a relational database and even the demo is described that way. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 72px;"><a href="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 72px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PhysioNet</span><span class="-me-1 flex h-full items-center rounded-full px-1 text-[#8F8F8F]">+1</span></span></span></a></span></span><br data-start="4740" data-end="4743">
Also note: PhysioNet explicitly calls out it’s available in CSV and also on <strong data-start="4819" data-end="4831">BigQuery</strong>, and there’s official code in the MIMIC code repo to support usage. <span class="" data-state="closed"><span class="ms-1 inline-flex max-w-full items-center select-none relative top-[-0.094rem] animate-[show_150ms_ease-in]" data-testid="webpage-citation-pill" style="width: 57px;"><a href="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/" class="flex h-4.5 overflow-hidden rounded-xl px-2 text-[9px] font-medium transition-colors duration-150 ease-in-out text-token-text-secondary! bg-[#F4F4F4]! dark:bg-[#303030]!" style="max-width: 57px;"><span class="relative start-0 bottom-0 flex h-full w-full items-center"><span class="flex h-4 w-full items-center justify-between overflow-hidden" style="opacity: 1; transform: none;"><span class="max-w-[15ch] grow truncate overflow-hidden text-center">PhysioNet</span></span></span></a></span></span></p>
<p data-start="4941" data-end="5041">If you tell me <strong data-start="4956" data-end="4992">what you want your “grain” to be</strong> (ICU stay vs hospital admission), I’ll give you:</p>
<ul data-start="5042" data-end="5245">
<li data-start="5042" data-end="5106">
<p data-start="5044" data-end="5106">a recommended load order (dimension tables first, then facts),</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5107" data-end="5142">
<p data-start="5109" data-end="5142">the 5–8 indexes that matter most,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5143" data-end="5245">
<p data-start="5145" data-end="5245">and a starter set of Postgres views so you can query like a sane person instead of drowning in CSVs.</p>
</li>
</ul>

[.text-message+&amp;]:mt-1" data-message-model-slug="gpt-5-2-thinking"><div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="266">ICU-stay-level is a very sane default for MIMIC, <em data-start="49" data-end="61">especially</em>
 for a course project where you want clean joins and a defensible “one 
row per case” dataset. But it’s not the only workable grain. Here are 
your real options, with pros/cons and the “gotchas” that matter.</p>
<hr data-start="268" data-end="271">
<h2 data-start="273" data-end="324">Option A: ICU-stay-level (one row per <code data-start="314" data-end="323">stay_id</code>)</h2>
<p data-start="325" data-end="447"><strong data-start="325" data-end="339">Best when:</strong> your stakeholder questions are ICU/QI focused (LOS, resource intensity, early deterioration, ICU workflow).</p>
<h3 data-start="449" data-end="457">Pros</h3>
<ul data-start="458" data-end="856">
<li data-start="458" data-end="541">
<p data-start="460" data-end="541"><strong data-start="460" data-end="491">Schema is optimized for it.</strong> Most ICU event tables naturally key on <code data-start="531" data-end="540">stay_id</code>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="542" data-end="632">
<p data-start="544" data-end="632"><strong data-start="544" data-end="571">Clear unit of analysis.</strong> “This ICU stay” is a coherent episode with <code data-start="615" data-end="631">intime/outtime</code>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="633" data-end="757">
<p data-start="635" data-end="757"><strong data-start="635" data-end="678">Feature engineering is straightforward.</strong> Aggregate first 6/24 hours, min/max/mean slopes, counts of interventions, etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="758" data-end="856">
<p data-start="760" data-end="856"><strong data-start="760" data-end="794">Stakeholder relevance is high.</strong> ICU director cares about ICU-specific processes and outcomes.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="858" data-end="874">Cons / risks</h3>
<ul data-start="875" data-end="1358">
<li data-start="875" data-end="1023">
<p data-start="877" data-end="1023"><strong data-start="877" data-end="903">Small N + correlation.</strong> A patient can have multiple ICU stays → not independent rows. You must split train/test by <code data-start="995" data-end="1007">subject_id</code> or you’ll leak.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1024" data-end="1160">
<p data-start="1026" data-end="1160"><strong data-start="1026" data-end="1055">Outcome definition traps.</strong> “ICU LOS” is easy; “recovery” is squishier; mortality can be in-ICU vs in-hospital. Pick clean outcomes.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1161" data-end="1358">
<p data-start="1163" data-end="1358"><strong data-start="1163" data-end="1203">Time leakage is the #1 failure mode.</strong> If you use features from the entire stay to predict LOS, you’re basically using the answer. You’ll want an <strong data-start="1311" data-end="1327">early-window</strong> feature set (e.g., first 24h).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1360" data-end="1484"><strong data-start="1360" data-end="1391">Portfolio-friendly framing:</strong> “Early ICU risk stratification / resource planning support” rather than “replicate doctors.”</p>
<hr data-start="1486" data-end="1489">
<h2 data-start="1491" data-end="1552">Option B: Hospital-admission-level (one row per <code data-start="1542" data-end="1551">hadm_id</code>)</h2>
<p data-start="1553" data-end="1650"><strong data-start="1553" data-end="1567">Best when:</strong> hospital admin cares about total utilization, throughput, and end-to-end outcomes.</p>
<h3 data-start="1652" data-end="1660">Pros</h3>
<ul data-start="1661" data-end="1959">
<li data-start="1661" data-end="1773">
<p data-start="1663" data-end="1773"><strong data-start="1663" data-end="1693">Broader operational story.</strong> Total hospital LOS, discharge disposition (if available), overall resource use.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1774" data-end="1867">
<p data-start="1776" data-end="1867"><strong data-start="1776" data-end="1819">Easier linkage to diagnoses/procedures.</strong> ICD/DRG-type tables key naturally at admission.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1868" data-end="1959">
<p data-start="1870" data-end="1959"><strong data-start="1870" data-end="1908">Often closer to “cost” narratives.</strong> Admin stakeholders like admission-level summaries.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1961" data-end="1977">Cons / risks</h3>
<ul data-start="1978" data-end="2235">
<li data-start="1978" data-end="2096">
<p data-start="1980" data-end="2096"><strong data-start="1980" data-end="2018">ICU is only part of the admission.</strong> ICU exposure may be partial and you can conflate ICU effects with floor care.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2097" data-end="2235">
<p data-start="2099" data-end="2235"><strong data-start="2099" data-end="2141">Feature engineering is more sprawling.</strong> You’ll touch more <code data-start="2160" data-end="2166">hosp</code> tables and need clearer inclusion criteria (“ICU admissions only?”).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2237" data-end="2240">
<h2 data-start="2242" data-end="2295">Option C: Patient-level (one row per <code data-start="2282" data-end="2294">subject_id</code>)</h2>
<p data-start="2296" data-end="2390"><strong data-start="2296" data-end="2310">Best when:</strong> the question is “who tends to do poorly?” rather than “which stay does poorly?”</p>
<h3 data-start="2392" data-end="2400">Pros</h3>
<ul data-start="2401" data-end="2541">
<li data-start="2401" data-end="2456">
<p data-start="2403" data-end="2456"><strong data-start="2403" data-end="2428">Simple, clean splits.</strong> No repeat-measures leakage.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2457" data-end="2541">
<p data-start="2459" data-end="2541"><strong data-start="2459" data-end="2489">Good for descriptive work.</strong> Comorbidities, demographics, baseline risk factors.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="2543" data-end="2559">Cons / risks</h3>
<ul data-start="2560" data-end="2763">
<li data-start="2560" data-end="2683">
<p data-start="2562" data-end="2683"><strong data-start="2562" data-end="2603">Too coarse for ICU process questions.</strong> ICU care is episodic; patient-level can blur critical timing and interventions.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2684" data-end="2763">
<p data-start="2686" data-end="2763"><strong data-start="2686" data-end="2709">You may lose power.</strong> With 100 patients, you’re reducing rows even further.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2765" data-end="2768">
<h2 data-start="2770" data-end="2842">Option D: Time-slice / early-window dataset (one row per stay-window)</h2>
<p data-start="2843" data-end="2902">Example: <code data-start="2852" data-end="2861">stay_id</code> + “first 6h”, “first 24h”, “day 2”, etc.</p>
<h3 data-start="2904" data-end="2912">Pros</h3>
<ul data-start="2913" data-end="3069">
<li data-start="2913" data-end="2984">
<p data-start="2915" data-end="2984"><strong data-start="2915" data-end="2942">Solves leakage cleanly.</strong> Features precede outcome by construction.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2985" data-end="3069">
<p data-start="2987" data-end="3069"><strong data-start="2987" data-end="3022">Lets you ask smarter questions.</strong> “By hour 6, can we predict prolonged ICU LOS?”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3071" data-end="3087">Cons / risks</h3>
<ul data-start="3088" data-end="3244">
<li data-start="3088" data-end="3157">
<p data-start="3090" data-end="3157"><strong data-start="3090" data-end="3111">More engineering.</strong> Need careful timestamp alignment and windows.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3158" data-end="3244">
<p data-start="3160" data-end="3244"><strong data-start="3160" data-end="3188">More choices to justify.</strong> Window length, missingness handling, aggregation logic.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3246" data-end="3312"><strong data-start="3246" data-end="3277">This is my favorite variant</strong> of ICU-stay-level for credibility.</p>
<hr data-start="3314" data-end="3317">
<h2 data-start="3319" data-end="3388">Option E: Event-level / longitudinal modeling (many rows per stay)</h2>
<p data-start="3389" data-end="3443">Think sequences, time series, survival, hazard models.</p>
<h3 data-start="3445" data-end="3453">Pros</h3>
<ul data-start="3454" data-end="3607">
<li data-start="3454" data-end="3553">
<p data-start="3456" data-end="3553"><strong data-start="3456" data-end="3489">Most faithful to ICU reality.</strong> Captures trajectories, irregular sampling, escalation patterns.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3554" data-end="3607">
<p data-start="3556" data-end="3607"><strong data-start="3556" data-end="3607">Great for “canary in the coal mine” narratives.</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3609" data-end="3625">Cons / risks</h3>
<ul data-start="3626" data-end="3820">
<li data-start="3626" data-end="3730">
<p data-start="3628" data-end="3730"><strong data-start="3628" data-end="3658">Heavy lift for the course.</strong> You can absolutely do it, but it’s easy to overbuild and under-explain.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3731" data-end="3820">
<p data-start="3733" data-end="3820"><strong data-start="3733" data-end="3777">Harder to grade + harder to communicate.</strong> Stakeholder deliverables get complex fast.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3822" data-end="3825">
<h1 data-start="3827" data-end="3891">My recommendation for <em data-start="3851" data-end="3857">your</em> course success + portfolio signal</h1>
<h3 data-start="3892" data-end="3976">Go with <strong data-start="3904" data-end="3922">ICU-stay-level</strong>, but implement it as <strong data-start="3944" data-end="3975">early-window ICU-stay-level</strong>.</h3>
<p data-start="3978" data-end="3993">That gives you:</p>
<ul data-start="3994" data-end="4140">
<li data-start="3994" data-end="4019">
<p data-start="3996" data-end="4019">clean relational joins,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4020" data-end="4047">
<p data-start="4022" data-end="4047">realistic ICU/QI framing,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4048" data-end="4084">
<p data-start="4050" data-end="4084">strong guardrails against leakage,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4085" data-end="4140">
<p data-start="4087" data-end="4140">and a story an ICU director/admin would actually buy.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="4142" data-end="4188">Concrete template (high signal, low drama)</h3>
<ul data-start="4189" data-end="4565">
<li data-start="4189" data-end="4223">
<p data-start="4191" data-end="4223"><strong data-start="4191" data-end="4201">Grain:</strong> one row per <code data-start="4214" data-end="4223">stay_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="4224" data-end="4314">
<p data-start="4226" data-end="4314"><strong data-start="4226" data-end="4239">Features:</strong> aggregated from <strong data-start="4256" data-end="4269">first 24h</strong> (or first 6h if you want more “operational”)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4315" data-end="4449">
<p data-start="4317" data-end="4348"><strong data-start="4317" data-end="4348">Primary outcome (pick one):</strong></p>
<ul data-start="4351" data-end="4449">
<li data-start="4351" data-end="4396">
<p data-start="4353" data-end="4396">Prolonged ICU LOS (binary: &gt; X days) <strong data-start="4390" data-end="4396">or</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="4399" data-end="4449">
<p data-start="4401" data-end="4449">ICU LOS (continuous, but consider log-transform)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="4450" data-end="4565">
<p data-start="4452" data-end="4485"><strong data-start="4452" data-end="4485">Secondary outcome (optional):</strong></p>
<ul data-start="4488" data-end="4565">
<li data-start="4488" data-end="4565">
<p data-start="4490" data-end="4565">resource intensity proxy (e.g., # labs, ventilation flag, vasopressor flag)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="4567" data-end="4606">Two “rules” that keep it defensible</h3>
<ol data-start="4607" data-end="4765">
<li data-start="4607" data-end="4687">
<p data-start="4610" data-end="4687"><strong data-start="4610" data-end="4635">Split by <code data-start="4621" data-end="4633">subject_id</code></strong>, not by rows (prevents same patient in train+test).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4688" data-end="4765">
<p data-start="4691" data-end="4765"><strong data-start="4691" data-end="4724">Feature time precedes outcome</strong> (your window ends before LOS “unfolds”).</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="4767" data-end="4770">
<h2 data-start="4772" data-end="4838">Your decision options (if you want influence with stakeholders)</h2>
<p data-start="4839" data-end="4902">Here’s how I’d present it in an Assignment 1 “options” section:</p>
<ol data-start="4904" data-end="5269">
<li data-start="4904" data-end="4999">
<p data-start="4907" data-end="4999"><strong data-start="4907" data-end="4938">ICU-stay early-window model</strong> (recommended): best alignment with ICU QI + avoids leakage</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5000" data-end="5085">
<p data-start="5003" data-end="5085"><strong data-start="5003" data-end="5028">Admission-level model</strong>: best for admin utilization story, broader but noisier</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5086" data-end="5177">
<p data-start="5089" data-end="5177"><strong data-start="5089" data-end="5127">Descriptive patient-level analysis</strong>: safest but least actionable for ICU operations</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5178" data-end="5269">
<p data-start="5181" data-end="5269"><strong data-start="5181" data-end="5203">Longitudinal model</strong>: highest realism, highest complexity risk for the course timeline</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="5271" data-end="5274">
<p data-start="5276" data-end="5520">If you tell me which <strong data-start="5297" data-end="5316">primary outcome</strong>
 you want (LOS vs mortality vs resource-intensity), I’ll give you a 
crisp “problem statement + success criteria + baseline” that fits both 
stakeholders and won’t get you dinged for leakage or vague goals.</p>
</div></div></div></div><div class="z-0 flex min-h-[46px] justify-start"><div class="touch:-me-2 touch:-ms-3.5 -ms-2.5 -me-1 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-y-4 p-1 select-none
