[.text-message+&amp;]:mt-1" data-message-model-slug="gpt-5-2-thinking"><div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="283">Leaning into <strong data-start="13" data-end="19">QI</strong>
 is the right move here because the course’s success criteria is 
intentionally squishy (“meaningful, evidence-based insights… sound 
methodology… practical relevance”). Your job is to <strong data-start="202" data-end="250">turn that into concrete, QI-flavored outputs</strong> without over-claiming causality.</p>
<p data-start="285" data-end="345">Here’s how to do that <em data-start="307" data-end="312">and</em> where Kaplan–Meier fits cleanly.</p>
<hr data-start="347" data-end="350">
<h2 data-start="352" data-end="417">Turn that vague success criteria into a measurable “QI rubric”</h2>
<p data-start="418" data-end="500">When they say “success will be measured by…”, you can operationalize it like this:</p>
<h3 data-start="502" data-end="544">1) Meaningful, evidence-based insights</h3>
<p data-start="545" data-end="560">You’ll deliver:</p>
<ul data-start="561" data-end="830">
<li data-start="561" data-end="677">
<p data-start="563" data-end="677"><strong data-start="563" data-end="605">A short list of high-leverage patterns</strong> (e.g., “patients with X profile have higher risk of prolonged ICU LOS”)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="678" data-end="728">
<p data-start="680" data-end="728"><strong data-start="680" data-end="698">Stratification</strong> (low/medium/high risk groups)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="729" data-end="830">
<p data-start="731" data-end="830"><strong data-start="731" data-end="758">Quantified effect sizes</strong> (differences in median time-to-event, hazard ratios, odds ratios, etc.)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="832" data-end="856">2) Sound methodology</h3>
<p data-start="857" data-end="869">You’ll show:</p>
<ul data-start="870" data-end="1164">
<li data-start="870" data-end="921">
<p data-start="872" data-end="921"><strong data-start="872" data-end="899">Clear cohort definition</strong> (inclusion/exclusion)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="922" data-end="959">
<p data-start="924" data-end="959"><strong data-start="924" data-end="947">Outcome definitions</strong> with timing</p>
</li>
<li data-start="960" data-end="1025">
<p data-start="962" data-end="1025"><strong data-start="962" data-end="981">Leakage control</strong> (first-24h features only if predicting LOS)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1026" data-end="1088">
<p data-start="1028" data-end="1088"><strong data-start="1028" data-end="1042">Validation</strong> (even basic, but honest: subject-level split)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1089" data-end="1164">
<p data-start="1091" data-end="1164"><strong data-start="1091" data-end="1113">Sensitivity checks</strong> (different LOS thresholds / alternative censoring)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1166" data-end="1217">3) Practical relevance to ICU operations / care</h3>
<p data-start="1218" data-end="1245">You’ll explicitly separate:</p>
<ul data-start="1246" data-end="1488">
<li data-start="1246" data-end="1332">
<p data-start="1248" data-end="1332"><strong data-start="1248" data-end="1274">Non-modifiable factors</strong> (age, baseline comorbidity proxies) → for risk adjustment</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1333" data-end="1488">
<p data-start="1335" data-end="1488"><strong data-start="1335" data-end="1382">Potentially modifiable care/process signals</strong> (early labs intensity, ventilation status, vasopressor use, delayed antibiotic? etc.) → for QI hypotheses</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1490" data-end="1547">That’s QI gold: “We can’t change X, but we can change Y.”</p>
<hr data-start="1549" data-end="1552">
<h2 data-start="1554" data-end="1619">Where Kaplan–Meier (KM) actually fits (and where it bites you)</h2>
<p data-start="1620" data-end="1697">KM is perfect for any “time-to-event” story, which is inherently QI-friendly:</p>
<h3 data-start="1699" data-end="1737">Clean KM use cases in this dataset</h3>
<p data-start="1738" data-end="1778">Pick one primary time-to-event endpoint:</p>
<ol data-start="1780" data-end="2396">
<li data-start="1780" data-end="2020">
<p data-start="1783" data-end="1846"><strong data-start="1783" data-end="1808">Time to ICU discharge</strong> (a.k.a. ICU LOS as a time-to-event)</p>
<ul data-start="1850" data-end="2020">
<li data-start="1850" data-end="1884">
<p data-start="1852" data-end="1884">time origin: <code data-start="1865" data-end="1882">icustays.intime</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1888" data-end="1934">
<p data-start="1890" data-end="1934">event: ICU discharge at <code data-start="1914" data-end="1932">icustays.outtime</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1938" data-end="2020">
<p data-start="1940" data-end="2020">Then compare curves by group (e.g., vent vs no vent, high vs low severity proxy)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2022" data-end="2195">
<p data-start="2025" data-end="2083"><strong data-start="2025" data-end="2054">Time to in-hospital death</strong> (if you define it cleanly)</p>
<ul data-start="2087" data-end="2195">
<li data-start="2087" data-end="2113">
<p data-start="2089" data-end="2113">time origin: ICU admit</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2117" data-end="2157">
<p data-start="2119" data-end="2157">event: death time (from hosp tables)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2161" data-end="2195">
<p data-start="2163" data-end="2195">censor: hospital discharge alive</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2197" data-end="2396">
<p data-start="2200" data-end="2275"><strong data-start="2200" data-end="2243">Composite “time to ICU discharge alive”</strong> (often the most QI-intuitive)</p>
<ul data-start="2279" data-end="2396">
<li data-start="2279" data-end="2315">
<p data-start="2281" data-end="2315">event: ICU discharge <em data-start="2302" data-end="2313">and alive</em></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2319" data-end="2396">
<p data-start="2321" data-end="2396">treat death as “did not achieve event” (but see competing risks note below)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 data-start="2398" data-end="2429">The gotcha: competing risks</h3>
<p data-start="2430" data-end="2558">If your “event” is ICU discharge, <strong data-start="2464" data-end="2493">death is a competing risk</strong>, not a clean censor. If you censor deaths, you can bias results.</p>
<p data-start="2560" data-end="2620"><strong data-start="2560" data-end="2620">Two defensible ways to handle this for a course project:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2621" data-end="2995">
<li data-start="2621" data-end="2799">
<p data-start="2623" data-end="2799"><strong data-start="2623" data-end="2654">Option A (simple + honest):</strong>
 KM for “time to ICU discharge” and explicitly state: “Deaths treated as
 censored; interpret as time-to-discharge among those not dying early.”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2800" data-end="2995">
<p data-start="2802" data-end="2871"><strong data-start="2802" data-end="2835">Option B (better QI framing):</strong> Use <strong data-start="2840" data-end="2870">two curves / two endpoints</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="2874" data-end="2995">
<li data-start="2874" data-end="2905">
<p data-start="2876" data-end="2905">time to ICU discharge alive</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2908" data-end="2995">
<p data-start="2910" data-end="2995">time to death<br data-start="2923" data-end="2926">
(You’re basically showing two operationally relevant trajectories.)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2997" data-end="3181">If you want to go one level more 
“grown-up,” you can mention you considered competing risks and 
optionally add a cumulative incidence plot later, but you don’t <em data-start="3157" data-end="3163">have</em> to over-engineer.</p>
<hr data-start="3183" data-end="3186">
<h2 data-start="3188" data-end="3241">Your best “QI-aligned” project shape (recommended)</h2>
<p data-start="3242" data-end="3278">Since you’re leaning ICU-stay-level:</p>
<h3 data-start="3280" data-end="3289">Grain</h3>
<ul data-start="3290" data-end="3317">
<li data-start="3290" data-end="3317">
<p data-start="3292" data-end="3317"><strong data-start="3292" data-end="3317">One row per <code data-start="3306" data-end="3315">stay_id</code></strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3319" data-end="3337">Feature window</h3>
<ul data-start="3338" data-end="3408">
<li data-start="3338" data-end="3408">
<p data-start="3340" data-end="3408"><strong data-start="3340" data-end="3363">First 24 hours only</strong> (prevents leakage and keeps it QI-realistic)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3410" data-end="3462">Primary outcome (QI-friendly and easy to defend)</h3>
<p data-start="3463" data-end="3472">Pick one:</p>
<ul data-start="3473" data-end="3666">
<li data-start="3473" data-end="3585">
<p data-start="3475" data-end="3585"><strong data-start="3475" data-end="3496">Prolonged ICU LOS</strong> (binary: &gt; median or &gt; 75th percentile)<br data-start="3536" data-end="3539">
<em data-start="3541" data-end="3585">Great for modeling + leadership messaging.</em></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3586" data-end="3666">
<p data-start="3588" data-end="3666"><strong data-start="3588" data-end="3613">Time to ICU discharge</strong> (survival endpoint)<br data-start="3633" data-end="3636">
<em data-start="3638" data-end="3666">Great for KM + Cox models.</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3668" data-end="3697">You can absolutely do both:</p>
<ul data-start="3698" data-end="3827">
<li data-start="3698" data-end="3744">
<p data-start="3700" data-end="3744">KM/Cox for interpretability + QI narrative</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3745" data-end="3827">
<p data-start="3747" data-end="3827">simple predictive model for “operational triage” (who is likely to be prolonged)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3829" data-end="3832">
<h2 data-start="3834" data-end="3896">Concrete “deliverables” that will read well to stakeholders</h2>
<p data-start="3897" data-end="3924">Here’s the set I’d aim for:</p>
<ol data-start="3926" data-end="4456">
<li data-start="3926" data-end="3970">
<p data-start="3929" data-end="3970"><strong data-start="3929" data-end="3961">Cohort + outcome definitions</strong> (1 page)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3971" data-end="4018">
<p data-start="3974" data-end="4018"><strong data-start="3974" data-end="3997">Descriptive profile</strong> of the 100 ICU stays</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4019" data-end="4092">
<p data-start="4022" data-end="4036"><strong data-start="4022" data-end="4035">KM curves</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="4040" data-end="4092">
<li data-start="4040" data-end="4092">
<p data-start="4042" data-end="4092">discharge curves by 2–3 clinically sensible groups</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="4093" data-end="4213">
<p data-start="4096" data-end="4145"><strong data-start="4096" data-end="4130">Cox proportional hazards model</strong> (lightweight):</p>
<ul data-start="4149" data-end="4213">
<li data-start="4149" data-end="4213">
<p data-start="4151" data-end="4213">hazard ratios for “faster vs slower discharge” (interpretable)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="4214" data-end="4310">
<p data-start="4217" data-end="4260"><strong data-start="4217" data-end="4259">A “modifiable vs non-modifiable” table</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="4264" data-end="4310">
<li data-start="4264" data-end="4310">
<p data-start="4266" data-end="4310">what’s signal vs what’s just risk adjustment</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="4311" data-end="4456">
<p data-start="4314" data-end="4393"><strong data-start="4314" data-end="4336">QI recommendations</strong> framed as <em data-start="4347" data-end="4372">hypotheses + next steps</em>, not policy decrees:</p>
<ul data-start="4397" data-end="4456">
<li data-start="4397" data-end="4456">
<p data-start="4399" data-end="4456">“Consider auditing X process in patients with Y profile…”</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="4458" data-end="4569">That absolutely satisfies the course’s “practical relevance” criterion without pretending you proved causality.</p>
<hr data-start="4571" data-end="4574">
<h2 data-start="4576" data-end="4613">Quick decision (so we don’t drift)</h2>
<p data-start="4614" data-end="4668">Which “time-to-event” do you want to be your headline?</p>
<ul data-start="4670" data-end="4844">
<li data-start="4670" data-end="4718">
<p data-start="4672" data-end="4718"><strong data-start="4672" data-end="4678">A)</strong> Time to ICU discharge (KM/Cox on LOS)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4719" data-end="4764">
<p data-start="4721" data-end="4764"><strong data-start="4721" data-end="4727">B)</strong> Time to death (mortality survival)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4765" data-end="4844">
<p data-start="4767" data-end="4844"><strong data-start="4767" data-end="4773">C)</strong> ICU discharge alive + death as separate trajectories (strongest story)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4846" data-end="5039">If you pick one, I’ll help you write the <strong data-start="4887" data-end="4920">Assignment 1 success criteria</strong> in a way that sounds like QI, and I’ll give you the exact cohort/outcome definition bullets to paste into your report.</p>
<p data-start="5041" data-end="5135">(And yes: KM curves are a great way to “lean QI” without over-indexing on black-box modeling.)</p>

[.text-message+&amp;]:mt-1" data-message-model-slug="gpt-5-2-thinking"><div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="217">Yep — in healthcare-land what you’re calling “recidivism” is usually <strong data-start="69" data-end="97">readmission / bounceback</strong>. And <strong data-start="103" data-end="149">Kaplan–Meier is absolutely a QI-native way</strong> to frame it: <em data-start="163" data-end="200">time to readmission after discharge</em>, with censoring.</p>
<p data-start="219" data-end="389">But with the <strong data-start="232" data-end="264">MIMIC-IV demo (100 patients)</strong>, the first question is whether you even have enough repeat admissions to make a readmission curve not look like a flat line.</p>
<h3 data-start="391" data-end="463">The 4 files I’d look at first (to decide if readmission is feasible)</h3>
<p data-start="464" data-end="551">These tell you whether “several visits per patient” is real in <em data-start="527" data-end="533">your</em> extracted subset:</p>
<ol data-start="553" data-end="1144">
<li data-start="553" data-end="685">
<p data-start="556" data-end="577"><code data-start="556" data-end="575">hosp/patients.csv</code></p>
<ul data-start="581" data-end="685">
<li data-start="581" data-end="685">
<p data-start="583" data-end="685">defines <strong data-start="591" data-end="603">patients</strong> (<code data-start="605" data-end="617">subject_id</code>) and demographics; often includes death info (useful for censoring)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="687" data-end="845">
<p data-start="690" data-end="713"><code data-start="690" data-end="711">hosp/admissions.csv</code></p>
<ul data-start="717" data-end="845">
<li data-start="717" data-end="793">
<p data-start="719" data-end="793">defines <strong data-start="727" data-end="747">hospitalizations</strong> (<code data-start="749" data-end="758">hadm_id</code>) with admit/discharge timestamps</p>
</li>
<li data-start="797" data-end="845">
<p data-start="799" data-end="845">this is the backbone for <strong data-start="824" data-end="839">readmission</strong> logic</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="847" data-end="1004">
<p data-start="850" data-end="870"><code data-start="850" data-end="868">icu/icustays.csv</code></p>
<ul data-start="874" data-end="1004">
<li data-start="874" data-end="944">
<p data-start="876" data-end="944">defines <strong data-start="884" data-end="897">ICU stays</strong> (<code data-start="899" data-end="908">stay_id</code>) tied to <code data-start="918" data-end="927">hadm_id</code> + <code data-start="930" data-end="942">subject_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="948" data-end="1004">
<p data-start="950" data-end="1004">tells you how much ICU exposure you have per admission</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1006" data-end="1144">
<p data-start="1009" data-end="1031"><code data-start="1009" data-end="1029">hosp/transfers.csv</code></p>
<ul data-start="1035" data-end="1144">
<li data-start="1035" data-end="1144">
<p data-start="1037" data-end="1144">movement log; useful for “ICU bounceback within same hospitalization” and other trajectory-style QI metrics</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="1146" data-end="1221">Those four give you the entire “how many episodes do I even have?” picture.</p>
<hr data-start="1223" data-end="1226">
<h2 data-start="1228" data-end="1273">Quick feasibility checks (run these first)</h2>
<h3 data-start="1274" data-end="1306">If you’ve loaded to Postgres</h3>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1307" data-end="2143"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">sql</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-sql"><span><span><span class="hljs-comment">-- 1) How many patients / admissions / ICU stays?</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span>
  (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> hosp.patients) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> patients,
  (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> hosp.admissions) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> admissions,
  (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> icu.icustays) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> icu_stays;

</span><span><span class="hljs-comment">-- 2) Admissions per patient (do we even have repeats?)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span>
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">filter</span></span><span> (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">where</span></span><span> n_adm </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">=</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">1</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> pts_1_adm,
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">filter</span></span><span> (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">where</span></span><span> n_adm </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">&gt;=</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">2</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> pts_2plus_adm,
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">max</span></span><span>(n_adm) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> max_adm_per_patient
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> (
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span> subject_id, </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> n_adm
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> hosp.admissions
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">group</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">by</span></span><span> subject_id
) x;

</span><span><span class="hljs-comment">-- 3) ICU stays per admission (bounceback potential)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span>
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">filter</span></span><span> (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">where</span></span><span> n_stay </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">=</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">1</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> hadm_1_icu_stay,
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">filter</span></span><span> (</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">where</span></span><span> n_stay </span><span><span class="hljs-operator">&gt;=</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-number">2</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> hadm_2plus_icu_stay,
  </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">max</span></span><span>(n_stay) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> max_icu_stays_per_hadm
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> (
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">select</span></span><span> hadm_id, </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">count</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-operator">*</span></span><span>) </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">as</span></span><span> n_stay
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> icu.icustays
  </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">group</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">by</span></span><span> hadm_id
) x;
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<h3 data-start="2145" data-end="2206">If you haven’t loaded to Postgres yet (pandas quick look)</h3>
<p data-start="2207" data-end="2278">Same idea: count patients, admissions per patient, stays per admission.</p>
<hr data-start="2280" data-end="2283">
<h2 data-start="2285" data-end="2349">If readmission is sparse, you still get great KM/QI endpoints</h2>
<p data-start="2350" data-end="2502">If the demo subset doesn’t have 
many patients with &gt;1 hospitalization, you can still do survival 
analysis with endpoints that are <em data-start="2480" data-end="2492">guaranteed</em> to exist:</p>
<h3 data-start="2504" data-end="2568">Option 1: “Time to ICU discharge” (ICU LOS as time-to-event)</h3>
<ul data-start="2569" data-end="2690">
<li data-start="2569" data-end="2621">
<p data-start="2571" data-end="2621">Pros: always defined via <code data-start="2596" data-end="2621">icustays.intime/outtime</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2622" data-end="2690">
<p data-start="2624" data-end="2690">QI story: “what factors are associated with prolonged ICU course?”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="2692" data-end="2749">Option 2: “Time to hospital discharge” (hospital LOS)</h3>
<ul data-start="2750" data-end="2844">
<li data-start="2750" data-end="2809">
<p data-start="2752" data-end="2809">Pros: always defined via <code data-start="2777" data-end="2809">admissions.admittime/dischtime</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="2810" data-end="2844">
<p data-start="2812" data-end="2844">QI story: end-to-end utilization</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="2846" data-end="2908">Option 3: “ICU bounceback” within the same hospitalization</h3>
<ul data-start="2909" data-end="3083">
<li data-start="2909" data-end="2985">
<p data-start="2911" data-end="2985">Define index ICU stay, then event = <strong data-start="2947" data-end="2966">second ICU stay</strong> (same <code data-start="2973" data-end="2982">hadm_id</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2986" data-end="3017">
<p data-start="2988" data-end="3017">Uses <code data-start="2993" data-end="3003">icustays</code> + <code data-start="3006" data-end="3017">transfers</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3018" data-end="3083">
<p data-start="3020" data-end="3083">QI story: “stepdown failure / premature transfer / instability”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3085" data-end="3160">This is often more <em data-start="3104" data-end="3130">operationally actionable</em> than true readmission anyway.</p>
<hr data-start="3162" data-end="3165">
<h2 data-start="3167" data-end="3206">My recommendation for your next move</h2>
<p data-start="3207" data-end="3344">Do <strong data-start="3210" data-end="3232">those three counts</strong> (patients/admissions/stays; 2+ admissions; 2+ ICU stays per admission). That will tell us in 2 minutes whether:</p>
<ul data-start="3346" data-end="3476">
<li data-start="3346" data-end="3376">
<p data-start="3348" data-end="3376">KM readmission is viable, or</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3377" data-end="3476">
<p data-start="3379" data-end="3476">we pivot to <strong data-start="3391" data-end="3408">ICU discharge</strong> or <strong data-start="3412" data-end="3426">bounceback</strong>, which will still look like a “real QI” analysis.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3478" data-end="3824">If you paste the results of the 
three SQL blocks (or just the numbers), I’ll tell you which survival 
endpoint gives you the strongest signal <strong data-start="3619" data-end="3650">with this demo-sized cohort</strong>,
 and I’ll propose 2–3 clinically/operationally meaningful stratification
 variables to plot (e.g., ventilation flag, early lactate group, 
vasopressor use, comorbidity proxy).</p>

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="215">Yep — these 4 files are enough to do a legit first-pass “recidivism / bounceback” feasibility check, and the news is: <strong data-start="118" data-end="172">this demo set actually <em data-start="143" data-end="149">does</em> have repeat episodes</strong> (more than I expected for “100 patients”).</p>
<h2 data-start="217" data-end="266">What’s in your 4 backbone tables (at a glance)</h2>
<p data-start="267" data-end="290">From what you uploaded:</p>
<ul data-start="292" data-end="673">
<li data-start="292" data-end="366">
<p data-start="294" data-end="366"><strong data-start="294" data-end="310">patients.csv</strong>: <strong data-start="312" data-end="328">100 patients</strong> (<code data-start="330" data-end="342">subject_id</code>) + demographics + <code data-start="361" data-end="366">dod</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="367" data-end="469">
<p data-start="369" data-end="469"><strong data-start="369" data-end="387">admissions.csv</strong>: <strong data-start="389" data-end="416">275 hospital admissions</strong> (<code data-start="418" data-end="427">hadm_id</code>) with admit/discharge times + death flags</p>
</li>
<li data-start="470" data-end="562">
<p data-start="472" data-end="562"><strong data-start="472" data-end="488">icustays.csv</strong>: <strong data-start="490" data-end="507">140 ICU stays</strong> (<code data-start="509" data-end="518">stay_id</code>) with <code data-start="525" data-end="541">intime/outtime</code> + careunit + ICU LOS</p>
</li>
<li data-start="563" data-end="673">
<p data-start="565" data-end="673"><strong data-start="565" data-end="582">transfers.csv</strong>: <strong data-start="584" data-end="609">1,190 transfer events</strong> (location/level-of-care movements; good for “bounceback” logic)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="675" data-end="776">So you’re not stuck with a single admission per patient — there’s actual longitudinal structure here.</p>
<hr data-start="778" data-end="781">
<h2 data-start="783" data-end="840">Is “recidivism / readmission” viable for Kaplan–Meier?</h2>
<p data-start="841" data-end="865"><strong data-start="841" data-end="849">Yes.</strong> In this subset:</p>
<ul data-start="867" data-end="1025">
<li data-start="867" data-end="922">
<p data-start="869" data-end="922"><strong data-start="869" data-end="888">48/100 patients</strong> have <strong data-start="894" data-end="920">≥2 hospital admissions</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="923" data-end="1025">
<p data-start="925" data-end="1025">median admissions per patient is <strong data-start="958" data-end="963">1</strong>, but the tail is real (max <strong data-start="991" data-end="997">20</strong> admissions for one patient)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1027" data-end="1122">When I compute “time from discharge → next hospital admission” (where a next admission exists):</p>
<ul data-start="1124" data-end="1297">
<li data-start="1124" data-end="1165">
<p data-start="1126" data-end="1165"><strong data-start="1126" data-end="1165">175 discharge→readmission intervals</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1166" data-end="1211">
<p data-start="1168" data-end="1211">median time to next admission ≈ <strong data-start="1200" data-end="1211">89 days</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1212" data-end="1297">
<p data-start="1214" data-end="1234">readmissions within:</p>
<ul data-start="1237" data-end="1297">
<li data-start="1237" data-end="1253">
<p data-start="1239" data-end="1253"><strong data-start="1239" data-end="1250">7 days:</strong> 22</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1256" data-end="1277">
<p data-start="1258" data-end="1277"><strong data-start="1258" data-end="1270">30 days:</strong> <strong data-start="1271" data-end="1277">53</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1280" data-end="1297">
<p data-start="1282" data-end="1297"><strong data-start="1282" data-end="1294">90 days:</strong> 88</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1299" data-end="1438">That is plenty to support a KM curve for “time to next admission” (overall), and you can also do a <strong data-start="1398" data-end="1420">30-day readmission</strong> focused analysis.</p>
<p data-start="1440" data-end="1479"><strong data-start="1440" data-end="1479">Key QI framing that will land well:</strong></p>
<blockquote data-start="1480" data-end="1645">
<p data-start="1482" data-end="1645">“Time to next <em data-start="1496" data-end="1506">recorded</em>
 hospital admission after discharge” (descriptive / 
hypothesis-generating), with a clear statement about censoring and 
small-N uncertainty.</p>
</blockquote>
<hr data-start="1647" data-end="1650">
<h2 data-start="1652" data-end="1715">ICU-flavored “recidivism” options (also feasible, smaller N)</h2>
<p data-start="1716" data-end="1774">If you mean <em data-start="1728" data-end="1745">ICU readmission</em> (which is a very QI metric):</p>
<ul data-start="1776" data-end="1970">
<li data-start="1776" data-end="1819">
<p data-start="1778" data-end="1819"><strong data-start="1778" data-end="1797">26/100 patients</strong> have <strong data-start="1803" data-end="1819">≥2 ICU stays</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1820" data-end="1881">
<p data-start="1822" data-end="1881">That yields <strong data-start="1834" data-end="1881">40 ICU-discharge → next ICU-admit intervals</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1882" data-end="1970">
<p data-start="1884" data-end="1907">ICU readmission within:</p>
<ul data-start="1910" data-end="1970">
<li data-start="1910" data-end="1927">
<p data-start="1912" data-end="1927"><strong data-start="1912" data-end="1925">48 hours:</strong> 8</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1930" data-end="1946">
<p data-start="1932" data-end="1946"><strong data-start="1932" data-end="1943">7 days:</strong> 14</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1949" data-end="1970">
<p data-start="1951" data-end="1970"><strong data-start="1951" data-end="1963">30 days:</strong> <strong data-start="1964" data-end="1970">21</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1972" data-end="2075">This is workable for an overall KM curve, but <strong data-start="2018" data-end="2074">stratifying into lots of groups will get sparse fast</strong>.</p>
<p data-start="2077" data-end="2152">Also: “ICU bounceback within the same hospitalization” exists but is small:</p>
<ul data-start="2153" data-end="2201">
<li data-start="2153" data-end="2201">
<p data-start="2155" data-end="2201"><strong data-start="2155" data-end="2171">9 admissions</strong> have <strong data-start="2177" data-end="2193">≥2 ICU stays</strong> (max 4)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2203" data-end="2287">So: <strong data-start="2207" data-end="2287">Hospital readmission KM = strong. ICU readmission KM = possible but tighter.</strong></p>
<hr data-start="2289" data-end="2292">
<h2 data-start="2294" data-end="2353">The one technical “gotcha” you’ll want to handle cleanly</h2>
<p data-start="2354" data-end="2454">For readmission KM: <strong data-start="2374" data-end="2415">in-hospital death is a competing risk</strong> (you can’t be readmitted if you died).</p>
<p data-start="2456" data-end="2597">Good news: there are only <strong data-start="2482" data-end="2517">15 admissions that end in death</strong> in this subset, and none of the observed readmission intervals come from those.</p>
<p data-start="2599" data-end="2633">For the course, you can do either:</p>
<ul data-start="2634" data-end="2827">
<li data-start="2634" data-end="2733">
<p data-start="2636" data-end="2733"><strong data-start="2636" data-end="2648">Simpler:</strong> restrict to <strong data-start="2661" data-end="2681">discharges alive</strong>, then KM time-to-readmission (state the limitation)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2734" data-end="2827">
<p data-start="2736" data-end="2827"><strong data-start="2736" data-end="2753">More correct:</strong> treat death as competing risk (optional upgrade if you feel like flexing)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2829" data-end="2832">
<h2 data-start="2834" data-end="2890">What I think you should do (given your QI background)</h2>
<p data-start="2891" data-end="2943">Start with <strong data-start="2902" data-end="2929">hospital readmission KM</strong> because it’s:</p>
<ul data-start="2944" data-end="3088">
<li data-start="2944" data-end="2978">
<p data-start="2946" data-end="2978">instantly legible to leadership,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2979" data-end="3026">
<p data-start="2981" data-end="3026">statistically more stable in this small demo,</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3027" data-end="3088">
<p data-start="3029" data-end="3088">and aligns with “realistically inform improvement efforts.”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3090" data-end="3172">Then (optional) add ICU readmission/bounceback as a secondary angle if it behaves.</p>
<h3 data-start="3174" data-end="3229">Your best “Module 1 / Module 2” exploration targets</h3>
<p data-start="3230" data-end="3263">Using only what you already have:</p>
<ul data-start="3264" data-end="3658">
<li data-start="3264" data-end="3301">
<p data-start="3266" data-end="3301">admissions per patient distribution</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3302" data-end="3333">
<p data-start="3304" data-end="3333">7/30/90-day readmission rates</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3334" data-end="3389">
<p data-start="3336" data-end="3389">KM curve: time to readmission after discharge (alive)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3390" data-end="3658">
<p data-start="3392" data-end="3447">stratify by 2–3 <em data-start="3408" data-end="3419">low-drama</em> variables you already have:</p>
<ul data-start="3450" data-end="3658">
<li data-start="3450" data-end="3490">
<p data-start="3452" data-end="3490">age group (from <code data-start="3468" data-end="3489">patients.anchor_age</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3493" data-end="3532">
<p data-start="3495" data-end="3532">admission type (urgent/elective/etc.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3535" data-end="3579">
<p data-start="3537" data-end="3579">insurance (proxy for access / social risk)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3582" data-end="3658">
<p data-start="3584" data-end="3658">“ICU exposure in admission” (whether that <code data-start="3626" data-end="3635">hadm_id</code> appears in <code data-start="3647" data-end="3657">icustays</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3660" data-end="3663">
<h2 data-start="3665" data-end="3701">If you want <em data-start="3680" data-end="3685">one</em> QI headline now</h2>
<p data-start="3702" data-end="3869"><strong data-start="3702" data-end="3789">“Time to readmission after discharge (KM), plus 30-day readmission as a benchmark.”</strong><br data-start="3789" data-end="3792">
It’s very QI, very defensible, and totally achievable with this dataset size.</p>
<p data-start="3871" data-end="4095">If you want, next step I can lay 
out the exact definitions you’ll paste into your report (index event, 
censoring rule, 30-day window, exclusions), so your methodology reads 
like a real QI analyst wrote it (because… one did).</p>

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="279">Totally fair — you don’t need to marry KM. The <strong data-start="47" data-end="60">good news</strong> is: even with just the 4 “spine” tables you uploaded, you already have <em data-start="132" data-end="142">multiple</em>
 QI-grade paths (readmission, ICU bounceback, LOS/flow timing). And yes,
 there’s enough longitudinal structure here to keep options open.</p>
<h3 data-start="281" data-end="349">First: what these 4 files already unlock (so we’re not guessing)</h3>
<p data-start="350" data-end="368">From <em data-start="355" data-end="361">your</em> files:</p>
<ul data-start="370" data-end="532">
<li data-start="370" data-end="401">
<p data-start="372" data-end="401">100 patients (<code data-start="386" data-end="400">patients.csv</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="402" data-end="446">
<p data-start="404" data-end="446">275 hospital admissions (<code data-start="429" data-end="445">admissions.csv</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="447" data-end="479">
<p data-start="449" data-end="479">140 ICU stays (<code data-start="464" data-end="478">icustays.csv</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="480" data-end="532">
<p data-start="482" data-end="532">1,190 transfer/location segments (<code data-start="516" data-end="531">transfers.csv</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="534" data-end="609">So this isn’t “100 patients = 100 visits.” There’s real repeat utilization:</p>
<ul data-start="610" data-end="836">
<li data-start="610" data-end="681">
<p data-start="612" data-end="681"><strong data-start="612" data-end="622">48/100</strong> patients have <strong data-start="637" data-end="654">2+ admissions</strong> (one patient has <strong data-start="672" data-end="678">20</strong>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="682" data-end="716">
<p data-start="684" data-end="716"><strong data-start="684" data-end="694">26/100</strong> have <strong data-start="700" data-end="716">2+ ICU stays</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="717" data-end="836">
<p data-start="719" data-end="836"><strong data-start="719" data-end="751">30-day hospital readmissions</strong> are common enough to analyze (I counted <strong data-start="792" data-end="798">53</strong> discharge→readmit intervals ≤30 days)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="838" data-end="904">That means you can absolutely do “recidivism,” <em data-start="885" data-end="889">or</em> you can pivot.</p>
<hr data-start="906" data-end="909">
<h2 data-start="911" data-end="981">Your throughput/FTE style analysis: what works here vs what doesn’t</h2>
<p data-start="982" data-end="1092">You’re describing <strong data-start="1000" data-end="1037">concurrent active cases at time t</strong> (interval overlap) → great in a production ED dataset.</p>
<h3 data-start="1094" data-end="1139">What <em data-start="1103" data-end="1112">doesn’t</em> translate cleanly to MIMIC</h3>
<p data-start="1140" data-end="1419">MIMIC deidentification uses <strong data-start="1168" data-end="1202">patient-specific date shifting</strong>, so across-patient “real calendar” concurrency is not meaningful for <strong data-start="1272" data-end="1294">true demand curves</strong> (e.g., “how many ICU patients were active at 3pm on Tuesdays”). You’d be stacking timelines that were shifted independently.</p>
<p data-start="1421" data-end="1574">Also: this dataset is a <strong data-start="1445" data-end="1478">subset of ICU-linked patients</strong>, not a full ED/hospital census, so it’s not appropriate for staffing math like “we need X FTE.”</p>
<h3 data-start="1576" data-end="1638">What <em data-start="1585" data-end="1591">does</em> translate beautifully (QI-throughput-adjacent)</h3>
<p data-start="1639" data-end="1755">You can still do interval-based flow metrics because <strong data-start="1692" data-end="1754">durations and sequencing within a hospitalization are real</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="1757" data-end="2145">
<li data-start="1757" data-end="1830">
<p data-start="1759" data-end="1830"><strong data-start="1759" data-end="1770">ED time</strong> (from <code data-start="1777" data-end="1788">transfers</code> careunit = Emergency Department / ED Obs)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1831" data-end="1941">
<p data-start="1833" data-end="1941"><strong data-start="1833" data-end="1881">Time from hospital admission → ICU admission</strong> (from <code data-start="1888" data-end="1910">admissions.admittime</code> to earliest <code data-start="1923" data-end="1940">icustays.intime</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1942" data-end="2145">
<p data-start="1944" data-end="2038"><strong data-start="1944" data-end="1962">ICU bounceback</strong> within the same hospitalization (ICU stay → non-ICU → ICU again within 48h)</p>
<ul data-start="2041" data-end="2145">
<li data-start="2041" data-end="2145">
<p data-start="2043" data-end="2145">In your data there are <strong data-start="2066" data-end="2071">8</strong> ICU bouncebacks within <strong data-start="2095" data-end="2102">48h</strong> (same hospitalization) — that’s <em data-start="2135" data-end="2141">very</em> QI.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2147" data-end="2230">Think of it as: <strong data-start="2163" data-end="2195">process timing + transitions</strong>, not “system-wide real-time load.”</p>
<hr data-start="2232" data-end="2235">
<h2 data-start="2237" data-end="2307">Three “baskets” we can keep open (so you’re not all-in on one idea)</h2>
<h3 data-start="2308" data-end="2374">Basket A — Utilization &amp; “recidivism” (your original instinct)</h3>
<ul data-start="2375" data-end="2512">
<li data-start="2375" data-end="2423">
<p data-start="2377" data-end="2423">Time to next admission (or 30-day readmission)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2424" data-end="2447">
<p data-start="2426" data-end="2447">Time to next ICU stay</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2448" data-end="2512">
<p data-start="2450" data-end="2512">Stratify by ICU exposure, admission type, insurance, age bands</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2514" data-end="2566"><strong data-start="2514" data-end="2532">Why it’s good:</strong> classic QI + leadership-friendly.</p>
<h3 data-start="2568" data-end="2629">Basket B — Flow &amp; stability (throughput-ish, QI-friendly)</h3>
<ul data-start="2630" data-end="2874">
<li data-start="2630" data-end="2692">
<p data-start="2632" data-end="2692">Time to ICU from hospital admit (early vs late ICU transfer)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2693" data-end="2754">
<p data-start="2695" data-end="2754">ED time before inpatient/ICU placement (within this cohort)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2755" data-end="2812">
<p data-start="2757" data-end="2812">ICU bounceback (48h / 7d), stepdown instability signals</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2813" data-end="2874">
<p data-start="2815" data-end="2874">Transfer “pathways” (ED → ICU → floor → discharge patterns)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2876" data-end="2929"><strong data-start="2876" data-end="2894">Why it’s good:</strong> aligns with how you already think.</p>
<h3 data-start="2931" data-end="3003">Basket C — Clinical intensity / severity proxies (to support A or B)</h3>
<p data-start="3004" data-end="3134">This is where additional tables matter: early labs/vitals/therapies to explain <em data-start="3083" data-end="3088">why</em> some stays bounce back, run long, or readmit.</p>
<hr data-start="3136" data-end="3139">
<h2 data-start="3141" data-end="3218">Yes: let’s look at a few more files. Here are the <em data-start="3194" data-end="3210">best next ones</em> to pull</h2>
<p data-start="3219" data-end="3282">If you want maximal flexibility with minimal chaos, grab these:</p>
<h3 data-start="3284" data-end="3341">Must-have dictionaries (so columns are interpretable)</h3>
<ul data-start="3342" data-end="3414">
<li data-start="3342" data-end="3365">
<p data-start="3344" data-end="3365"><code data-start="3344" data-end="3365">hosp/d_labitems.csv</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3366" data-end="3385">
<p data-start="3368" data-end="3385"><code data-start="3368" data-end="3385">icu/d_items.csv</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3386" data-end="3414">
<p data-start="3388" data-end="3414"><code data-start="3388" data-end="3414">hosp/d_icd_diagnoses.csv</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3416" data-end="3457">Clinical signals (best ROI for “why”)</h3>
<ul data-start="3458" data-end="3610">
<li data-start="3458" data-end="3533">
<p data-start="3460" data-end="3533"><code data-start="3460" data-end="3480">hosp/labevents.csv</code>  <em data-start="3482" data-end="3533">(labs; huge value for early risk + QI hypotheses)</em></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3534" data-end="3610">
<p data-start="3536" data-end="3610"><code data-start="3536" data-end="3557">icu/chartevents.csv</code> <em data-start="3558" data-end="3610">(vitals/flowsheets; can be big but extremely rich)</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3612" data-end="3643">Clinical context &amp; grouping</h3>
<ul data-start="3644" data-end="3726">
<li data-start="3644" data-end="3726">
<p data-start="3646" data-end="3726"><code data-start="3646" data-end="3670">hosp/diagnoses_icd.csv</code> <em data-start="3671" data-end="3726">(comorbidity-ish context; helps stratify and explain)</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="3728" data-end="3769">Interventions (optional but powerful)</h3>
<ul data-start="3770" data-end="3927">
<li data-start="3770" data-end="3850">
<p data-start="3772" data-end="3850"><code data-start="3772" data-end="3793">icu/inputevents.csv</code> <em data-start="3794" data-end="3850">(vasopressors/fluids etc depending on what’s included)</em></p>
</li>
<li data-start="3851" data-end="3927">
<p data-start="3853" data-end="3927"><code data-start="3853" data-end="3878">icu/procedureevents.csv</code> <em data-start="3879" data-end="3927">(vents, lines, etc — depends on demo contents)</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3929" data-end="4084">If you upload just <strong data-start="3948" data-end="4008">labevents + d_labitems + diagnoses_icd + d_icd_diagnoses</strong>, we can already build strong QI narratives without drowning in chartevents.</p>
<hr data-start="4086" data-end="4089">
<h2 data-start="4091" data-end="4118">My take on your instinct</h2>
<p data-start="4119" data-end="4239">You’re right to be skeptical about “throughput staffing math” here — but you’re also right that the dataset is flexible.</p>
<p data-start="4241" data-end="4274">This MIMIC demo is <em data-start="4260" data-end="4269">perfect</em> for:</p>
<ul data-start="4275" data-end="4412">
<li data-start="4275" data-end="4337">
<p data-start="4277" data-end="4337"><strong data-start="4277" data-end="4313">time-to-event / bounceback / LOS</strong> style QI questions, and</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4338" data-end="4412">
<p data-start="4340" data-end="4412">“what early signals predict a rough course?” (labs/vitals/interventions)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4414" data-end="4439">It’s <strong data-start="4419" data-end="4426">not</strong> perfect for:</p>
<ul data-start="4440" data-end="4510">
<li data-start="4440" data-end="4510">
<p data-start="4442" data-end="4510">real-world census curves and FTE demand planning over calendar time.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="4512" data-end="4515">
<p data-start="4517" data-end="4796">If you want a clean next move: upload these four next files (if present):<br data-start="4590" data-end="4593">
<strong data-start="4593" data-end="4674"><code data-start="4595" data-end="4610">labevents.csv</code>, <code data-start="4612" data-end="4628">d_labitems.csv</code>, <code data-start="4630" data-end="4649">diagnoses_icd.csv</code>, <code data-start="4651" data-end="4672">d_icd_diagnoses.csv</code></strong><br data-start="4674" data-end="4677">
…and I’ll tell you, based on what’s actually in them, which 2–3 analysis directions are the best “capstone-grade” bets.</p>

Dimension table for labevents provides a description of all lab items.
d_labitems

d_labitems contains definitions for all itemid associated with lab measurements in the MIMIC database. All data in labevents link to the d_labitems table. Each unique (fluid, category, label) tuple in the hospital database was assigned an itemid in this table, and the use of this itemid facilitates efficient storage and querying of the data.

Laboratory data contains information collected and recorded in the hospital laboratory database. This includes measurements made in wards within the hospital and clinics outside the hospital. Most concepts in this table have been mapped to LOINC codes, an openly available ontology which facilitates interoperability.
Links to

    labevents on itemid

Important considerations

This table used to contain a column called loinc_code, which stored standardized identifiers for laboratory measurements. To support ongoing improvement of these labels, the assignment of LOINC codes is now done in the MIMIC Code Repository.
Table columns
Name 	Postgres data type
itemid 	INTEGER
label 	VARCHAR(50)
fluid 	VARCHAR(50)
category 	VARCHAR(50)
Detailed Description
itemid

A unique identifier for a laboratory concept. itemid is unique to each row, and can be used to identify data in labevents associated with a specific concept.
label

The label column describes the concept which is represented by the itemid.
fluid

fluid describes the substance on which the measurement was made. For example, chemistry measurements are frequently performed on blood, which is listed in this column as ‘BLOOD’. Many of these measurements are also acquirable on other fluids, such as urine, and this column differentiates these distinct concepts.
category
category provides higher level information as to the type of measurement. For example, a category of ‘ABG’ indicates that the measurement is an arterial blood gas.""" """d_icd_diagnoses
Dimension table for diagnoses_icd; provides a description of ICD-9/ICD-10 billed diagnoses.
The d_icd_diagnoses table

This table defines International Classification of Diseases (ICD) Version 9 and 10 codes for diagnoses. These codes are assigned at the end of the patient’s stay and are used by the hospital to bill for care provided.
Links to

    diagnoses_icd ON icd_code and icd_version

Table columns
Name 	Postgres data type
icd_code 	CHAR(7) NOT NULL
icd_version 	INTEGER NOT NULL
long_title 	VARCHAR(255)
Detailed Description
icd_code, icd_version

icd_code is the International Coding Definitions (ICD) code.

There are two versions for this coding system: version 9 (ICD-9) and version 10 (ICD-10). These can be differentiated using the icd_version column. In general, ICD-10 codes are more detailed, though code mappings (or “cross-walks”) exist which convert ICD-9 codes to ICD-10 codes.

Both ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes are often presented with a decimal. This decimal is not required for interpretation of an ICD code; i.e. the icd_code of ‘0010’ is equivalent to ‘001.0’.

ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes have distinct formats: ICD-9 codes are 5 character long strings which are entirely numeric (with the exception of codes prefixed with “E” or “V” which are used for external causes of injury or supplemental classification). Importantly, ICD-9 codes are retained as strings in the database as the leading 0s in codes are meaningful.

ICD-10 codes are 3-7 characters long and always prefixed by a letter followed by a set of numeric values.
long_title
The long_title provides the meaning of the ICD code. For example, the ICD-9 code 0010 has long_title “Cholera due to vibrio cholerae”.""" """d_items
Dimension table describing itemid. Defines concepts recorded in the events table in the ICU module.
The d_items table

Table source: Metavision ICU databases.

Table purpose: Definition table for all items in the ICU databases.

Number of rows: 4,014

Links to:

    chartevents on itemid
    datetimeevents on itemid
    inputevents on itemid
    outputevents on itemid
    procedureevents on itemid

Important considerations

    If the linksto column is null, then the data is currently unavailable, but planned for a future release.

Table columns
Name 	Postgres data type
itemid 	INTEGER
label 	VARCHAR(200)
abbreviation 	VARCHAR(100)
linksto 	VARCHAR(50)
category 	VARCHAR(100)
unitname 	VARCHAR(100)
param_type 	VARCHAR(30)
lownormalvalue 	FLOAT
highnormalvalue 	FLOAT
Detailed Description

The D_ITEMS table defines itemid, which represents measurements in the database. Measurements of the same type (e.g. heart rate) will have the same itemid (e.g. 220045). Values in the itemid column are unique to each row. All itemids will have a value &gt; 220000.
itemid

As an alternate primary key to the table, itemid is unique to each row.
label, abbreviation

The label column describes the concept which is represented by the itemid. The abbreviation column, only available in Metavision, lists a common abbreviation for the label.
linksto

linksto provides the table name which the data links to. For example, a value of ‘chartevents’ indicates that the itemid of the given row is contained in CHARTEVENTS. A single itemid is only used in one event table, that is, if an itemid is contained in CHARTEVENTS it will not be contained in any other event table (e.g. IOEVENTS, CHARTEVENTS, etc).
category

category provides some information of the type of data the itemid corresponds to. Examples include ‘ABG’, which indicates the measurement is sourced from an arterial blood gas, ‘IV Medication’, which indicates that the medication is administered through an intravenous line, and so on.
unitname

unitname specifies the unit of measurement used for the itemid. This column is not always available, and this may be because the unit of measurement varies, a unit of measurement does not make sense for the given data type, or the unit of measurement is simply missing. Note that there is sometimes additional information on the unit of measurement in the associated event table, e.g. the valueuom column in CHARTEVENTS.
param_type

param_type describes the type of data which is recorded: a date, a number or a text field.
lownormalvalue, highnormalvalue
These columns store reference ranges for the measurement. Note that a reference range encompasses the expected value of a measurement: values outside of this may still be physiologically plausible, but are considered unusual."""</div></div></div></div></div><div class="z-0 flex justify-end"><div class="touch:-me-2 touch:-ms-3.5 -ms-2.5 -me-1 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-y-4 p-1 select-none wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="183">Yep — with these extra tables, you’ve officially got <em data-start="53" data-end="63">multiple</em> viable “baskets,” and (importantly) enough event-level signal to do real ICU/QI-style work even with only 100 patients.</p>
<h2 data-start="185" data-end="228">Quick inventory (what you actually have)</h2>
<p data-start="229" data-end="257">From the files you uploaded:</p>
<ul data-start="259" data-end="1411">
<li data-start="259" data-end="619">
<p data-start="261" data-end="287"><strong data-start="261" data-end="287">Core “who/when” tables</strong></p>
<ul data-start="290" data-end="619">
<li data-start="290" data-end="332">
<p data-start="292" data-end="332"><code data-start="292" data-end="302">patients</code> (<strong data-start="304" data-end="311">100</strong> unique <code data-start="319" data-end="331">subject_id</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="335" data-end="468">
<p data-start="337" data-end="468"><code data-start="337" data-end="349">admissions</code> (<strong data-start="351" data-end="358">275</strong> <code data-start="359" data-end="368">hadm_id</code>) — includes <em data-start="381" data-end="400">hospital outcomes</em> (<code data-start="402" data-end="424">hospital_expire_flag</code>) + ED timestamps (<code data-start="443" data-end="454">edregtime</code>, <code data-start="456" data-end="467">edouttime</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="471" data-end="535">
<p data-start="473" data-end="535"><code data-start="473" data-end="483">icustays</code> (<strong data-start="485" data-end="492">140</strong> <code data-start="493" data-end="502">stay_id</code>) — ICU start/stop, unit, ICU LOS</p>
</li>
<li data-start="538" data-end="619">
<p data-start="540" data-end="619"><code data-start="540" data-end="551">transfers</code> (<strong data-start="553" data-end="560">709</strong> <code data-start="561" data-end="574">transfer_id</code>) — step-by-step movements between care units</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="621" data-end="1100">
<p data-start="623" data-end="658"><strong data-start="623" data-end="658">Clinical “what happened” tables</strong></p>
<ul data-start="661" data-end="1100">
<li data-start="661" data-end="749">
<p data-start="663" data-end="749"><code data-start="663" data-end="676">chartevents</code> (<strong data-start="678" data-end="689">668,862</strong> rows) — high-frequency vitals/assessments tied to <code data-start="740" data-end="749">stay_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="752" data-end="850">
<p data-start="754" data-end="850"><code data-start="754" data-end="765">labevents</code> (<strong data-start="767" data-end="778">107,727</strong> rows) — labs tied mostly to <code data-start="807" data-end="816">hadm_id</code> (but ~26% don’t have a <code data-start="840" data-end="849">hadm_id</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="853" data-end="940">
<p data-start="855" data-end="940"><code data-start="855" data-end="868">inputevents</code> (<strong data-start="870" data-end="880">20,404</strong> rows) — meds/fluids with start/stop times tied to <code data-start="931" data-end="940">stay_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="943" data-end="1033">
<p data-start="945" data-end="1033"><code data-start="945" data-end="962">procedureevents</code> (<strong data-start="964" data-end="973">1,468</strong> rows) — ventilation, imaging, lines, etc. tied to <code data-start="1024" data-end="1033">stay_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1036" data-end="1100">
<p data-start="1038" data-end="1100"><code data-start="1038" data-end="1053">diagnoses_icd</code> (<strong data-start="1055" data-end="1064">2,601</strong> rows) — diagnoses tied to <code data-start="1091" data-end="1100">hadm_id</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1102" data-end="1411">
<p data-start="1104" data-end="1169"><strong data-start="1104" data-end="1169">Dictionary / dimension tables (the glue that makes it usable)</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1172" data-end="1411">
<li data-start="1172" data-end="1270">
<p data-start="1174" data-end="1270"><code data-start="1174" data-end="1183">d_items</code> (<strong data-start="1185" data-end="1194">4,014</strong>) maps ICU <code data-start="1205" data-end="1213">itemid</code> → human labels (chartevents/inputevents/procedureevents)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1273" data-end="1344">
<p data-start="1275" data-end="1344"><code data-start="1275" data-end="1287">d_labitems</code> (<strong data-start="1289" data-end="1298">1,624</strong>) maps lab <code data-start="1309" data-end="1317">itemid</code> → human labels (labevents)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1347" data-end="1411">
<p data-start="1349" data-end="1411"><code data-start="1349" data-end="1366">d_icd_diagnoses</code> (<strong data-start="1368" data-end="1379">109,775</strong>) maps ICD code → diagnosis name</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-start="1413" data-end="1471">How it’s interconnected (the join graph you’re missing)</h2>
<p data-start="1472" data-end="1496">Think of <strong data-start="1481" data-end="1495">three keys</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="1498" data-end="1640">
<li data-start="1498" data-end="1522">
<p data-start="1500" data-end="1522"><code data-start="1500" data-end="1512">subject_id</code> = patient</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1523" data-end="1565">
<p data-start="1525" data-end="1565"><code data-start="1525" data-end="1534">hadm_id</code> = hospital encounter/admission</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1566" data-end="1640">
<p data-start="1568" data-end="1640"><code data-start="1568" data-end="1577">stay_id</code> = ICU stay (a hospitalization can have <strong data-start="1617" data-end="1639">multiple ICU stays</strong>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1642" data-end="1666">And <strong data-start="1646" data-end="1665">one mapping key</strong>:</p>
<ul data-start="1667" data-end="1761">
<li data-start="1667" data-end="1761">
<p data-start="1669" data-end="1761"><code data-start="1669" data-end="1677">itemid</code> = “what measurement/med/procedure is this?” (resolved via <code data-start="1736" data-end="1745">d_items</code> / <code data-start="1748" data-end="1760">d_labitems</code>)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1763" data-end="1783"><strong data-start="1763" data-end="1783">Practical joins:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1784" data-end="2187">
<li data-start="1784" data-end="1827">
<p data-start="1786" data-end="1827"><code data-start="1786" data-end="1796">patients</code> → <code data-start="1799" data-end="1811">admissions</code> on <code data-start="1815" data-end="1827">subject_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1828" data-end="1873">
<p data-start="1830" data-end="1873"><code data-start="1830" data-end="1842">admissions</code> → <code data-start="1845" data-end="1860">diagnoses_icd</code> on <code data-start="1864" data-end="1873">hadm_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1874" data-end="1914">
<p data-start="1876" data-end="1914"><code data-start="1876" data-end="1888">admissions</code> → <code data-start="1891" data-end="1901">icustays</code> on <code data-start="1905" data-end="1914">hadm_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1915" data-end="1992">
<p data-start="1917" data-end="1992"><code data-start="1917" data-end="1927">icustays</code> → (<code data-start="1931" data-end="1944">chartevents</code>, <code data-start="1946" data-end="1959">inputevents</code>, <code data-start="1961" data-end="1978">procedureevents</code>) on <code data-start="1983" data-end="1992">stay_id</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1993" data-end="2115">
<p data-start="1995" data-end="2115"><code data-start="1995" data-end="2006">labevents</code> joins best via <code data-start="2022" data-end="2031">hadm_id</code> <strong data-start="2032" data-end="2039">and</strong> time-windowing to ICU (<code data-start="2063" data-end="2074">charttime</code> between <code data-start="2083" data-end="2100">icustays.intime</code> and <code data-start="2105" data-end="2114">outtime</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2116" data-end="2187">
<p data-start="2118" data-end="2187">Use <code data-start="2122" data-end="2131">d_items</code> / <code data-start="2134" data-end="2146">d_labitems</code> to turn <code data-start="2155" data-end="2163">itemid</code> into readable variables</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-start="2189" data-end="2254">The “throughput/FTE demand” catch (why your instinct is right)</h2>
<p data-start="2255" data-end="2649">MIMIC’s dates are <strong data-start="2273" data-end="2284">shifted</strong> for privacy, and the shifts are <strong data-start="2317" data-end="2337">patient-specific</strong>. That preserves <em data-start="2354" data-end="2380">within-patient intervals</em> (great for LOS, time-to-event, care timelines), but it breaks the idea of <strong data-start="2455" data-end="2487">true system-wide concurrency</strong>
 (your “active cases at any moment in time across the whole hospital”) 
because patient A’s “2148-08-16” isn’t the same real-world day as 
patient B’s “2148-08-16”.</p>
<p data-start="2651" data-end="2654">So:</p>
<ul data-start="2655" data-end="2871">
<li data-start="2655" data-end="2769">
<p data-start="2657" data-end="2769">✅ You <em data-start="2663" data-end="2668">can</em> do process interval work (ED→ICU time, ICU LOS, time-to-extubation, time-to-vasopressor start, etc.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2770" data-end="2871">
<p data-start="2772" data-end="2871">🚫 You <em data-start="2779" data-end="2786">can’t</em> do real staffing-by-clock-time occupancy curves like you’d do in production ops data</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-start="2873" data-end="2919">What these tables enable (multiple baskets)</h2>
<p data-start="2920" data-end="2961">Here are your best options, with QI tilt:</p>
<h3 data-start="2963" data-end="3032">Option A — ICU-stay-level QI modeling (my default recommendation)</h3>
<p data-start="3033" data-end="3070"><strong data-start="3033" data-end="3042">Unit:</strong> 1 row per <code data-start="3053" data-end="3062">stay_id</code> (n=140)</p>
<p data-start="3072" data-end="3100"><strong data-start="3072" data-end="3100">Outcomes you can defend:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="3101" data-end="3249">
<li data-start="3101" data-end="3172">
<p data-start="3103" data-end="3172">ICU LOS (continuous) or “prolonged ICU LOS” (e.g., &gt; 75th percentile)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3173" data-end="3249">
<p data-start="3175" data-end="3249">In-hospital mortality (15 deaths total; all are in ICU-related admissions)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3251" data-end="3286"><strong data-start="3251" data-end="3286">Features you can build cleanly:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="3287" data-end="3597">
<li data-start="3287" data-end="3351">
<p data-start="3289" data-end="3351">First-24h vitals from <code data-start="3311" data-end="3324">chartevents</code> (HR, RR, SpO2, NIBP, etc.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3352" data-end="3424">
<p data-start="3354" data-end="3424">Early labs from <code data-start="3370" data-end="3381">labevents</code> (Cr, BUN, Na, K, Hgb/Hct, platelets, etc.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3425" data-end="3511">
<p data-start="3427" data-end="3511">Treatment intensity from <code data-start="3452" data-end="3465">inputevents</code> (e.g., norepinephrine, propofol, antibiotics)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3512" data-end="3597">
<p data-start="3514" data-end="3597">Procedures from <code data-start="3530" data-end="3547">procedureevents</code> (invasive ventilation/extubation, imaging, lines)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3599" data-end="3866"><strong data-start="3599" data-end="3608">Pros:</strong> very CRISP-DM-friendly, strong “QI vibe,” uses the ICU module the way it’s meant to be used.<br data-start="3701" data-end="3704">
<strong data-start="3704" data-end="3713">Cons:</strong> sample size = 140 → keep models interpretable (penalized regression, simple trees) and focus more on <em data-start="3815" data-end="3840">evidence-based insights</em> than leaderboard-chasing.</p>
<h3 data-start="3868" data-end="3927">Option B — Admission-level outcomes + recidivism flavor</h3>
<p data-start="3928" data-end="3965"><strong data-start="3928" data-end="3937">Unit:</strong> 1 row per <code data-start="3948" data-end="3957">hadm_id</code> (n=275)</p>
<p data-start="3967" data-end="4010">You actually <em data-start="3980" data-end="3984">do</em> have repeated admissions:</p>
<ul data-start="4011" data-end="4144">
<li data-start="4011" data-end="4144">
<p data-start="4013" data-end="4144">86 “next-admission intervals” across patients (good enough for <strong data-start="4076" data-end="4106">readmission rate summaries</strong>, maybe a simple time-to-readmit view)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4146" data-end="4160">This supports:</p>
<ul data-start="4161" data-end="4286">
<li data-start="4161" data-end="4236">
<p data-start="4163" data-end="4236">7/30/90-day readmission counts (descriptive + stratified by risk factors)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4237" data-end="4286">
<p data-start="4239" data-end="4286">Hospital LOS and discharge disposition analyses</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4288" data-end="4457"><strong data-start="4288" data-end="4297">Pros:</strong> more rows, easier “hospital admin” story.<br data-start="4339" data-end="4342">
<strong data-start="4342" data-end="4351">Cons:</strong> you’ll still end up summarizing ICU events into admission-level features (doable, just more design work).</p>
<h3 data-start="4459" data-end="4536">Option C — Time-to-event (Kaplan–Meier) that <em data-start="4508" data-end="4536">actually fits this dataset</em></h3>
<p data-start="4537" data-end="4626">KM makes sense when you have <strong data-start="4566" data-end="4595">time-to-event + censoring</strong>. The best candidates here are:</p>
<ul data-start="4628" data-end="5000">
<li data-start="4628" data-end="4741">
<p data-start="4630" data-end="4741"><strong data-start="4630" data-end="4652">Time to extubation</strong> among ventilated patients (you have both “Invasive Ventilation” and “Extubation” events)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4742" data-end="4858">
<p data-start="4744" data-end="4858"><strong data-start="4744" data-end="4796">Survival from ICU admission to in-hospital death</strong> (censor at discharge; only 15 events, so interpret carefully)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4859" data-end="5000">
<p data-start="4861" data-end="5000"><strong data-start="4861" data-end="4879">ICU bounceback</strong> within same hospitalization (there are 12 ICU-return intervals; 8 within 48h) — probably descriptive, not heavy modeling</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="5002" data-end="5080">Option D — Process metrics (QI narrative without pretending it’s staffing)</h3>
<p data-start="5081" data-end="5090">Examples:</p>
<ul data-start="5091" data-end="5276">
<li data-start="5091" data-end="5146">
<p data-start="5093" data-end="5146">ED arrival → ICU admission time (when ED times exist)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5147" data-end="5200">
<p data-start="5149" data-end="5200">Admission → ICU time (you can compute this broadly)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5201" data-end="5276">
<p data-start="5203" data-end="5276">ICU transitions using <code data-start="5225" data-end="5236">transfers</code> (sequence patterns, time in unit types)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="5278" data-end="5360">This is great for “operational relevance,” just not full “demand staffing curves.”</p>
<h2 data-start="5362" data-end="5421">A couple “sanity anchor” insights from your actual files</h2>
<p data-start="5422" data-end="5450">Just to ground expectations:</p>
<ul data-start="5452" data-end="5674">
<li data-start="5452" data-end="5553">
<p data-start="5454" data-end="5553"><strong data-start="5454" data-end="5505">140 ICU stays across 128 ICU-related admissions</strong> (so yes, some bouncebacks/multiple stays exist)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5554" data-end="5609">
<p data-start="5556" data-end="5609"><strong data-start="5556" data-end="5585">Median ICU LOS ~2.16 days</strong> (75th ~4.91; max ~20.5)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5610" data-end="5674">
<p data-start="5612" data-end="5674"><strong data-start="5612" data-end="5665">In-hospital mortality among ICU admissions ~11.7%</strong> (15/128)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="5676" data-end="5809">And your meds/procedures data is <em data-start="5709" data-end="5722">rich enough</em> to support severity/treatment-intensity proxies (vasopressors, sedation, ventilation).</p>
<h2 data-start="5811" data-end="5878">What I’d do next (Module 1 “Data Discovery” deliverable mindset)</h2>
<p data-start="5879" data-end="5955">Pick <strong data-start="5884" data-end="5891">one</strong> primary analysis spine now (you can add a side analysis later):</p>
<p data-start="5957" data-end="6033"><strong data-start="5957" data-end="5979">Recommended spine:</strong> <em data-start="5980" data-end="5996">ICU-stay-level</em> with an “early window” feature set</p>
<ol data-start="6034" data-end="6406">
<li data-start="6034" data-end="6080">
<p data-start="6037" data-end="6080">Define cohort: all ICU stays (<code data-start="6067" data-end="6077">icustays</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6081" data-end="6136">
<p data-start="6084" data-end="6136">Define feature window: first 6h or 24h of ICU stay</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6137" data-end="6247">
<p data-start="6140" data-end="6247">Define outcomes: prolonged ICU LOS + mortality (and optionally time-to-extubation as a KM “figure candy”)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6248" data-end="6406">
<p data-start="6251" data-end="6406">Build a single “analysis-ready” 
table: one row per stay, columns grouped as Demographics / Admission / 
Early Vitals / Early Labs / Interventions / Outcomes</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="6408" data-end="6595">If you want, paste the <strong data-start="6431" data-end="6459">list of CSVs in your zip</strong> (or upload the zip) and I’ll tell you exactly which <em data-start="6512" data-end="6524">additional</em> tables are worth bringing in vs. which are noise for a clean capstone.</p>
<p data-start="6597" data-end="6802">Also: once you’re happy with the repo skeleton + your first real README draft, <strong data-start="6676" data-end="6692">commit early</strong> (even if it’s just scaffolding + notes). That “show your work” repo being clean matters a lot in this course.</p>
