empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="182">100% — and that’s exactly the <em data-start="30" data-end="37">right</em> ICU/QI instinct: <strong data-start="55" data-end="83">“ICU” isn’t a phenotype.</strong> It’s a location + intensity of care, and the pathway is driven by the underlying <em data-start="165" data-end="181">reason for ICU</em>.</p>
<p data-start="184" data-end="311">You don’t have to solve it today, but you <em data-start="226" data-end="234">should</em> set yourself up so you can segment cleanly later without redoing everything.</p>
<h2 data-start="313" data-end="391">The practical way to handle “different ICU types” without boiling the ocean</h2>
<h3 data-start="393" data-end="468">1) Start with a broad cohort, but bake in a “pathway label” placeholder</h3>
<p data-start="469" data-end="548">Early in the project (Module 2-ish), create an admission/stay-level field like:</p>
<ul data-start="550" data-end="732">
<li data-start="550" data-end="619">
<p data-start="552" data-end="619"><code data-start="552" data-end="568">index_dx_group</code> (trauma / sepsis / neuro / cardiac / resp / other)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="620" data-end="664">
<p data-start="622" data-end="664"><code data-start="622" data-end="645">dominant_service_line</code> (if you can infer)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="665" data-end="732">
<p data-start="667" data-end="732"><code data-start="667" data-end="685">icu_reason_proxy</code> (derived from diagnosis + early interventions)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="734" data-end="856">Even if it’s crude at first, having the column in your analysis table prevents you from having to rebuild downstream code.</p>
<h3 data-start="858" data-end="937">2) Use diagnoses as the first-pass grouping (fast, defensible, not perfect)</h3>
<p data-start="938" data-end="955">You already have:</p>
<ul data-start="956" data-end="1033">
<li data-start="956" data-end="989">
<p data-start="958" data-end="989"><code data-start="958" data-end="973">diagnoses_icd</code> (per <code data-start="979" data-end="988">hadm_id</code>)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="990" data-end="1033">
<p data-start="992" data-end="1033"><code data-start="992" data-end="1009">d_icd_diagnoses</code> (human-readable titles)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1035" data-end="1072">So you can build groupings in phases:</p>
<p data-start="1074" data-end="1132"><strong data-start="1074" data-end="1094">Phase 1 (cheap):</strong> group by ICD chapter / prefix rules</p>
<ul data-start="1133" data-end="1319">
<li data-start="1133" data-end="1183">
<p data-start="1135" data-end="1183">Trauma: ICD-10 <code data-start="1150" data-end="1154">S*</code>/<code data-start="1155" data-end="1159">T*</code> or ICD-9 <code data-start="1169" data-end="1178">800–959</code> etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1184" data-end="1221">
<p data-start="1186" data-end="1221">Stroke: ICD-10 <code data-start="1201" data-end="1207">I63*</code>, <code data-start="1209" data-end="1215">I61*</code>, etc.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1222" data-end="1271">
<p data-start="1224" data-end="1271">STEMI: ICD-10 <code data-start="1238" data-end="1244">I21*</code> (with subsets if you want)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1272" data-end="1319">
<p data-start="1274" data-end="1319">Sepsis: ICD-10 <code data-start="1289" data-end="1295">A41*</code>, <code data-start="1297" data-end="1305">R65.2*</code> etc (messier)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1321" data-end="1370">This gives you “good enough to explore” segments.</p>
<p data-start="1372" data-end="1442"><strong data-start="1372" data-end="1393">Phase 2 (better):</strong> enrich with <em data-start="1406" data-end="1421">interventions</em> as pathway markers</p>
<ul data-start="1443" data-end="1608">
<li data-start="1443" data-end="1531">
<p data-start="1445" data-end="1531"><code data-start="1445" data-end="1462">procedureevents</code>: ventilation, extubation, dialysis-ish, etc (depends what’s in demo)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1532" data-end="1608">
<p data-start="1534" data-end="1608"><code data-start="1534" data-end="1547">inputevents</code>: vasopressors, sedation, antibiotics classes (again depends)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1610" data-end="1730">Now “neuro ICU” isn’t just an ICD label — you’ll see clinical intensity patterns that make the grouping more believable.</p>
<h3 data-start="1732" data-end="1789">3) Guardrail: don’t over-segment with N=140 ICU stays</h3>
<p data-start="1790" data-end="1850">This dataset <em data-start="1803" data-end="1809">will</em> punish you if you try to do 12 subtypes.</p>
<p data-start="1852" data-end="1871">A solid compromise:</p>
<ul data-start="1872" data-end="2005">
<li data-start="1872" data-end="1968">
<p data-start="1874" data-end="1968">start with <strong data-start="1885" data-end="1911">3–5 high-level buckets</strong> (e.g., cardiac / neuro / trauma / infection-ish / other)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1969" data-end="2005">
<p data-start="1971" data-end="2005">anything too small becomes “other”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2007" data-end="2071">That keeps plots/models stable and stops you from chasing noise.</p>
<hr data-start="2073" data-end="2076">
<h2 data-start="2078" data-end="2139">How this connects to your likely final story (QI-friendly)</h2>
<p data-start="2140" data-end="2160">You can frame it as:</p>
<blockquote data-start="2162" data-end="2426">
<p data-start="2164" data-end="2426">“We built an early-window ICU risk 
and utilization model, then tested whether the relationships differ 
across major clinical pathways (cardiac vs neuro vs trauma…). Some 
factors are global predictors; others are pathway-specific, suggesting 
different QI levers.”</p>
</blockquote>
<p data-start="2428" data-end="2506">That’s <em data-start="2435" data-end="2444">exactly</em> how QI people talk: <strong data-start="2465" data-end="2506">global levers vs service-line levers.</strong></p>
<hr data-start="2508" data-end="2511">
<h2 data-start="2513" data-end="2572">Tiny setup task you can do now (no deep exploration yet)</h2>
<p data-start="2573" data-end="2678">When you build your first “analysis-ready” stay table, include these columns even if they’re blank/rough:</p>
<ul data-start="2679" data-end="2886">
<li data-start="2679" data-end="2705">
<p data-start="2681" data-end="2705"><code data-start="2681" data-end="2696">pathway_group</code> (string)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2706" data-end="2762">
<p data-start="2708" data-end="2762"><code data-start="2708" data-end="2723">index_dx_top1</code> (the first/primary ICD title you pick)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2763" data-end="2821">
<p data-start="2765" data-end="2821"><code data-start="2765" data-end="2775">dx_count</code> (# diagnoses on admission — proxy complexity)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2822" data-end="2886">
<p data-start="2824" data-end="2886"><code data-start="2824" data-end="2842">icu_service_hint</code> (optional, if you infer from careunit/unit)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2888" data-end="2961">It’s like leaving mounting holes in the wall before you hang the cabinet.</p>
<hr data-start="2963" data-end="2966">
<p data-start="2968" data-end="3033">Whenever you’re ready, the next <em data-start="3000" data-end="3024">low-effort, high-value</em> step is:</p>
<ul data-start="3034" data-end="3137">
<li data-start="3034" data-end="3137">
<p data-start="3036" data-end="3137">pull the <strong data-start="3045" data-end="3077">top 20 diagnosis long_titles</strong> among ICU-related admissions and map them into 4–5 buckets.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3139" data-end="3258">I can help you make a clean mapping table (rules-based) that looks professional in the report and keeps your code tidy.</p>

<p data-start="189" data-end="282">Here’s a clean way to “call in the favor” without making it weird or time-consuming for them.</p>
<h2 data-start="284" data-end="320">What to ask for (keep it <em data-start="312" data-end="319">tight</em>)</h2>
<p data-start="321" data-end="379">You want <strong data-start="330" data-end="347">10–15 minutes</strong> of guidance on just two things:</p>
<ol data-start="381" data-end="627">
<li data-start="381" data-end="509">
<p data-start="384" data-end="509"><strong data-start="384" data-end="404">Pathway buckets:</strong> “If I’m grouping ICU cases into ~4–5 buckets for analysis, what buckets make the most clinical sense?”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="510" data-end="627">
<p data-start="513" data-end="627"><strong data-start="513" data-end="537">QI framing language:</strong> “What’s the least inflammatory / most accurate way to describe X without blaming a unit?”</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="629" data-end="682">That’s it. No “can you review my whole project” trap.</p>
<h2 data-start="684" data-end="742">The buckets that usually work (so you show up prepared)</h2>
<p data-start="743" data-end="778">Show them a starting proposal like:</p>
<ul data-start="780" data-end="961">
<li data-start="780" data-end="803">
<p data-start="782" data-end="803"><strong data-start="782" data-end="803">Trauma / surgical</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="804" data-end="848">
<p data-start="806" data-end="848"><strong data-start="806" data-end="817">Cardiac</strong> (STEMI/ACS, shock, arrhythmia)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="849" data-end="894">
<p data-start="851" data-end="894"><strong data-start="851" data-end="860">Neuro</strong> (stroke, ICH, status epilepticus)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="895" data-end="941">
<p data-start="897" data-end="941"><strong data-start="897" data-end="941">Sepsis / infection / respiratory failure</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="942" data-end="961">
<p data-start="944" data-end="961"><strong data-start="944" data-end="961">Other / mixed</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="963" data-end="1031">They’ll correct you in 2 minutes (and that correction is the value).</p>

<p data-start="104" data-end="132"><strong data-start="104" data-end="132"><code data-start="106" data-end="130">docs/notes_module01.md</code></strong></p>

<p data-start="250" data-end="389">Below is a <strong data-start="261" data-end="279">ready-to-paste</strong> <code data-start="280" data-end="299">notes_module01.md</code> that captures Module 1 <em data-start="323" data-end="328">and</em> locks in your early project decisions without boxing you in.</p>
<hr data-start="391" data-end="394">
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="396" data-end="7284"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">markdown</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Module 1 Notes — Course + CRISP-DM + Project Selection</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; Goal of this file: capture key takeaways from Module 1, record early decisions, and keep a running list of next actions/questions.</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; This is not polished writing — it’s working notes.</span></span><span>

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 1) Course structure in one page</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Major deliverables (CRISP-DM aligned)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 1 (Module 5): Business + Data Understanding Report**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> problem framing, stakeholders, success criteria, EDA, data quality, limitations
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 2 (Module 9): Data Preparation + Modeling Report**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> cleaning, feature engineering, model comparison, evaluation (technical)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Assignment 3 (Module 13): Final Report + 3-slide exec deck**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> evaluation in business terms, deployment feasibility, risks, recommendations, reflection

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### “Show your work”</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Repo submitted pass/fail
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Needs clear structure + README + evidence that analysis supports the report

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 2) CRISP-DM refresher (what matters / what I care about)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### The six phases</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> Business Understanding
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> Data Understanding
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> Data Preparation
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> Modeling
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">5.</span></span><span> Evaluation
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">6.</span></span><span> Deployment

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Key point:**</span></span><span> iterative/cyclical, not linear. Expect to go backward.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Hierarchical structure (why it’s useful)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Phases**</span></span><span> → </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Generic Tasks**</span></span><span> → </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Specialized Tasks**</span></span><span> → </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Process Instances**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Translation: the framework is stable, but my project implementation is a “process instance” with documented decisions.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Why standardizing matters (practical)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Prevents skipping ahead to modeling without a real business question
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Creates shared vocabulary for stakeholders
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Captures lessons learned so future work is faster/cleaner

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 3) Real-world reflection (analyst influence + politics)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Observation</span></span><span>
In practice, analytics often becomes “shadow leadership”:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Stakeholders ask for “data,” but </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*the analyst controls framing*</span></span><span>:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what options get presented
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what metrics get defined
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what caveats get emphasized
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what language gets used (which can trigger politics)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Personal rule of thumb</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Always present options, but be transparent about:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what I recommend and </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*why*</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> risks/perverse incentives
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> what I’m intentionally not recommending and why (briefly)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Wording matters</span></span><span>
Executives often half-listen and go by gut.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Avoid blame language.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Prefer “signal framing”:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> e.g., “canary in the coal mine” vs “delays start in the waiting room”
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> State what the metric </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*can*</span></span><span> support vs what it cannot.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 4) Project selection decision</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Selected CONTEXT+DATASET</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Patient Care Analysis (MIMIC-IV demo)**</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Why this dataset</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Strong alignment with my day job: healthcare ops + quality improvement
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Clinical complexity is real (multiple linked tables, irregular measurements, missingness)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> But it’s better documented than typical real-world hospital data → less “data archaeology,” more analysis/learning

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Stakeholders</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> ICU Medical Director (clinical protocol relevance, implementable insights)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Hospital Administration (utilization, quality metrics, operational impact)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Success criteria (operational interpretation)</span></span><span>
The course success criteria is broad; I will define “success” as:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Clear, defensible cohort + endpoint definitions
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Sound methodology + honest limitations
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Practical QI-oriented insights
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Deliverables that read like a professional healthcare analytics report

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 5) Data inventory (initial)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Core spine tables</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> patients
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> admissions
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> icustays
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> transfers

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Clinical “event” tables (available in the demo extract I downloaded)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> labevents + d<span class="hljs-emphasis">_labitems
- chartevents + d_</span>items
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> inputevents
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> procedureevents
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> diagnoses</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">_icd + d_</span></span><span>icd<span class="hljs-emphasis">_diagnoses

### Important constraint (throughput / demand curves)
- Because MIMIC uses date shifting for de-identification, system-wide concurrency by clock-time (true “how many active cases at time t across the hospital”) is not trustworthy.
- What *is* trustworthy: within-encounter intervals/durations (LOS, time-to-intervention, time between transitions), and within-patient longitudinal sequences.

---

## 6) Current analysis direction (not locked in)

### Why I’m not married to any single method yet
KM/survival analysis popped into my head because it’s QI-friendly, but I’m keeping options open until EDA confirms what’s feasible.

### Candidate “baskets” (keep multiple viable paths)
</span></span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Basket A — Utilization / “recidivism”**</span></span><span>
- Hospital readmission: time from discharge → next admission (7/30/90 day windows)
- ICU readmission/bounceback where feasible

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Basket B — Flow / process metrics (QI-throughput-adjacent)**</span></span><span>
- Admission → ICU time
- ED timestamps (if present) → ICU time
- ICU transitions and “bounceback” patterns using transfers + icustays

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Basket C — ICU course severity / intensity**</span></span><span>
- First 24h labs/vitals → prolonged ICU LOS, mortality, or other outcomes
- Interventions as signals (vasopressors, ventilation/procedures, etc.)

### Unit of analysis options
- ICU stay-level (stay_id)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Admission-level (hadm<span class="hljs-emphasis">_id)
- Patient-level (subject_</span>id) for longitudinal utilization (may be sparse)

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 7) Early cohort/phenotype caution (ICU ≠ one thing)</span></span><span>
ICU stays need segmentation:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Trauma vs stroke vs STEMI vs sepsis/resp failure are different pathways.
Plan: create a simple “pathway<span class="hljs-emphasis">_group” using diagnoses + interventions later.
For now: postpone until EDA confirms sample sizes for each group.

---

## 8) Repo + workflow decisions (Module 1)

### Repo goals
- Keep it reproducible and portfolio-friendly
- Keep data out of Git (large files), document how to obtain locally
- Commit early and often (scaffold + notes counts as progress)

### Planned structure (current)
- `README.md`
- `docs/`
  - `notes_</span>module01.md` (this file)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Questions to answer early</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> readmission?

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Entry 1 — Module 1 (Project Foundation + Data Discovery)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### What I completed</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Reviewed course structure, grading, and the three major assignments aligned to CRISP-DM.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Reviewed CRISP-DM phases and the “hierarchical structure” concept (phases → tasks → specialized tasks → process instance).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Chose a project option: </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Patient Care Analysis (MIMIC-IV demo)**</span></span><span>.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Set up (or planned) repository structure to support “show your work” requirements.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Skimmed dataset documentation and confirmed key tables needed for analysis:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> patients, admissions, icustays, transfers
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> labevents + d</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">_labitems, chartevents + d_</span></span><span>items
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> diagnoses</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">_icd + d_</span></span><span>icd<span class="hljs-emphasis">_diagnoses
  - inputevents, procedureevents

### Key takeaways
- CRISP-DM is iterative: it’s normal to move backward when data quality issues or new questions appear.
- Documentation is not extra — it’s a deliverable that supports alignment and reproducibility.
- In real-world analytics, wording and metric selection can drive politics and incentives; accuracy and framing matter.
- MIMIC’s deidentification (date shifting) preserves </span></span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**durations/intervals**</span></span><span> within a patient encounter but limits “true calendar time” analyses (e.g., real demand curves across patients).

### Decisions made
- </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Project selection:**</span></span><span> MIMIC-IV ICU Patient Care Analysis.
- </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Initial framing:**</span></span><span> lean toward a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**QI-style**</span></span><span> narrative (operational + clinical relevance).
- </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Keep options open:**</span></span><span> not committing yet to Kaplan–Meier or any single method until EDA confirms feasibility.
- </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Repository choice:**</span></span><span> keep raw data out of Git; document how to obtain data locally; commit scaffold + notes early.

### Open questions
- What is the best </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**unit of analysis**</span></span><span> given sample size and table structure?
  - ICU stay-level (stay_id) vs admission-level (hadm</span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">_id) vs patient-level (subject_</span></span><span>id)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Which </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**primary outcome(s)**</span></span><span> are strongest for a capstone-grade story with this dataset?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICU LOS, in-hospital mortality, ICU bounceback, hospital readmission
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> How complete are ED timestamps (edregtime/edouttime) for flow metrics?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> What is a defensible “early window” for feature extraction (6h vs 24h) without leakage?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> How should ICU stays be grouped into high-level pathways (cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/etc.) without over-segmenting?

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### Next steps</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Do a lightweight EDA pass focused on feasibility:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> counts per key entity (patients/admissions/stays)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> missingness and timestamp availability
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> distribution checks for LOS and outcome flags
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Draft a short “analysis plan” for Assignment 1:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> stakeholder questions → measurable objectives → candidate outcomes → candidate predictors
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Create a first-pass mapping approach for ICU pathway grouping (diagnoses-based, upgraded later with interventions).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Commit repo scaffold + Module 1 notes + Process Diary entry 1.
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>

<h2 data-start="129" data-end="161">1) Create the files + folders</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="162" data-end="433"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span><span class="hljs-comment"># from repo root</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">mkdir</span></span><span> -p docs/process_diary data/raw data/processed notebooks src results/figures

</span><span><span class="hljs-comment"># create docs files</span></span><span>
nano docs/notes_module01.md
nano docs/process_diary/entry_01_module_01.md

</span><span><span class="hljs-comment"># (optional but recommended)</span></span><span>
nano .gitignore
nano data/README.md
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="435" data-end="600"><strong data-start="435" data-end="462">Put your Module 1 notes</strong> in <code data-start="466" data-end="490">docs/notes_module01.md</code> (the long one I gave you).<br data-start="517" data-end="520">
<strong data-start="520" data-end="553">Put the Process Diary Entry 1</strong> in <code data-start="557" data-end="599">docs/process_diary/entry_01_module_01.md</code>.</p>
<p data-start="602" data-end="639">For <code data-start="606" data-end="622">data/README.md</code>, keep it simple:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="640" data-end="834"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">md</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-md"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Data</span></span><span>

Raw data is not committed to this repository.

Place the MIMIC-IV demo CSV files in:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> data/raw/

Derived datasets created during analysis will be written to:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> data/processed/
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<h2 data-start="836" data-end="873">2) .gitignore (copy/paste starter)</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="874" data-end="1129"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">gitignore</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-gitignore"><span># Python
.venv/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.ipynb_checkpoints/

# OS / editor
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
.vscode/
.idea/

# Data (keep raw out of git)
data/raw/
data/processed/

# Results (optional: keep figures if you want; otherwise ignore)
# results/
</span></code></div></div></pre>
<blockquote data-start="1131" data-end="1217">
<p data-start="1133" data-end="1217">If you want your plots to show in GitHub later, <strong data-start="1181" data-end="1216">don’t ignore <code data-start="1196" data-end="1214">results/figures/</code></strong>.</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 data-start="1219" data-end="1279">3) Confirm you’re not about to commit the huge data files</h2>

</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1303" data-end="1391">You should <strong data-start="1314" data-end="1321">NOT</strong> see <code data-start="1326" data-end="1341">labevents.csv</code>, <code data-start="1343" data-end="1360">chartevents.csv</code>, etc. If you do, stop and run:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1392" data-end="1413"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git reset
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1414" data-end="1472">Then make sure the <code data-start="1433" data-end="1445">.gitignore</code> is saved, and check again.</p>

<h2 data-start="330" data-end="369">1) Confirm the commit exists locally</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="370" data-end="413"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">log</span></span><span> --oneline --decorate -5
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="414" data-end="483">You should see your commit message (or something close) in that list.</p>
<h2 data-start="485" data-end="537">2) Confirm what files are actually tracked by git</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="538" data-end="573"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git ls-files | </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">head</span></span><span> -50
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="574" data-end="601">You should see things like:</p>
<ul data-start="602" data-end="728">
<li data-start="602" data-end="615">
<p data-start="604" data-end="615"><code data-start="604" data-end="615">README.md</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="616" data-end="630">
<p data-start="618" data-end="630"><code data-start="618" data-end="630">.gitignore</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="631" data-end="649">
<p data-start="633" data-end="649"><code data-start="633" data-end="649">pyproject.toml</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="650" data-end="676">
<p data-start="652" data-end="676"><code data-start="652" data-end="676">docs/notes_module01.md</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="677" data-end="721">
<p data-start="679" data-end="721"><code data-start="679" data-end="721">docs/process_diary/entry_01_module_01.md</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="722" data-end="728">
<p data-start="724" data-end="728">etc.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-start="730" data-end="766">3) Confirm your remote is correct</h2>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="767" data-end="792"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git remote -v
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<h2 data-start="794" data-end="844">4) Optional: confirm GitHub has the same commit</h2>
<p data-start="845" data-end="876">This is the “trust but verify”:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="877" data-end="921"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git </span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">log</span></span><span> --oneline origin/main -5
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="922" data-end="953">It should match your local log.</p>
<hr data-start="955" data-end="958">
<h3 data-start="960" data-end="1028">If <code data-start="967" data-end="976">git log</code> shows commits but you don’t see the files on GitHub</h3>
<p data-start="1029" data-end="1096">That usually means you’re looking at the wrong repo or branch. Run:</p>
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="1097" data-end="1133"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">bash</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-bash"><span><span>git branch
git remote -v
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="1134" data-end="1199">and make sure you’re viewing <strong data-start="1163" data-end="1171">main</strong> on the correct GitHub repo.</p>
<hr data-start="1201" data-end="1204">
<h3 data-start="1206" data-end="1277">One more quick check: do you maybe have files, but they’re ignored?</h3>

## Course map (CRISP-DM alignment)
- Unit 1 (M1–M5): Business Understanding + Data Understanding → **Assignment 1**

- Unit 3 (M10–M13): Evaluation + Deployment → **Assignment 3**

## Module checklist (definition of done)
### M1 — Intro + CRISP-DM
- [ ] Repo skeleton created
- [ ] README has run instructions + repo map
- [ ] Environment reproducible (uv or venv)
- [ ] Tracker/diary/decision log created

### M2 — Business Understanding (Part 1)
- [ ] 1-page problem framing bullets (business objective, DS objective)
- [ ] Stakeholders + decision(s) they need to make (even if fictional)
- [ ] Initial success criteria draft (business + technical)
- [ ] Add 3–5 assumptions/risks to docs

### M3 — Business Understanding (Part 2)
- [ ] Constraints + risks refined
- [ ] “Perverse incentives” check (what could be misinterpreted / gamed)
- [ ] Report A1 outline filled to 60%

### M4 — Data Understanding (Part 1)
- [ ] Data inventory (tables/files, row counts, grain, keys)
- [ ] Initial EDA notebook started (missingness + distributions)
- [ ] Data dictionary draft started

### M5 — Data Understanding (Part 2) + **Assignment 1 due**
- [ ] EDA complete enough to support claims
- [ ] Data quality section drafted (issues + impact + mitigations)
- [ ] Assignment 1 report drafted (10–15 pages target)
- [ ] Repo ZIP ready for submission (notebooks run, outputs saved, README updated)

### M6 — Data Prep (Part 1)
- [ ] Cleaning plan drafted (what/why)
- [ ] Train/test split strategy chosen (leakage check)
- [ ] Pipeline notebook/script started

### M7 — Data Prep (Part 2)
- [ ] Feature engineering complete (with rationale)
- [ ] Final processed dataset exported to <code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">data/processed/</code>
- [ ] Prep decisions logged

### M8 — Modeling (Part 1)
- [ ] Baseline model built
- [ ] 2 candidate model families implemented
- [ ] Evaluation framework fixed (metrics + validation)

### M9 — Modeling (Part 2) + **Assignment 2 due**
- [ ] Model comparison completed fairly
- [ ] Best model selected + documented
- [ ] Model artifacts saved (where applicable)
- [ ] Assignment 2 report drafted (10–14 pages target)
- [ ] Repo ZIP ready for submission

### M10 — Evaluation (Part 1)
- [ ] Error analysis + interpretation
- [ ] What model gets wrong + why (limitations)

### M11 — Evaluation (Part 2)
- [ ] Business implications drafted (impact story)
- [ ] Risks/ethics section drafted

### M12 — Deployment (Part 1)
- [ ] Deployment options + feasibility
- [ ] Monitoring plan draft

### M13 — Deployment (Part 2) + **Assignment 3 due**
- [ ] Final report drafted (10–12 pages target)
- [ ] 3-slide executive deck drafted
- [ ] Repo integrated + cleaned for final submission ZIP

### M14 — Wrap-up
- [ ] Final reflection (lessons learned)
- [ ] Portfolio-friendly cleanup (optional)

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="172">Yep — let’s do a fast “Module 2 = Business Understanding (Part 1)” review, <em data-start="75" data-end="111">anchored to your ICU/MIMIC project</em>, then you can roll straight into Module 3 with a clean head.</p>
<h2 data-start="174" data-end="201">Module 2 in one sentence</h2>
<p data-start="202" data-end="391">Module 2 is where you stop being “a person with data” and become “a person with a decision to support,” with explicit <strong data-start="320" data-end="390">objectives, success criteria, constraints, assumptions, and a plan</strong>.</p>
<h2 data-start="393" data-end="441">What Module 2 is really asking you to produce</h2>
<p data-start="442" data-end="505">Think of it as a lightweight <strong data-start="471" data-end="490">Project Charter</strong> (QI-flavored):</p>
<h3 data-start="507" data-end="538">1) Stakeholders → decisions</h3>
<ul data-start="539" data-end="717">
<li data-start="539" data-end="635">
<p data-start="541" data-end="635"><strong data-start="541" data-end="565">ICU Medical Director</strong>: “What should we standardize/change?” (protocol, pathway, monitoring)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="636" data-end="717">
<p data-start="638" data-end="717"><strong data-start="638" data-end="656">Hospital Admin</strong>: “What moves utilization/LOS/cost without harming outcomes?”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="719" data-end="803">Your output should <em data-start="738" data-end="750">explicitly</em> name 1–2 decisions your analysis is meant to inform.</p>
<h3 data-start="805" data-end="876">2) Business objective → data science objective (keep them distinct)</h3>
<ul data-start="877" data-end="1166">
<li data-start="877" data-end="996">
<p data-start="879" data-end="996"><strong data-start="879" data-end="915">Business objective (QI framing):</strong> improve care + resource utilization (LOS, ICU bed utilization, adverse outcomes)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="997" data-end="1166">
<p data-start="999" data-end="1166"><strong data-start="999" data-end="1026">Data science objective:</strong>
 build an analysis/model that quantifies which factors (patient factors +
 early signals + care processes) are associated with the outcome(s)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1168" data-end="1214">3) Success criteria (business + technical)</h3>
<p data-start="1215" data-end="1295">The course gives a broad success definition. In Module 2 you make it measurable:</p>
<p data-start="1297" data-end="1326"><strong data-start="1297" data-end="1326">Business success examples</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1327" data-end="1579">
<li data-start="1327" data-end="1477">
<p data-start="1329" data-end="1477">Identify 2–3 actionable levers that
 plausibly translate into QI interventions (e.g., earlier recognition, 
bundle compliance proxies, triage/routing)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1478" data-end="1579">
<p data-start="1480" data-end="1579">Provide stratification that helps target resources (e.g., “top decile predicted prolonged ICU LOS”)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1581" data-end="1611"><strong data-start="1581" data-end="1611">Technical success examples</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1612" data-end="1819">
<li data-start="1612" data-end="1646">
<p data-start="1614" data-end="1646">Clear cohort/outcome definitions</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1647" data-end="1684">
<p data-start="1649" data-end="1684">No leakage (feature window defined)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1685" data-end="1751">
<p data-start="1687" data-end="1751">Baseline + improved model performance (even modest, given N=100)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1752" data-end="1819">
<p data-start="1754" data-end="1819">Calibration / interpretability suitable for clinical stakeholders</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1821" data-end="1878">4) Assess situation (constraints, assumptions, risks)</h3>
<p data-start="1879" data-end="1928">This is the “don’t get blindsided later” section.</p>
<p data-start="1930" data-end="1968"><strong data-start="1930" data-end="1968">Constraints (MIMIC demo realities)</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1969" data-end="2149">
<li data-start="1969" data-end="2020">
<p data-start="1971" data-end="2020">Small N (100 patients) → limited model complexity</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2021" data-end="2102">
<p data-start="2023" data-end="2102">De-ID date shifting → intervals OK; real-world concurrency/demand curves not OK</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2103" data-end="2149">
<p data-start="2105" data-end="2149">Missingness + irregular sampling is inherent</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2151" data-end="2196"><strong data-start="2151" data-end="2196">Assumptions (you should write these down)</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2197" data-end="2378">
<li data-start="2197" data-end="2262">
<p data-start="2199" data-end="2262">Outcomes/labels in the dataset are reliable enough for analysis</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2263" data-end="2315">
<p data-start="2265" data-end="2315">First X hours contain meaningful predictive signal</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2316" data-end="2378">
<p data-start="2318" data-end="2378">Diagnostic coding is good enough for coarse pathway grouping</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2380" data-end="2389"><strong data-start="2380" data-end="2389">Risks</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2390" data-end="2548">
<li data-start="2390" data-end="2424">
<p data-start="2392" data-end="2424">Overfitting / unstable estimates</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2425" data-end="2478">
<p data-start="2427" data-end="2478">Clinical heterogeneity (trauma vs neuro vs cardiac)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2479" data-end="2548">
<p data-start="2481" data-end="2548">“QI story” could be misconstrued as blame if phrasing isn’t careful</p>
</li>
</ul>

<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="2783" data-end="5093"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">md</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-md"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Module 2 — Business Understanding (Part 1)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Role + stakeholders</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Role: healthcare data analyst supporting QI
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Primary stakeholders:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICU Medical Director (protocol + clinical relevance)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Hospital Administration (utilization, quality metrics)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Business objective (QI framing)</span></span><span>
Identify actionable factors associated with ICU outcomes and resource utilization to inform quality improvement initiatives and operational planning.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Decisions this work should inform</span></span><span>
1) Which patient subgroups should be prioritized for targeted QI interventions/resources?
2) Which early clinical signals/care process markers are associated with prolonged ICU LOS or worse outcomes?

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Data science objective</span></span><span>
Using MIMIC-IV demo, build an interpretable analysis/model that uses early-encounter features to estimate risk of a selected outcome (e.g., prolonged ICU LOS and/or in-hospital mortality), and translate findings into practical recommendations.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Candidate outcomes (not final)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Primary (pick 1): prolonged ICU LOS (e.g., &gt;75th percentile) OR in-hospital mortality
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Secondary: ICU LOS as continuous, discharge disposition, ICU readmission/bounceback (if feasible)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Candidate unit of analysis</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> ICU stay-level (stay<span class="hljs-emphasis">_id) preferred for “ICU course” questions
- Admission-level (hadm_</span>id) for “hospital course” questions
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Patient-level (subject<span class="hljs-emphasis">_id) only if longitudinal signal exists (likely sparse in demo)

## Success criteria
- Business: 2–3 actionable insights + clear limitations + QI-safe framing
- Technical: reproducible pipeline, no leakage (feature window defined), baseline vs final model comparison, interpretable outputs

## Constraints
- N=100 demo sample limits statistical power/model complexity
- Deidentified date shifting limits calendar-time throughput analysis across patients
- Missingness/irregular sampling is expected

## Assumptions
- Feature window: first 6–24h captures clinically meaningful signals
- Diagnoses/interventions can support coarse pathway grouping
- Outputs will be interpreted as association, not causation

## Risks + mitigations
- Overfitting → simple models + cross-validation + regularization
- Heterogeneity → pathway grouping + sensitivity checks
- Misinterpretation/blame → careful language + “canary” framing + stakeholder-oriented summaries
</span></span></span></code></div></div></pre>
