<p data-start="804" data-end="981">Yeah — the “good starting point” we kicked around was <strong data-start="858" data-end="898">broad pathway / service-line cohorts</strong> (big buckets you can actually support with <em data-start="942" data-end="949">N=100</em>), not super-granular diagnoses.</p>
<h3 data-start="983" data-end="1022">Starter cohort set (ICU-stay level)</h3>
<p data-start="1023" data-end="1124">If you want something that maps cleanly to QI conversations and doesn’t explode into tiny cell sizes:</p>
<ol data-start="1126" data-end="1783">
<li data-start="1126" data-end="1223">
<p data-start="1129" data-end="1223"><strong data-start="1129" data-end="1150">Cardiac / CCU-ish</strong><br data-start="1150" data-end="1153">
ACS/STEMI, cardiogenic shock, malignant arrhythmia, acute HF decomp</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1224" data-end="1328">
<p data-start="1227" data-end="1328"><strong data-start="1227" data-end="1252">Neuro / Neuro-ICU-ish</strong><br data-start="1252" data-end="1255">
ischemic stroke, ICH/SAH, status epilepticus, neurocritical monitoring</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1329" data-end="1430">
<p data-start="1332" data-end="1430"><strong data-start="1332" data-end="1363">Trauma / Surgical / Post-op</strong><br data-start="1363" data-end="1366">
MVA/trauma, post-op monitoring, surgical complications/bleeds</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1431" data-end="1576">
<p data-start="1434" data-end="1576"><strong data-start="1434" data-end="1488">Sepsis / Shock / Infection-driven critical illness</strong><br data-start="1488" data-end="1491">
sepsis, septic shock, bacteremia, severe infection with pressors/organ dysfunction</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1577" data-end="1680">
<p data-start="1580" data-end="1680"><strong data-start="1580" data-end="1603">Respiratory failure</strong><br data-start="1603" data-end="1606">
ARDS, severe pneumonia, COPD exacerbation needing vent/BiPAP escalation</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1681" data-end="1783">
<p data-start="1684" data-end="1783"><strong data-start="1684" data-end="1709">Other / Mixed medical</strong><br data-start="1709" data-end="1712">
DKA/metabolic, renal, GI bleed/liver failure, tox, “everything else”</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="1785" data-end="1836">That’s usually the sweet spot: <strong data-start="1816" data-end="1831">5–7 cohorts</strong> max.</p>
<hr data-start="1838" data-end="1841">
<h3 data-start="1843" data-end="1895">How to assign cohorts in MIMIC (pragmatic order)</h3>
<p data-start="1896" data-end="2150"><strong data-start="1896" data-end="1929">Best “cheap proxy” (fastest):</strong> use the ICU unit itself<br data-start="1953" data-end="1956">
From <code data-start="1961" data-end="1971">icustays</code>, you’ll usually have <code data-start="1993" data-end="2009">first_careunit</code> / <code data-start="2012" data-end="2027">last_careunit</code> (e.g., MICU/SICU/CCU/TSICU/NICU). This is a great <em data-start="2078" data-end="2090">first-pass</em> stratifier and often aligns with the pathway buckets above.</p>
<p data-start="2152" data-end="2382"><strong data-start="2152" data-end="2194">More clinically “true” (still doable):</strong> diagnosis-driven grouping<br data-start="2220" data-end="2223">
Use <code data-start="2227" data-end="2242">diagnoses_icd</code> (by <code data-start="2247" data-end="2256">hadm_id</code>) + <code data-start="2260" data-end="2288">d_icd_diagnoses.long_title</code> to map ICD codes/titles into those buckets (regex/keyword mapping works fine for a capstone).</p>
<p data-start="2384" data-end="2514"><strong data-start="2384" data-end="2414">Even better (QI-flavored):</strong> primary cohort + severity flags<br data-start="2446" data-end="2449">
Make <strong data-start="2454" data-end="2476">one primary cohort</strong> per ICU stay <em data-start="2490" data-end="2496">plus</em> 2–3 binary flags:</p>
<ul data-start="2515" data-end="2679">
<li data-start="2515" data-end="2591">
<p data-start="2517" data-end="2591"><code data-start="2517" data-end="2535">ventilated_early</code> (from vent-related items in <code data-start="2564" data-end="2577">chartevents</code> / procedures)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2592" data-end="2640">
<p data-start="2594" data-end="2640"><code data-start="2594" data-end="2613">vasopressor_early</code> (from <code data-start="2620" data-end="2633">inputevents</code> items)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2641" data-end="2679">
<p data-start="2643" data-end="2679"><code data-start="2643" data-end="2653">dialysis</code> / <code data-start="2656" data-end="2661">RRT</code> flag (if present)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2681" data-end="2762">This gives you case-mix control without turning your project into a taxonomy war.</p>
<hr data-start="2764" data-end="2767">
<h3 data-start="2769" data-end="2828">A sane “tie-break” rule (so every stay lands somewhere)</h3>
<p data-start="2829" data-end="2983">If a stay could fit multiple buckets, pick <strong data-start="2872" data-end="2879">one</strong> using a priority order like:<br>
<strong data-start="2909" data-end="2983">Trauma/Surgical → Neuro → Cardiac → Sepsis/Shock → Respiratory → Other</strong></p>
<p data-start="2985" data-end="3086">(Reason: those top pathways usually dominate resource pattern + LOS, and it keeps categories stable.)</p>
<hr data-start="3088" data-end="3091">
<p data-start="3093" data-end="3365">If you want, next time we open the data we can do a quick count of ICU stays by <code data-start="3173" data-end="3189">first_careunit</code>
 + top ICD titles per admission to see whether your demo sample actually
 supports all 6 buckets or whether we should collapse to 4 (e.g., merge 
Resp into Sepsis/Medical, etc.).</p>

<h2 data-start="229" data-end="265">Open questions (still unresolved)</h2>
<h3 data-start="267" data-end="298">1) Grain / unit of analysis</h3>
<ul data-start="299" data-end="549">
<li data-start="299" data-end="412">
<p data-start="301" data-end="412">Are we modeling at <strong data-start="320" data-end="332">ICU stay</strong> (<code data-start="334" data-end="343">stay_id</code>), <strong data-start="346" data-end="368">hospital admission</strong> (<code data-start="370" data-end="379">hadm_id</code>), or <strong data-start="385" data-end="396">patient</strong> (<code data-start="398" data-end="410">subject_id</code>)?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="413" data-end="549">
<p data-start="415" data-end="549">How many patients have <strong data-start="438" data-end="460">multiple ICU stays</strong> or <strong data-start="464" data-end="487">multiple admissions</strong> (i.e., how much “recidivism” even exists in the demo subset)?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="551" data-end="614">2) Outcome selection (what are we predicting / explaining?)</h3>
<ul data-start="615" data-end="952">
<li data-start="615" data-end="885">
<p data-start="617" data-end="677">What outcomes are feasible with <em data-start="649" data-end="655">this</em> data and sample size?</p>
<ul data-start="680" data-end="885">
<li data-start="680" data-end="705">
<p data-start="682" data-end="705">ICU LOS vs hospital LOS</p>
</li>
<li data-start="708" data-end="753">
<p data-start="710" data-end="753">In-hospital mortality (if present, counts?)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="756" data-end="830">
<p data-start="758" data-end="830">ICU transfer patterns / stepdown / bounceback (if the tables support it)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="833" data-end="885">
<p data-start="835" data-end="885">Readmission/return visits (likely limited in demo)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="886" data-end="952">
<p data-start="888" data-end="952">Which outcome tells the best <strong data-start="917" data-end="929">QI story</strong> without over-claiming?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="954" data-end="1005">3) Cohort definition (your “ICU pathways” idea)</h3>
<ul data-start="1006" data-end="1363">
<li data-start="1006" data-end="1251">
<p data-start="1008" data-end="1085">What’s the most defensible cohort grouping approach <em data-start="1060" data-end="1084">given what’s available</em>?</p>
<ul data-start="1088" data-end="1251">
<li data-start="1088" data-end="1140">
<p data-start="1090" data-end="1140">ICD titles only (diagnoses_icd + d_icd_diagnoses)?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1143" data-end="1199">
<p data-start="1145" data-end="1199">Care unit / first careunit / last careunit (icustays)?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1202" data-end="1251">
<p data-start="1204" data-end="1251">Hybrid (ICD + procedureevents + key meds/labs)?</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1252" data-end="1363">
<p data-start="1254" data-end="1363">Do we have enough N to keep cohorts separate (cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/etc.), or do we need fewer buckets?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1365" data-end="1401">4) Time window / leakage control</h3>
<ul data-start="1402" data-end="1611">
<li data-start="1402" data-end="1531">
<p data-start="1404" data-end="1493">What is the “early window” for predictors so you’re not cheating with future information?</p>
<ul data-start="1496" data-end="1531">
<li data-start="1496" data-end="1531">
<p data-start="1498" data-end="1531">First 6h / 12h / 24h of ICU stay?</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1532" data-end="1611">
<p data-start="1534" data-end="1611">Are chart/lab timestamps dense enough to support an early-window feature set?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1613" data-end="1665">5) Data completeness &amp; missingness reality check</h3>
<ul data-start="1666" data-end="1866">
<li data-start="1666" data-end="1771">
<p data-start="1668" data-end="1771">How sparse are <strong data-start="1683" data-end="1698">chartevents</strong>, <strong data-start="1700" data-end="1713">labevents</strong>, <strong data-start="1715" data-end="1730">inputevents</strong>, <strong data-start="1732" data-end="1751">procedureevents</strong> in the demo subset?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1772" data-end="1866">
<p data-start="1774" data-end="1866">Are key variables missing systematically (e.g., sicker patients measured more often → bias)?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1868" data-end="1937">6) Practical “QI-style” framing that matches the success criteria</h3>
<ul data-start="1938" data-end="2228">
<li data-start="1938" data-end="2101">
<p data-start="1940" data-end="2010">What exactly is the “decision” your stakeholders would make from this?</p>
<ul data-start="2013" data-end="2101">
<li data-start="2013" data-end="2035">
<p data-start="2015" data-end="2035">Protocol refinement?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2038" data-end="2060">
<p data-start="2040" data-end="2060">Resource allocation?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2063" data-end="2101">
<p data-start="2065" data-end="2101">Risk stratification / early warning?</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2102" data-end="2228">
<p data-start="2104" data-end="2228">What’s your success criteria in <em data-start="2136" data-end="2152">measurable-ish</em> terms for a class project (since you can’t measure real deployment impact)?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="2230" data-end="2281">7) Tooling / workflow (smaller, but still open)</h3>
<ul data-start="2282" data-end="2521">
<li data-start="2282" data-end="2433">
<p data-start="2284" data-end="2433">Do you want to load into <strong data-start="2309" data-end="2321">Postgres</strong> now for repeatable SQL-driven EDA, or stay Python-first with pandas until the first inventory notebook is done?</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2434" data-end="2521">
<p data-start="2436" data-end="2521">If Postgres: do you want a lightweight schema + a db diagram / ERD to document joins?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2523" data-end="2683">If you want the “ready to paste” version for your <strong data-start="2573" data-end="2597">00_master_tracker.md</strong> under “Open questions,” tell me and I’ll format it exactly like your checklist style.</p>

<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="128" data-end="2200"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">md</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-md"><span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Notes / parking lot</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Open questions:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> What is the best unit of analysis for this dataset?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> ICU stay-level (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span>) vs admission-level (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`hadm_id`</span></span><span>) vs patient-level (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`subject_id`</span></span><span>)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> How many patients have multiple ICU stays or multiple admissions (i.e., is “recidivism” even measurable in the demo subset)?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Which primary outcome(s) are feasible and tell a defensible QI-style story with N≈100?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> ICU LOS vs hospital LOS
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> In-hospital mortality (is event count sufficient?)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> ICU transfer patterns / stepdown / ICU bounceback (if supported)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> Readmission/return visits (likely limited — confirm)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Cohort strategy: what’s the most defensible way to group ICU stays into high-level pathways without over-segmenting?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> ICD-based cohorts (cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/other) vs care-unit-based vs hybrid (ICD + procedures + meds/labs)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> Do we have enough cases per cohort to model separately, or do we need fewer buckets?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> What is a defensible “early window” for feature extraction that avoids leakage?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> 6h vs 12h vs 24h from ICU admit (confirm timestamp density supports this)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Data completeness check:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> How sparse are </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`chartevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`labevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`inputevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`procedureevents`</span></span><span> in the demo subset?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> Is missingness systematic (sicker patients measured more often → bias)?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Stakeholder decision clarity:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> What exact decision(s) should this analysis inform (protocol changes, resource allocation, early risk flagging, etc.)?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> What “success” looks like in measurable-ish terms for a class project (since real deployment impact isn’t measurable here)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Workflow/tooling:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> Load into Postgres now for repeatable SQL EDA vs stay Python/pandas-first until inventory is done
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> If Postgres: do we need a lightweight ERD/db diagram to document joins and grains?
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Things to look up later:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICD10 codes for specific ICU cohorts (Cardiac, Neuro, Trauma, Sepsis, Other)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">    -</span></span><span> Verify with Dr. Gibney (UCI Health) whether this cohort mental model is “good enough” for a capstone framing
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="2202" data-end="2418">If you want, I can also give you a <strong data-start="2237" data-end="2273">1–2 sentence “Current objective”</strong>
 for the top of the tracker that matches these open questions (something
 like “finish feasibility EDA + lock grain/outcomes + draft BU 
bullets”).</p>

## Module checklist (definition of done)

- [ ] Add 3–5 assumptions/risks to docs

### M3 — Business Understanding (Part 2)
- [ ] Constraints + risks refined
- [ ] “Perverse incentives” check (what could be misinterpreted / gamed)
- [ ] Report A1 outline filled to 60%

### M4 — Data Understanding (Part 1)
- [ ] Data inventory (tables/files, row counts, grain, keys)
- [ ] Initial EDA notebook started (missingness + distributions)
- [ ] Data dictionary draft started

### M5 — Data Understanding (Part 2) + **Assignment 1 due**
- [ ] EDA complete enough to support claims
- [ ] Data quality section drafted (issues + impact + mitigations)
- [ ] Assignment 1 report drafted (10–15 pages target)
- [ ] Repo ZIP ready for submission (notebooks run, outputs saved, README updated)

### M6 — Data Prep (Part 1)
- [ ] Cleaning plan drafted (what/why)
- [ ] Train/test split strategy chosen (leakage check)

### M10 — Evaluation (Part 1)
- [ ] Error analysis + interpretation

### M11 — Evaluation (Part 2)

- [ ] Risks/ethics section drafted

### M12 — Deployment (Part 1)

## Notes / parking lot
- Open questions:
  - What is the best unit of analysis for this dataset?
    - ICU stay-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">stay_id</code>) vs admission-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">hadm_id</code>) vs patient-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">subject_id</code>)
    - How many patients have multiple ICU stays or multiple admissions (i.e., is “recidivism” even measurable in the demo subset)?
  - Which primary outcome(s) are feasible and tell a defensible QI-style story with N≈100?
    - ICU LOS vs hospital LOS
    - In-hospital mortality (is event count sufficient?)
    - ICU transfer patterns / stepdown / ICU bounceback (if supported)
    - Readmission/return visits (likely limited — confirm)
  - Cohort strategy: what’s the most defensible way to group ICU stays into high-level pathways without over-segmenting?
    - ICD-based cohorts (cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/other) vs care-unit-based vs hybrid (ICD + procedures + meds/labs)
    - Do we have enough cases per cohort to model separately, or do we need fewer buckets?
  - What is a defensible “early window” for feature extraction that avoids leakage?
    - 6h vs 12h vs 24h from ICU admit (confirm timestamp density supports this)
  - Data completeness check:
    - How sparse are <code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">chartevents</code>, <code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">labevents</code>, <code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">inputevents</code>, <code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">procedureevents</code> in the demo subset?
    - Is missingness systematic (sicker patients measured more often → bias)?
  - Stakeholder decision clarity:
    - What exact decision(s) should this analysis inform (protocol changes, resource allocation, early risk flagging, etc.)?
    - What “success” looks like in measurable-ish terms for a class project (since real deployment impact isn’t measurable here)
  - Workflow/tooling:
    - Load into Postgres now for repeatable SQL EDA vs stay Python/pandas-first until inventory is done
    - If Postgres: do we need a lightweight ERD/db diagram to document joins and grains?
- Things to look up later:
  - ICD10 codes for specific ICU cohorts (Cardiac, Neuro, Trauma, Sepsis, Other)
    - Verify with Dr. Gibney (UCI Health) whether this cohort mental model is “good enough” for a capstone framing

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="161">Yep — your tracker is <strong data-start="22" data-end="31">close</strong>, but a few parts are <strong data-start="53" data-end="101">out of sync with what you actually completed</strong> (and you can tighten it now that we’ve peeked at the data).</p>
<h2 data-start="163" data-end="180">What’s correct</h2>
<ul data-start="181" data-end="497">
<li data-start="181" data-end="270">
<p data-start="183" data-end="270"><strong data-start="183" data-end="206">Current module = M3</strong> ✅ (matches your screenshot: Module 3 has first two items done).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="271" data-end="381">
<p data-start="273" data-end="381"><strong data-start="273" data-end="296">Risk level = Medium</strong> ✅ (small cohort + healthcare data leakage risk + “demo subset” quirks still matter).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="382" data-end="497">
<p data-start="384" data-end="497">The “open questions” list is directionally right — but a couple are no longer “unknown” after a quick data check.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 data-start="499" data-end="521">What I would change</h2>
<h3 data-start="522" data-end="579">1) Fix the “Next 3 actions” (they’re slightly M2-ish)</h3>
<p data-start="580" data-end="601">Right now you’ve got:</p>
<ol data-start="602" data-end="681">
<li data-start="602" data-end="635">
<p data-start="605" data-end="635">write <code data-start="611" data-end="635">docs/notes_module02.md</code></p>
</li>
<li data-start="636" data-end="656">
<p data-start="639" data-end="656">assumptions/risks</p>
</li>
<li data-start="657" data-end="681">
<p data-start="660" data-end="681">start M3 deliverables</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="683" data-end="731">But you’re <strong data-start="694" data-end="711">already in M3</strong>, so I’d reframe as:</p>
<ul data-start="732" data-end="970">
<li data-start="732" data-end="808">
<p data-start="734" data-end="808"><strong data-start="734" data-end="760">Catch-up (if missing):</strong> <code data-start="761" data-end="785">docs/notes_module02.md</code> (1 short page is fine)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="809" data-end="970">
<p data-start="811" data-end="970"><strong data-start="811" data-end="825">Main work:</strong>
 write the M3 sections that will go straight into Assignment 1 
(Background, objectives, success criteria, responsibility, DS goals, 
project plan)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="972" data-end="1016">2) Your M2 checklist looks overly “done”</h3>
<p data-start="1017" data-end="1028">You marked:</p>
<ul data-start="1029" data-end="1102">
<li data-start="1029" data-end="1102">
<p data-start="1031" data-end="1102"><code data-start="1031" data-end="1102">[x] 1-page problem framing bullets (business objective, DS objective)</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1104" data-end="1261">But based on what you pasted earlier, you’ve got <strong data-start="1153" data-end="1207">process diary + project selection + table scouting</strong>… not necessarily a clean “one-pager” yet. I’d either:</p>
<ul data-start="1262" data-end="1393">
<li data-start="1262" data-end="1299">
<p data-start="1264" data-end="1299">mark that as <strong data-start="1277" data-end="1284">[ ]</strong> (not done), or</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1300" data-end="1393">
<p data-start="1302" data-end="1393">rename it to what you actually did: <strong data-start="1338" data-end="1392">“Project selection + initial framing draft exists”</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="1395" data-end="1460">3) Update open questions with what we now know from your CSVs</h3>
<p data-start="1461" data-end="1584">From the files you uploaded (patients/admissions/icustays/transfers + events tables), here’s what’s <strong data-start="1561" data-end="1583">already answerable</strong>:</p>
<p data-start="1586" data-end="1602"><strong data-start="1586" data-end="1602">Grain / size</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1603" data-end="1704">
<li data-start="1603" data-end="1637">
<p data-start="1605" data-end="1637">Patients (<code data-start="1615" data-end="1627">subject_id</code>): <strong data-start="1630" data-end="1637">100</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1638" data-end="1671">
<p data-start="1640" data-end="1671">Admissions (<code data-start="1652" data-end="1661">hadm_id</code>): <strong data-start="1664" data-end="1671">275</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1672" data-end="1704">
<p data-start="1674" data-end="1704">ICU stays (<code data-start="1685" data-end="1694">stay_id</code>): <strong data-start="1697" data-end="1704">140</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1706" data-end="1736"><strong data-start="1706" data-end="1736">“Recidivism” is measurable</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1737" data-end="1876">
<li data-start="1737" data-end="1783">
<p data-start="1739" data-end="1783">Patients with <strong data-start="1753" data-end="1769">&gt;1 admission</strong>: <strong data-start="1771" data-end="1783">48 / 100</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1784" data-end="1829">
<p data-start="1786" data-end="1829">Patients with <strong data-start="1800" data-end="1815">&gt;1 ICU stay</strong>: <strong data-start="1817" data-end="1829">26 / 100</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1830" data-end="1876">
<p data-start="1832" data-end="1876">Admissions with <strong data-start="1848" data-end="1863">&gt;1 ICU stay</strong>: <strong data-start="1865" data-end="1876">9 / 275</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="1878" data-end="2091">So the open question is no longer “is recidivism even measurable?” → it is. The real open question becomes:<br data-start="1985" data-end="1988">
<strong data-start="1988" data-end="2022">what definition + time horizon</strong> (30-day readmit? ICU readmit? next admission regardless of timing?).</p>
<p data-start="2093" data-end="2119"><strong data-start="2093" data-end="2119">ED timestamps coverage</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2120" data-end="2338">
<li data-start="2120" data-end="2338">
<p data-start="2122" data-end="2199">Admissions with ED times present (both <code data-start="2161" data-end="2172">edregtime</code> and <code data-start="2177" data-end="2188">edouttime</code>): <strong data-start="2191" data-end="2199">~66%</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2202" data-end="2338">
<li data-start="2202" data-end="2338">
<p data-start="2204" data-end="2338">So ED-flow work is possible <strong data-start="2232" data-end="2248">for a subset</strong>, and missing ED times likely reflect non-ED pathways (transfers, scheduled admits, etc.).</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2340" data-end="2382"><strong data-start="2340" data-end="2382">Event table density is not the limiter</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2383" data-end="2691">
<li data-start="2383" data-end="2492">
<p data-start="2385" data-end="2450"><code data-start="2385" data-end="2398">chartevents</code>: <strong data-start="2400" data-end="2416">668,862 rows</strong> (all <strong data-start="2422" data-end="2429">140</strong> ICU stays have some)</p>
<ul data-start="2453" data-end="2492">
<li data-start="2453" data-end="2492">
<p data-start="2455" data-end="2492">Median <strong data-start="2462" data-end="2492">~2,520 chart rows per stay</strong></p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2493" data-end="2560">
<p data-start="2495" data-end="2560"><code data-start="2495" data-end="2506">labevents</code>: <strong data-start="2508" data-end="2524">107,727 rows</strong> (labs exist for <strong data-start="2541" data-end="2548">252</strong> admissions)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2561" data-end="2624">
<p data-start="2563" data-end="2624"><code data-start="2563" data-end="2576">inputevents</code>: <strong data-start="2578" data-end="2593">20,404 rows</strong> (events for <strong data-start="2606" data-end="2613">138</strong> ICU stays)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2625" data-end="2691">
<p data-start="2627" data-end="2691"><code data-start="2627" data-end="2644">procedureevents</code>: <strong data-start="2646" data-end="2660">1,468 rows</strong> (events for <strong data-start="2673" data-end="2680">138</strong> ICU stays)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2693" data-end="2927">So your bigger constraint is <strong data-start="2722" data-end="2729">not</strong> “not enough data.”<br data-start="2748" data-end="2751">
It’s <strong data-start="2756" data-end="2763">(a)</strong> “N=100 patients for generalizable modeling” and <strong data-start="2812" data-end="2819">(b)</strong> “feature leakage + dimensionality” (too many measurements, too easy to accidentally use post-outcome info).</p>
<hr data-start="2929" data-end="2932">

"""Business Understanding Overview
Introduction

Welcome to the Business Understanding phase of CRISP-DM! This phase represents the foundation of every successful data science project. Think of it as the compass that guides your entire journey - without proper business understanding, even the most sophisticated models and cleanest data will fail to deliver meaningful value.

In this module, you'll explore why the Business Understanding phase is critical, understand its four key tasks, and see how it sets the stage for all subsequent work in the CRISP-DM lifecycle.
Required Readings from CRISP-DM Guide

To deepen your understanding of the Business Understanding phase, please read the following sections from the CRISP-DM Guide:

Reference Model (pages 13-17): Provides concise definitions of each task and output in the Business Understanding phase.

User Guide (pages 30-37): Offers detailed guidance on how to perform each task, including specific activities, common pitfalls, and practical advice.

Business Understanding Outputs (page 57-58): Describes the purpose and contents of reports typically produced during this phase.

These readings will provide the detailed framework that supports the conceptual overview presented here.
Step-by-step data mining guide
Pete Chapman (NCR), Julian Clinton (SPSS), Randy Kerber (NCR),
Thomas Khabaza (SPSS), Thomas Reinartz (DaimlerChrysler),
Colin Shearer (SPSS) and Rüdiger Wirth (DaimlerChrysler)
CRISP-DM 1.0
