Purpose: Record key project decisions (what, why, tradeoffs) so future-me (and graders) can trace scope, assumptions, and reasoning.

---

## D001 — Project selection: ICU Patient Care Analysis (MIMIC-IV Demo)
- **Decision:** Use the ICU Patient Care Analysis dataset (MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo) as the course case study.
- **Date:** 2026-01-26
- **Options considered:**
  - COVID Drivers: Pennsylvania Traffic Safety
  - Consumer Product Safety Analysis
  - POGOH Bike Share Growth Analysis
  - BYOD (not pursued)
- **Rationale:**
  - Closest alignment to my professional domain (healthcare operations + QI analytics)
  - Realistic clinical complexity (linked tables, missingness, irregular measurements) without “data archaeology” overhead
  - Strong documentation and stable schemas support reproducibility and CRISP-DM deliverables
  - Portfolio-safe (no HIPAA/EHR exposure)
- **Tradeoffs / risks:**
  - Small sample size (~100 patients) limits complex modeling and generalization
  - Some outcomes/questions (e.g., throughput demand curves) may be infeasible due to limited coverage and missing timestamp patterns
  - De-identified date shifting preserves within-patient intervals but limits true calendar-time analyses across patients
- **What would change my mind:**
  - The demo subset is too sparse for a rigorous, defensible analysis (e.g., key tables mostly empty, outcomes too rare, or timestamps too incomplete)
  - The project cannot produce practical, evidence-based insights consistent with the course success criteria

---

## D002 — Analysis posture: QI-style framing (operations + clinical relevance)
- **Decision:** Frame the work as a quality-improvement oriented analysis (actionable insights + operational relevance), not purely academic modeling.
- **Date:** 2026-01-26
- **Options considered:**
  - Pure prediction-first approach (maximize model performance)
  - Descriptive clinical epidemiology-style report
  - QI/ops style: combine descriptive + interpretable models + practical recommendations
- **Rationale:**
  - Matches stakeholder needs in the provided context (medical director + hospital admin)
  - Matches how decisions are actually made in hospitals (interpretation + process improvement, not just “best AUC”)
- **Tradeoffs / risks:**
  - Risk of over-claiming causal impact from observational data (must be explicit about limitations)
  - QI framing requires careful language to avoid “perverse incentives” and political misinterpretation
- **What would change my mind:**
  - If EDA shows outcome/predictor structure supports a clearer predictive task that is easier to validate and explain

---

## D003 — Unit of analysis: keep options open until EDA confirms feasibility
- **Decision:** Do not lock the unit of analysis yet; shortlist:
  - ICU stay-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">stay_id</code>)
  - Hospital admission-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">hadm_id</code>)
  - Patient-level (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">subject_id</code>)
- **Date:** 2026-01-26
- **Rationale:**
  - Different questions map naturally to different grains (LOS and interventions at ICU-stay level; comorbidity/history at admission/patient level)
  - Small N means the “right” grain may be dictated by event availability and missingness
- **Tradeoffs / risks:**
  - Delays committing to a single modeling target until data feasibility is established
- **What would change my mind:**
  - Clear EDA signal that one grain has adequate coverage and produces a cleaner, defensible outcome definition

---

## D004 — Repository hygiene: keep raw data out of Git
- **Decision:** Do not commit raw MIMIC files to Git; document how to obtain and place them locally.
- **Date:** 2026-01-26
- **Rationale:**
  - Avoid accidental exposure, reduce repo bloat, and keep workflows reproducible
  - Align with common DS best practices (raw data is read-only and typically excluded from version control)
- **Tradeoffs / risks:**
  - Requires setup steps for anyone reproducing the work
- **What would change my mind:**
  - Only if course instructions explicitly require bundling datasets in the submission ZIP (then include in ZIP but still not in Git)"""  colaborate with me ask me the questions I need to answer and Hi Kriselle,
Thanks for following up. I'm not aware of any formally published LOS targets for our ED, though Colette or someone else on this email chain may have an additional perspective... but my view is that if we do set goals, they really should apply to the sub-cycle times the ED directry controls rather than the undifferentiated overal LOS. I'l explain below. 

To help frame the discussion, I'm sharing national benchmarks and our own current metrics. For context, these benchmarks come from the Academy of Administrators in Academic Emergency Medicine (AAAEM), a long-standing national benchmarking program for academic EDs developed in collaboration with leaders across major academic medical centers. Our Chair, Dr. Fox, shared the latest AAAEM deck with me earlier this year when I requested it to support a related analysis. The benchmark metrics I am citing come from slide 44 in that deck.

AAAEM national LOS benchmarks (median)

    Discarged: 6.2 hr total (1.2 arrival-to-provider, 4.0 provider-to-decision, 1.0 decision-to-depart)
    Admitted: 14.1 hr total (1.2 arrival-to-provider, 5.3 provider-to-decision, 7.6 decision-to-depart/boarding)


UCI ED - quick comparisons

    Decision-to-depart (discarged): Our OTF KPI runs ~30 min... half the AAAEM 1.0 hr
    Overall LOS (discharged): ~340 hrs (5.6 hr), ~10% faster than the 6.2 hr national benchmark
    Overall LOS (admitted): ~16.6 hr median vs  14.1hr. The delta here is entirely boarding and then some.


Boarding Impact (The driver of variance)
As an example... last month we logged 28313 total boarding hours with 1,379 admits (~23.6% of arrivals) which means an average of ~20.5 hr of boarding per admit. Even if we allow for the fact that means tend to overstate central tendency vs medians (this is just the data I have readily available) our median boarding is still plausibly ~2-2.5x the AAAEM benchmark of 7.6 hr. 
Here, it's also important to note that boarding varies significantly by service... looking at our data, we can see ICU boarding has improved (relative to where it was last year (~8-9 hrs)) and is now closer to ~6 hours. Before that it was consistently ~2-3 hours for several years prior:  

meanwhile when we look at something like telemetry boarding per patient, we can see boarding here has been consistently long and well above the overall AAAEM national benchmark (~7.6 hrs):


... and that's just for the patients that get a bed.. Looking at our average LOS for admitted-but-never-had-bed-assigned (admits ultimately discharged from ED), we can see that within the last year LOS has ranged from an average of ~19 hours to ~48.7 hrs... with the bulk of that dirrectly attributable to boarding

Bottom line. LOS is not monolithic; the AAAEM framework intentionally separates arrival-to-provider, provider-to-decision, and decision-to-depart/boarding. When viewed through this lense, it's clear our ED is at or under national benchmarks on the portions it controls. The remaining gap is clearly boarding, which is driven by factors outside of the ED's control, i.e. hospital bed capacity and downstream placement.

I can certainly provide more detailed, definition-aligned pulls if needed, but I think the data here already show where the operational lever lies. To keep everyone’s effort focused and effective, we should avoid treating LOS as a single undifferentiated metric at least not without that astrix.

Luis

    This trend becomes even more apparent when we look at average ICU boarding hours per patient (i.e., total boarding hours per month divided by distinct ICU-level counts). Despite stable ICU volumes, FY2025 shows a sustained and significant increase in boarding time per patient…often double or triple historical averages.

    I believe this reflects a throughput issue, not an ED demand surge. In practice, more ICU-level care is being delivered in the ED for longer stretches while patients wait for ICU bed placement…care that legally requires a 2:1 nurse-to-patient ratio.

     

    Notably, this shift began around September 2024, which I think points to some sort of operational or policy change around that time. I realize these trends aren’t easily captured through traditional snapshots or census-based planning, but, as you can now see…the extended boarding timeframes show up clearly when we trace patient-level flow. That’s where this type of analysis can add value to the existing models.

     

    To be clear, the coefficient-based planning method previously used may still be viable…if the coefficients are revisited and recalibrated to reflect current realities. I’m happy to walk through any of this further during today’s meeting and discuss how we might better align planning assumptions with observed operations.

     

    Best,

    Luis

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="102">Yep — <strong data-start="6" data-end="83">that email is <em data-start="22" data-end="31">exactly</em> the kind of Business Understanding frame you want</strong>, because it shows:</p>
<ul data-start="104" data-end="353">
<li data-start="104" data-end="154">
<p data-start="106" data-end="154">who’s asking (execs / ops / finance leadership),</p>
</li>
<li data-start="155" data-end="239">
<p data-start="157" data-end="239">what they’re <em data-start="170" data-end="178">really</em> trying to decide (resource allocation / staffing / targets),</p>
</li>
<li data-start="240" data-end="353">
<p data-start="242" data-end="353">and the classic trap you already flagged: <strong data-start="284" data-end="352">treating LOS as one monolithic number instead of sub-cycle times</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="355" data-end="540">Below is a <strong data-start="366" data-end="385">first-pass D005</strong> you can drop into your <code data-start="409" data-end="428">docs/decisions.md</code> <em data-start="429" data-end="436">as-is</em>, plus the <strong data-start="447" data-end="462">2–3 prompts</strong> you need to answer so we can lock it down cleanly without inventing anything.</p>
<hr data-start="542" data-end="545">
<h2 data-start="547" data-end="633">D005 — Stakeholder framing and decision focus: throughput/resource utilization lens</h2>
<p data-start="635" data-end="1012"><strong data-start="635" data-end="648">Decision:</strong>
 Frame the project’s “customer request” as an operational improvement 
initiative where executive leadership (e.g., CMO/COO/CFO) and the ICU 
Medical Director need decision-support around ICU resource utilization 
and throughput, rather than a purely academic modeling exercise.<br data-start="923" data-end="926">
<strong data-start="926" data-end="935">Date:</strong> 2026-02-01 (or whatever date you want to stamp it)<br data-start="986" data-end="989">
<strong data-start="989" data-end="1012">Options considered:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1013" data-end="2170">
<li data-start="1013" data-end="1074">
<p data-start="1015" data-end="1074">Pure clinical insight framing (clinical epidemiology style)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1075" data-end="1120">
<p data-start="1077" data-end="1120">Prediction-only framing (maximize AUC/RMSE)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1121" data-end="1217">
<p data-start="1123" data-end="1217">Ops/QI framing (exec decision support, resource utilization, actionable levers)<br>
<strong data-start="1203" data-end="1217">Rationale:</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1218" data-end="1350">
<p data-start="1220" data-end="1350">Mirrors how hospital analytics 
requests show up in real life: executive concern → operational metric(s)
 → “what lever do we pull?”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1351" data-end="1461">
<p data-start="1353" data-end="1461">Keeps the analysis tied to decisions (staffing/resource planning, throughput bottlenecks, realistic targets)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1462" data-end="1611">
<p data-start="1464" data-end="1611">Reinforces your “LOS is not monolithic” principle: avoid undifferentiated LOS narratives that can be misinterpreted or gamed<br>
<strong data-start="1589" data-end="1611">Tradeoffs / risks:</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1612" data-end="1715">
<p data-start="1614" data-end="1715">Risk of over-claiming causality from observational EHR data (must use careful language + limitations)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1716" data-end="1819">
<p data-start="1718" data-end="1819">Risk of the analysis becoming too broad (“everything affects LOS”) without a tight decision statement</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1820" data-end="1984">
<p data-start="1822" data-end="1984">Risk of perverse incentives if 
findings are treated as performance targets without context (e.g., 
pushing LOS down inappropriately)<br>
<strong data-start="1954" data-end="1984">What would change my mind:</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="1985" data-end="2170">
<p data-start="1987" data-end="2170">If the demo dataset can’t support 
operationally meaningful sub-cycle definitions (too sparse/timestamps 
too limited), fall back to a narrower, descriptive + interpretable model
 story.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2172" data-end="2175">
<h2 data-start="2177" data-end="2272">Convert your real-world example into 2–3 bullets for the Business Understanding “Background”</h2>
<p data-start="2273" data-end="2364">You can paraphrase the email chain like this (no PHI/PII, no screenshots, no names needed):</p>
<ul data-start="2366" data-end="2847">
<li data-start="2366" data-end="2527">
<p data-start="2368" data-end="2527">Executive/ops leadership requests 
operational targets tied to staffing/productivity models (resource 
allocation), using LOS/boarding-style metrics as inputs.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2528" data-end="2696">
<p data-start="2530" data-end="2696">Key analytic risk: treating LOS as a
 single undifferentiated metric can misattribute responsibility and 
obscure the true operational lever (sub-cycle times matter).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2697" data-end="2847">
<p data-start="2699" data-end="2847">The analysis goal is decision support: identify <em data-start="2747" data-end="2754">which</em> components drive variance and where intervention is plausible vs outside the unit’s control.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2849" data-end="2988"><em data-start="2849" data-end="2988">(Also:
 don’t paste that original email text into the repo—strip 
names/emails/phone numbers if you keep it as a “real-world analog” 
note.)</em></p>
<hr data-start="2990" data-end="2993">
<h1 data-start="2995" data-end="3041">Two questions to “lock” D005 (so it’s crisp)</h1>
<p data-start="3043" data-end="3068">Reply with short bullets:</p>
<ol data-start="3070" data-end="3148">
<li data-start="3070" data-end="3148">
<p data-start="3073" data-end="3148"><strong data-start="3073" data-end="3138">What is the primary decision you want your project to inform?</strong> Pick one:</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="3149" data-end="3504">
<li data-start="3149" data-end="3276">
<p data-start="3151" data-end="3276">A) “Which ICU patient cohorts consume disproportionate ICU resources (LOS/utilization), and what early factors predict that?”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3277" data-end="3394">
<p data-start="3279" data-end="3394">B) “Which care-process components (sub-cycle times) drive prolonged ICU stays, and where are the plausible levers?”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3395" data-end="3504">
<p data-start="3397" data-end="3504">C) “How should leadership interpret ICU performance metrics to avoid misattribution / perverse incentives?”</p>
</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2" data-start="3506" data-end="3608">
<li data-start="3506" data-end="3608">
<p data-start="3509" data-end="3608"><strong data-start="3509" data-end="3573">What’s your ICU analog to the ED ‘sub-cycle time’ framework?</strong> (1–3 items)<br>
Examples (you choose):</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="3609" data-end="3825">
<li data-start="3609" data-end="3700">
<p data-start="3611" data-end="3700">time from ICU admit → first key intervention (ventilation/vasopressors/antibiotics proxy)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3701" data-end="3767">
<p data-start="3703" data-end="3767">time in ICU on specific high-intensity supports (vent, pressors)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3768" data-end="3825">
<p data-start="3770" data-end="3825">ICU admit → ICU discharge readiness (proxy) / discharge</p>
</li>
</ul>
<ol start="3" data-start="3827" data-end="3878">
<li data-start="3827" data-end="3878">
<p data-start="3830" data-end="3878"><strong data-start="3830" data-end="3878">Who “judges” business success in your story?</strong></p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="3879" data-end="3915">
<li data-start="3879" data-end="3915">
<p data-start="3881" data-end="3915">Exec sponsor? ICU director? Joint?</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3917" data-end="4059">Once you answer those, I’ll rewrite
 D005 with a tight, unambiguous “decision statement” and success 
criteria language that matches your style.</p>
<p data-start="4061" data-end="4195">If you want, after D005 is locked we’ll do <strong data-start="4104" data-end="4131">D006 (primary endpoint)</strong> next, because that’s the other big “analysis paralysis killer.”</p>
<p data-start="4197" data-end="4373">(Entities I’m anchoring to your context once, for clarity: <span class="hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline"><span class="whitespace-normal">UCI Health</span></span>, <span class="hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline"><span class="whitespace-normal">CRISP-DM</span></span>, <span class="hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline"><span class="whitespace-normal">MIMIC-IV</span></span>.)</p>

wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="142">Got it — with your answers, D005 can be <strong data-start="40" data-end="97">tight, decision-oriented, and explicitly cohort-first</strong> without drifting into “we’ll do everything.”</p>
<p data-start="144" data-end="307">Here’s a cleaned-up D005 you can 
paste into your Decisions Log, plus a commit message, and then the next 
two “locking” questions for D006/D007 so we keep momentum.</p>
<hr data-start="309" data-end="312">
<h2 data-start="314" data-end="406">D005 — Decision focus: cohort-based ICU resource consumption + early predictors (QI lens)</h2>
<ul data-start="408" data-end="2606">
<li data-start="408" data-end="600">
<p data-start="410" data-end="600"><strong data-start="410" data-end="423">Decision:</strong> Frame the project around an ICU Director–driven QI/ops question: <strong data-start="489" data-end="600">which ICU patient subtypes consume disproportionate resources, and what early factors predict that pattern?</strong></p>
</li>
<li data-start="601" data-end="623">
<p data-start="603" data-end="623"><strong data-start="603" data-end="612">Date:</strong> 2026-02-01</p>
</li>
<li data-start="624" data-end="775">
<p data-start="626" data-end="775"><strong data-start="626" data-end="669">Primary stakeholder / judge of success:</strong> ICU Medical Director (exec leadership is a secondary audience, but ICU Director is the primary evaluator)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="776" data-end="1028">
<p data-start="778" data-end="801"><strong data-start="778" data-end="801">Options considered:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="804" data-end="1028">
<li data-start="804" data-end="860">
<p data-start="806" data-end="860">Pure clinical description (epidemiology-style summary)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="863" data-end="909">
<p data-start="865" data-end="909">Prediction-only (optimize model performance)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="912" data-end="1028">
<p data-start="914" data-end="1028">Cohort-first QI framing (subtypes → differences in utilization/outcomes → early predictors → interpretable levers)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1029" data-end="1409">
<p data-start="1031" data-end="1045"><strong data-start="1031" data-end="1045">Rationale:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1048" data-end="1409">
<li data-start="1048" data-end="1167">
<p data-start="1050" data-end="1167">Matches how real hospital questions arrive: operational pressure → identify the drivers → focus on actionable levers.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1170" data-end="1268">
<p data-start="1172" data-end="1268">Encourages <strong data-start="1183" data-end="1205">sub-cycle thinking</strong> (not treating utilization/LOS as one undifferentiated metric).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1271" data-end="1409">
<p data-start="1273" data-end="1409">Supports a defensible narrative with small N: start with <em data-start="1330" data-end="1349">group differences</em> and then test whether early indicators explain variability.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1410" data-end="2021">
<p data-start="1412" data-end="1434"><strong data-start="1412" data-end="1434">Tradeoffs / risks:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1437" data-end="2021">
<li data-start="1437" data-end="1583">
<p data-start="1439" data-end="1583"><strong data-start="1439" data-end="1461">Small sample risk:</strong> subtype counts may be too small for separate models; may require fewer buckets or pooled modeling with cohort indicators.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1586" data-end="1711">
<p data-start="1588" data-end="1711"><strong data-start="1588" data-end="1614">Data feasibility risk:</strong> “recidivism” / ICU return rates may be limited by the demo subset structure and event frequency.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1714" data-end="1866">
<p data-start="1716" data-end="1866"><strong data-start="1716" data-end="1742">Causal overreach risk:</strong> observational EHR data → must avoid implying interventions <em data-start="1802" data-end="1810">caused</em> changes; stick to association and plausible mechanisms.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1869" data-end="2021">
<p data-start="1871" data-end="2021"><strong data-start="1871" data-end="1899">Perverse-incentive risk:</strong> findings could be misread as performance targets (e.g., “shorten LOS”) without clinical nuance; language must be careful.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2022" data-end="2314">
<p data-start="2024" data-end="2067"><strong data-start="2024" data-end="2067">Decision statement (what this enables):</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2070" data-end="2314">
<li data-start="2070" data-end="2184">
<p data-start="2072" data-end="2184">Compare ICU subtypes (e.g., trauma/neuro/cardiac/sepsis/other) on <strong data-start="2138" data-end="2162">resource utilization</strong> and related outcomes.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2187" data-end="2314">
<p data-start="2189" data-end="2314">Identify early-encounter features (first-hours labs/vitals/interventions) that predict high utilization within/among cohorts.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2315" data-end="2606">
<p data-start="2317" data-end="2347"><strong data-start="2317" data-end="2347">What would change my mind:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2350" data-end="2606">
<li data-start="2350" data-end="2480">
<p data-start="2352" data-end="2480">If cohort sizes or table coverage are too sparse, pivot to fewer cohorts (or a single pooled model with minimal stratification).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2483" data-end="2606">
<p data-start="2485" data-end="2606">If “early window” data density is insufficient to avoid leakage, shift to a simpler descriptive + interpretable approach.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="2608" data-end="2726"><em data-start="2608" data-end="2726">(If you mention the dataset name in the log, keep it consistent: <span class="hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline"><span class="whitespace-normal">MIMIC-IV</span></span> demo subset.)</em></p>
<hr data-start="2728" data-end="2731">
<h2 data-start="2733" data-end="2824">Practical “sub-cycle” candidates you already named (for your Business Understanding doc)</h2>
<p data-start="2825" data-end="2921">These are good because they map to operational levers without pretending you control everything:</p>
<ul data-start="2923" data-end="3115">
<li data-start="2923" data-end="2968">
<p data-start="2925" data-end="2968">ICU admit → ICU discharge (overall ICU LOS)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2969" data-end="3041">
<p data-start="2971" data-end="3041">Vent-related: time on vent / weaning time (if vent proxy is available)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3042" data-end="3115">
<p data-start="3044" data-end="3115">Procedure-driven: ICU admit → key procedure completed (if identifiable)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="3117" data-end="3233">You’re not committing yet — you’re recording <strong data-start="3162" data-end="3186">candidate sub-cycles</strong> that reflect how ICU pathways actually differ.</p>
<hr data-start="3235" data-end="3238">
<h2 data-start="3240" data-end="3279">Suggested commit title + description</h2>
<p data-start="3281" data-end="3362"><strong data-start="3281" data-end="3291">Title:</strong> <code data-start="3292" data-end="3336">docs: add D005 cohort-first ICU QI framing</code><br data-start="3336" data-end="3339">
<strong data-start="3339" data-end="3362">Description (body):</strong></p>
<ul data-start="3363" data-end="3623">
<li data-start="3363" data-end="3452">
<p data-start="3365" data-end="3452">Add D005 to Decisions Log: cohort-based resource utilization focus + early predictors</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3453" data-end="3517">
<p data-start="3455" data-end="3517">Clarify ICU Director as primary stakeholder/judge of success</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3518" data-end="3623">
<p data-start="3520" data-end="3623">Record risks: small N, sparse cohort counts, recidivism feasibility, causal/perverse-incentive language</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3625" data-end="3628">
<h2 data-start="3630" data-end="3708">Next: D006 + D007 (2 quick questions each, then I’ll write the log entries)</h2>
<h3 data-start="3710" data-end="3759">D006 — Primary “resource consumption” outcome</h3>
<p data-start="3760" data-end="3827">Pick <strong data-start="3765" data-end="3780">one primary</strong> and 1 secondary (so you don’t boil the ocean):</p>
<ol data-start="3829" data-end="3859">
<li data-start="3829" data-end="3859">
<p data-start="3832" data-end="3859">Primary outcome (choose 1):</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="3860" data-end="3976">
<li data-start="3860" data-end="3880">
<p data-start="3862" data-end="3880">A) ICU LOS (hours)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3881" data-end="3931">
<p data-start="3883" data-end="3931">B) Prolonged ICU LOS flag (e.g., &gt; X percentile)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3932" data-end="3976">
<p data-start="3934" data-end="3976">C) Vent duration / vent-days (if feasible)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2" data-start="3978" data-end="4010">
<li data-start="3978" data-end="4010">
<p data-start="3981" data-end="4010">Secondary outcome (choose 1):</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="4011" data-end="4164">
<li data-start="4011" data-end="4070">
<p data-start="4013" data-end="4070">A) In-hospital mortality (only if event count isn’t tiny)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4071" data-end="4122">
<p data-start="4073" data-end="4122">B) ICU readmission/bounceback (only if supported)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4123" data-end="4164">
<p data-start="4125" data-end="4164">C) Hospital LOS (admission → discharge)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-start="4166" data-end="4228">D007 — Cohort definition approach (how we bucket subtypes)</h3>
<ol data-start="4229" data-end="4294">
<li data-start="4229" data-end="4294">
<p data-start="4232" data-end="4294">Are cohorts <strong data-start="4244" data-end="4258">ICD-driven</strong> (diagnosis-based) as your baseline?</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="4295" data-end="4419">
<li data-start="4295" data-end="4348">
<p data-start="4297" data-end="4348">A) Yes: primary ICD grouping per ICU stay/admission</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4349" data-end="4419">
<p data-start="4351" data-end="4419">B) Hybrid: ICD + key interventions (vent, pressors, major procedure)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2" data-start="4421" data-end="4486">
<li data-start="4421" data-end="4486">
<p data-start="4424" data-end="4486">How many buckets are you willing to keep <em data-start="4465" data-end="4485">for the first pass</em>?</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul data-start="4487" data-end="4543">
<li data-start="4487" data-end="4513">
<p data-start="4489" data-end="4513">A) 3–4 (safer for N≈100)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4514" data-end="4543">
<p data-start="4516" data-end="4543">B) 5–6 (richer but riskier)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="4545" data-end="4678">Answer those bullets, and I’ll 
draft D006 + D007 in the same style as D001–D005, without inventing 
anything you haven’t already said.</p>

class="flex w-full flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full wrap-break-word dark markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="79">Perfect — that gives us clean, defensible “scope locks” without overcommitting.</p>
<p data-start="81" data-end="197">Below are <strong data-start="91" data-end="99">D006</strong> and <strong data-start="104" data-end="112">D007</strong> written in the same style as D001–D005. Paste them straight into your Decisions Log.</p>
<hr data-start="199" data-end="202">
<h2 data-start="204" data-end="279">D006 — Primary outcome: ICU LOS (hours), with prolonged LOS as secondary</h2>
<ul data-start="280" data-end="1684">
<li data-start="280" data-end="497">
<p data-start="282" data-end="497"><strong data-start="282" data-end="295">Decision:</strong> Use <strong data-start="300" data-end="328">ICU length of stay (LOS)</strong> as the primary outcome, measured <strong data-start="362" data-end="391">ICU admit → ICU discharge</strong> (hours). Use <strong data-start="405" data-end="426">prolonged ICU LOS</strong> (e.g., high-percentile / threshold-based flag) as a secondary outcome.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="498" data-end="520">
<p data-start="500" data-end="520"><strong data-start="500" data-end="509">Date:</strong> 2026-02-01</p>
</li>
<li data-start="521" data-end="647">
<p data-start="523" data-end="556"><strong data-start="523" data-end="556">Options considered (primary):</strong></p>
<ul data-start="559" data-end="647">
<li data-start="559" data-end="576">
<p data-start="561" data-end="576">ICU LOS (hours)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="579" data-end="603">
<p data-start="581" data-end="603">Prolonged ICU LOS flag</p>
</li>
<li data-start="606" data-end="647">
<p data-start="608" data-end="647">Vent duration / vent-days (if feasible)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="648" data-end="1059">
<p data-start="650" data-end="664"><strong data-start="650" data-end="664">Rationale:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="667" data-end="1059">
<li data-start="667" data-end="772">
<p data-start="669" data-end="772">ICU LOS is the most direct, widely understood proxy for ICU resource utilization and throughput burden.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="775" data-end="946">
<p data-start="777" data-end="946">A prolonged LOS indicator provides a 
“QI-friendly” framing (“who becomes long-stay”) that is often more 
operationally actionable than only modeling a continuous outcome.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="949" data-end="1059">
<p data-start="951" data-end="1059">Works with a cohort-first approach: compare LOS distributions across cohorts, then explore early predictors.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1060" data-end="1453">
<p data-start="1062" data-end="1084"><strong data-start="1062" data-end="1084">Tradeoffs / risks:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1087" data-end="1453">
<li data-start="1087" data-end="1212">
<p data-start="1089" data-end="1212">LOS is influenced by downstream constraints and clinical complexity; must avoid implying the ICU “controls” LOS end-to-end.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1215" data-end="1338">
<p data-start="1217" data-end="1338">Prolonged LOS threshold choice can be arbitrary; must document how threshold is defined (e.g., percentile-based) and why.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1341" data-end="1453">
<p data-start="1343" data-end="1453">Small N may limit stability of any predictive modeling; descriptive + interpretable approaches may be favored.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1454" data-end="1684">
<p data-start="1456" data-end="1486"><strong data-start="1456" data-end="1486">What would change my mind:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1489" data-end="1684">
<li data-start="1489" data-end="1564">
<p data-start="1491" data-end="1564">If EDA shows LOS timestamps are unreliable/incomplete for too many stays.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1567" data-end="1684">
<p data-start="1569" data-end="1684">If event counts for prolonged LOS are too small (e.g., very few “long-stay” cases) to support even simple modeling.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="1686" data-end="1689">
<h2 data-start="1691" data-end="1773">D007 — Cohort strategy: hybrid ICD + interventions, using 3–4 buckets initially</h2>
<ul data-start="1774" data-end="3204">
<li data-start="1774" data-end="2026">
<p data-start="1776" data-end="2026"><strong data-start="1776" data-end="1789">Decision:</strong> Define ICU subtypes using a <strong data-start="1818" data-end="1837">hybrid approach</strong>: diagnoses (ICD-based) augmented with key <strong data-start="1880" data-end="1897">interventions</strong> (e.g., vent/procedure proxies where available). Start with <strong data-start="1957" data-end="1979">3–4 coarse buckets</strong> for the first pass to avoid over-segmentation.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2027" data-end="2049">
<p data-start="2029" data-end="2049"><strong data-start="2029" data-end="2038">Date:</strong> 2026-02-01</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2050" data-end="2233">
<p data-start="2052" data-end="2075"><strong data-start="2052" data-end="2075">Options considered:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2078" data-end="2233">
<li data-start="2078" data-end="2117">
<p data-start="2080" data-end="2117">ICD-only cohorting (diagnosis-driven)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2120" data-end="2160">
<p data-start="2122" data-end="2160">Hybrid cohorting (ICD + interventions)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2163" data-end="2233">
<p data-start="2165" data-end="2233">Unsupervised clustering (phenotyping) as a later/optional refinement</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2234" data-end="2596">
<p data-start="2236" data-end="2250"><strong data-start="2236" data-end="2250">Rationale:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2253" data-end="2596">
<li data-start="2253" data-end="2389">
<p data-start="2255" data-end="2389">ICD alone may miss meaningful 
pathway differences driven by care processes (e.g., ventilation, 
procedure-timing, escalation patterns).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2392" data-end="2493">
<p data-start="2394" data-end="2493">Hybrid definition better matches “real ICU mental models” (clinical + operational pathway signals).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2496" data-end="2596">
<p data-start="2498" data-end="2596">3–4 buckets is statistically safer with N≈100 and keeps the story interpretable for a QI audience.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2597" data-end="2929">
<p data-start="2599" data-end="2621"><strong data-start="2599" data-end="2621">Tradeoffs / risks:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2624" data-end="2929">
<li data-start="2624" data-end="2717">
<p data-start="2626" data-end="2717">Hybrid definitions can become subjective; must document rules clearly and keep them simple.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2720" data-end="2823">
<p data-start="2722" data-end="2823">Intervention data may be sparse; cohorting rules must degrade gracefully if a table is missing/empty.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2826" data-end="2929">
<p data-start="2828" data-end="2929">Coarse buckets may hide important heterogeneity; acceptable early tradeoff for stability and clarity.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2930" data-end="3204">
<p data-start="2932" data-end="2962"><strong data-start="2932" data-end="2962">What would change my mind:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2965" data-end="3204">
<li data-start="2965" data-end="3056">
<p data-start="2967" data-end="3056">If ICD or intervention fields are too incomplete to support consistent cohort assignment.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3059" data-end="3204">
<p data-start="3061" data-end="3204">If EDA shows one bucket dominates 
or buckets collapse (e.g., too few cases), forcing fewer buckets or a 
pooled analysis with cohort indicators.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3206" data-end="3209">
<h3 data-start="3211" data-end="3244">Tiny “next commit” suggestion</h3>
<p data-start="3245" data-end="3327"><strong data-start="3245" data-end="3255">Title:</strong> <code data-start="3256" data-end="3313">docs: add D006 outcome + D007 cohort strategy decisions</code><br data-start="3313" data-end="3316">
<strong data-start="3316" data-end="3325">Body:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="3328" data-end="3508">
<li data-start="3328" data-end="3383">
<p data-start="3330" data-end="3383">Add D006 (ICU LOS primary; prolonged LOS secondary)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3384" data-end="3444">
<p data-start="3386" data-end="3444">Add D007 (hybrid ICD+interventions; 3–4 initial cohorts)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3445" data-end="3508">
<p data-start="3447" data-end="3508">Note feasibility triggers: timestamp coverage + cohort counts</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3510" data-end="3513">
<p data-start="3515" data-end="3736">If you want to keep the log <em data-start="3543" data-end="3550">extra</em> clean, the next thing to lock (D008) is: <strong data-start="3592" data-end="3622">what’s your “early window”</strong> for predictors (6h vs 12h vs 24h) and whether you’ll do “no leakage” strictly from <em data-start="3706" data-end="3715">pre-ICU</em> vs <em data-start="3719" data-end="3735">post-ICU-admit</em>.</p>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Options considered (primary):**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICU LOS (hours)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Prolonged ICU LOS flag
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Vent duration / vent-days (if feasible)

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Works with a cohort-first approach: compare LOS distributions across cohorts, then explore early predictors.

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**What would change my mind:**</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## D007 — Cohort strategy: hybrid ICD + interventions, using 3–4 buckets initially</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Decision:**</span></span><span> Define ICU subtypes using a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**hybrid approach**</span></span><span>: diagnoses (ICD-based) augmented with key </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**interventions**</span></span><span> (e.g., vent/procedure proxies where available). Start with </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**3–4 coarse buckets**</span></span><span> for the first pass to avoid over-segmentation.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Date:**</span></span><span> 2026-02-01
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Options considered:**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICD-only cohorting (diagnosis-driven)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Hybrid cohorting (ICD + interventions)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Unsupervised clustering (phenotyping) as a later/optional refinement
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Rationale:**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> ICD alone may miss meaningful pathway differences driven by care processes (e.g., ventilation, procedure-timing, escalation patterns).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Hybrid definition better matches “real ICU mental models” (clinical + operational pathway signals).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> 3–4 buckets is statistically safer with N≈100 and keeps the story interpretable for a QI audience.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Tradeoffs / risks:**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Hybrid definitions can become subjective; must document rules clearly and keep them simple.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Intervention data may be sparse; cohorting rules must degrade gracefully if a table is missing/empty.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Coarse buckets may hide important heterogeneity; acceptable early tradeoff for stability and clarity.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**What would change my mind:**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> If ICD or intervention fields are too incomplete to support consistent cohort assignment.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> If EDA shows one bucket dominates or buckets collapse (e.g., too few cases), forcing fewer buckets or a pooled analysis with cohort indicators.
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
