<p data-start="609" data-end="930">Below is a <strong data-start="620" data-end="670">Module 3 “Business Understanding” working pack</strong> you can copy straight into your repo as raw markdown. It’s <strong data-start="730" data-end="770">intentionally a first draft skeleton</strong>: it uses only what you’ve already said / decided, and where we <em data-start="834" data-end="843">haven’t</em> pinned something down yet I left <strong data-start="877" data-end="889"><code data-start="879" data-end="887">[TODO]</code></strong> placeholders instead of inventing facts.</p>
<hr data-start="932" data-end="935">
<pre class="overflow-visible! px-0!" data-start="937" data-end="12992"><div class="contain-inline-size rounded-2xl corner-superellipse/1.1 relative bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary"><div class="flex items-center text-token-text-secondary px-4 py-2 text-xs font-sans justify-between h-9 bg-token-sidebar-surface-primary select-none rounded-t-2xl corner-t-superellipse/1.1">markdown</div><div class="sticky top-[calc(var(--sticky-padding-top)+9*var(--spacing))]"><div class="absolute end-0 bottom-0 flex h-9 items-center pe-2"><div class="bg-token-bg-elevated-secondary text-token-text-secondary flex items-center gap-4 rounded-sm px-2 font-sans text-xs"><button class="flex gap-1 items-center select-none py-1" aria-label="Copy"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true" class="icon-sm"><use href="/cdn/assets/sprites-core-o8lw6oto.svg#ce3544" fill="currentColor"></use></svg>Copy code</button></div></div></div><div class="overflow-y-auto p-4" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Module 3 — Business Understanding (Working Draft Notes)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Project:**</span></span><span> ICU Patient Care Analysis (MIMIC-IV Demo)  
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**CRISP-DM Phase:**</span></span><span> Business Understanding  
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Last updated:**</span></span><span> 2026-02-01

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 0) Anchor Decisions We Already Made (so the draft stays consistent)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D001 — Project selection:**</span></span><span> ICU Patient Care Analysis using MIMIC-IV Demo (small N, de-identified, time-shifted dates preserve within-encounter intervals).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D002 — Posture:**</span></span><span> Quality-improvement style framing (actionable + operationally relevant; avoid “model-as-the-point”).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D003 — Unit of analysis:**</span></span><span> Keep options open until EDA confirms feasibility (ICU stay-level </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span> tentatively favored).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D004 — Repo hygiene:**</span></span><span> Raw data stays out of Git; document access + local placement steps.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D005 — Stakeholder frame:**</span></span><span> Executive/leadership-driven ops improvement (CMO ↔ ICU Medical Director) oriented around </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**resource utilization + throughput**</span></span><span>, not academic novelty.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D006 — Outcomes emphasis:**</span></span><span> Primary outcome family centers on </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU admit → ICU discharge**</span></span><span> (ICU LOS / ICU utilization time). Secondary sub-cycle outcomes include </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**vent weaning time**</span></span><span> (if ventilated) and </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**time-to-procedure**</span></span><span> for procedure-driven ICU stays.  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> NOTE: final operational definitions are pending quick EDA checks for availability/coverage.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**D007 — Cohorting strategy:**</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Group ICU stays into clinically meaningful pathways**</span></span><span> (e.g., trauma / neuro / cardiac / sepsis / etc.) and test whether there are meaningful differences in LOS / utilization / recidivism and the drivers behind those differences.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 1) Background (1–1.5 pages target)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1.1 Organizational / Context Description</span></span><span>
This project is framed as a hospital operations / quality-improvement analysis focused on ICU patient care patterns using a publicly available ICU dataset (MIMIC-IV Demo). The analysis is designed to mirror a realistic hospital improvement request: executive leadership is concerned about resource utilization and throughput, and the ICU Medical Director needs a defensible, clinically literate breakdown of what drives longer ICU utilization in specific cohorts.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Key constraints of the data context (MIMIC-IV Demo):**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> De-identified dataset; dates are shifted, but </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**within-patient time intervals remain meaningful**</span></span><span> for LOS/sub-cycle analyses.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Small demo sample size (~100 patients), which limits model complexity and generalization; emphasis is on defensible methods and interpretable results.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1.2 Domain and Context Assessment (Why ICU throughput/utilization matters)</span></span><span>
In real hospital operations, “LOS” is not monolithic; operational value comes from isolating actionable sub-cycle intervals and identifying which cohorts drive disproportionate utilization. This project applies that same lens in the ICU context: rather than treating ICU duration as a single number, we aim to understand the pathways and early signals that reliably associate with longer ICU resource consumption.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1.3 Problem Situation (What’s the decision pressure?)</span></span><span>
Leadership wants to understand:
1) </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Which ICU cohorts consume disproportionate ICU time/resources**</span></span><span>, and  
2) </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**What early factors predict that trajectory**</span></span><span>, so that staffing, care pathways, and operational planning can be improved.

The analysis will start with high-level cohort differences (trauma/neuro/cardiac/etc.) and then drill into plausible drivers (e.g., time-dependent labs like cultures, ventilation course, procedure wait times), subject to feasibility in the demo tables.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1.4 Why Data Science / Analytics (Why this approach?)</span></span><span>
This problem is well-suited to data-driven methods because ICU care generates structured, time-stamped events across admissions, transfers, ICU stays, labs, and bedside charting. Even in a small demo sample, a careful workflow can produce:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Cohort comparisons (descriptive + statistical testing)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Interpretable models for early risk stratification (if feasible without leakage)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Operationally meaningful sub-cycle metrics (ventilation course, procedure timing) where available

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1.5 Stakeholders (Who cares and how they use it?)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Medical Director:**</span></span><span> wants clinically credible cohort insights, drivers of prolonged ICU utilization, and actionable levers.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**CMO / executive leadership:**</span></span><span> wants a high-level, defensible story tied to resource utilization and throughput priorities.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Secondary stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> ICU nursing leadership / staffing planners: care intensity + prolonged utilization implications  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Bed management / capacity planning: understanding which cohorts tend to “run long”  
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Finance: resource utilization framing (not purely cost, but operational burden)

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Technical stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Analytics / DS practitioner (me): builds reproducible pipeline + documentation; avoids leakage; communicates uncertainty clearly.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 2) Business Objectives &amp; Success Criteria (1.5–2 pages target)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2.1 Primary Business Objective</span></span><span>
Identify ICU patient sub-cohorts (clinical pathways) that demonstrate meaningfully different ICU utilization patterns and determine which early factors are most associated with </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**disproportionate ICU resource consumption**</span></span><span>, in a way that supports QI-style operational action.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2.2 Secondary Objectives</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Characterize ICU utilization as </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**sub-cycle intervals**</span></span><span> where feasible (e.g., ventilator weaning time; time-to-procedure for procedure-driven ICU stays).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Evaluate whether certain cohorts show higher </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**recidivism**</span></span><span> (e.g., ICU bounceback / return to ICU), contingent on feasible definitions in the demo data.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Translate findings into an executive-safe narrative that avoids overclaiming causality and instead emphasizes measurable associations and operational hypotheses.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2.3 Quantitative Success Criteria (project-level, not “production”)</span></span><span>
Because this is a small demo dataset, success is defined less by maximum predictive performance and more by rigor + defensibility:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Coverage: At least </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`[TODO]%`</span></span><span> of ICU stays have sufficient timestamp coverage to compute the primary ICU utilization outcome.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Cohort comparisons: Statistical tests reported with effect sizes + uncertainty (CIs where feasible); avoid p-value fishing.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Leakage control: Early-window features defined (tentatively 6–24h) and validated to prevent target leakage.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2.4 Qualitative Success Criteria</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> The analysis is interpretable and “QI-safe”: conclusions are framed as </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**associations + operational hypotheses**</span></span><span>, not causal claims.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Cohort definitions and metric logic are transparent enough that another analyst could reproduce them from the repo.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Results map to plausible operational levers (even if only as recommendations for what to measure next in a real system).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2.5 Impact Statement (in-scope impact)</span></span><span>
Deliver a cohort-level “where the ICU time goes” story and early signal candidates that could inform staffing/capacity discussions and prompt deeper investigation in a full dataset (beyond the demo subset).

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 3) Assessment of Responsibility (1.5–2 pages target)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3.1 Legal / Regulatory</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Data source is de-identified and publicly distributed for research/education; no PHI handling in this project repo.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Practical constraint: do not attempt re-identification; do not publish anything that implies real-world identity.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3.2 Privacy / Data Protection</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Even de-identified datasets can pose re-identification risk in principle; mitigate by:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Reporting results at cohort/aggregate level
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Avoiding “rare case storytelling” that creates quasi-identifiers
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Keeping raw extracts out of Git (already captured in D004)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3.3 Bias / Fairness</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Demo sample size + ICU heterogeneity create representation risk: cohort sizes may be tiny and unstable.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Measurement bias: missingness is likely not random (some things are charted only when clinically relevant).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Mitigation: explicitly report missingness, avoid strong claims when N is small, favor interpretable methods, and treat results as hypothesis-generating.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3.4 Stakeholder Impacts / Misuse Risks</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Risk: stakeholders could misinterpret results as causal (“this cohort causes delays”) or use results to blame clinicians or services.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Mitigation: frame outputs as “where patterns appear,” attach uncertainty, and connect to operational measurement improvement rather than blame.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3.5 Concrete Mitigations (what we will actually do)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Predefine outcomes + early windows to reduce fishing and leakage.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Report effect sizes + uncertainty; avoid overfitting or complex models that can’t be justified.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Maintain a decisions log and clear metric definitions to prevent interpretive drift.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 4) Data Science Goals &amp; Success Criteria (1–1.5 pages target)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 4.1 Technical Problem Framing</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary task:**</span></span><span> cohort-stratified analysis of ICU utilization (ICU LOS / ICU time) and identification of early predictors associated with high utilization.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Candidate task types (final selection depends on EDA feasibility):**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Descriptive + hypothesis testing across pathway cohorts
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Regression/classification for “prolonged ICU utilization” defined as </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`[TODO threshold definition]`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Secondary time-to-event style analyses if sample size supports it (not committed yet)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 4.2 Target / Outcomes (current intended definitions)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary outcome family:**</span></span><span> ICU admit → ICU discharge interval (ICU utilization time)
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Secondary outcomes:**</span></span><span> ventilator weaning time (if ventilated), time-to-procedure (for procedure-driven ICU stays), recidivism/bounceback (definition TBD by table feasibility)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 4.3 Success Criteria (technical)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Model/analysis is interpretable and beats a trivial baseline (where modeling is used).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Results are stable under reasonable sensitivity checks (e.g., different cohort grouping rules; different early-window cutoffs if feasible).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 4.4 Constraints &amp; Assumptions</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Small N limits complexity; preference for methods that remain defensible with limited data.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> De-identified date shifting: no “calendar time across patients” claims; focus on within-encounter intervals.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 5) Project Plan (1–1.5 pages target)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 5.1 Phase Plan (remaining CRISP-DM phases)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data Understanding**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Confirm join keys + grain across patients/admissions/icustays/transfers.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Count entities; inspect timestamp completeness; quantify missingness.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data Preparation**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Define ICU pathway cohort rules (diagnosis-based, intervention-based, or hybrid — choose simplest defensible rule first).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Define primary outcome and early-window features (6–24h) with leakage checks.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Create analysis-ready table at chosen grain (likely </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span>).

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Modeling**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Start with descriptive + cohort comparisons.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> If feasible, build a simple interpretable model for prolonged ICU utilization (baseline logistic/linear models before anything complex).

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Evaluation**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Evaluate against success criteria: interpretability, leakage control, stability, effect sizes/uncertainty.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Identify what breaks (coverage, missingness) and rescope if needed.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Deployment (academic framing)**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> “Deployment” = reproducible notebook + documented pipeline + clear story and limitations; propose what a real hospital implementation would require.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 5.2 Risks &amp; Contingencies</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk:**</span></span><span> Cohort sizes too small for meaningful inference.  
  </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Contingency:**</span></span><span> merge cohorts into broader buckets; prioritize descriptive insights over modeling.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk:**</span></span><span> Key sub-cycle timestamps not present in demo subset.  
  </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Contingency:**</span></span><span> keep sub-cycle metrics as “nice-to-have”; focus on ICU LOS and what can be computed defensibly.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk:**</span></span><span> Leakage risk in early predictors.  
  </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Contingency:**</span></span><span> tighten window (e.g., first 6h) and/or restrict predictors to clearly early signals.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 5.3 Milestones (course-aligned)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Milestone 1: Feasibility EDA complete (counts, missingness, grain decision).

&gt; **AI use note:** This draft was assembled with help from a generative AI assistant acting as a writing/organization aid (summarizing my notes, structuring outlines, and converting brainstormed bullets into a first draft). All project decisions, interpretations, and final wording are mine.

## 1) Background / Context (project framing)

I am completing a capstone-style case study using the **ICU Patient Care Analysis** option on the **MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo** (open-access subset; N≈100 ICU patients). The dataset represents realistic EHR complexity (ICU stays, transfers, vitals, labs, diagnoses, inputs, procedures), but the demo subset is small and may be sparse for some event tables.

This project is intentionally framed with a **QI-style** narrative: the goal is to describe and analyze ICU care patterns and outcomes in a way that resembles real operational/clinical analytics work (e.g., using interval-based timestamps, clarifying assumptions, and avoiding metric framing that creates misleading incentives).

**Important dataset constraint:** MIMIC dates are **patient-shifted** for de-identification. This preserves **durations/intervals** within a patient encounter, but it limits “true calendar time” analyses across patients (e.g., real-world demand curves by hour/day across the entire cohort).

### Tables already identified as in-scope (current shortlist)
Hospital / core:
- admissions
ICU / flow:
- icustays
- transfers
Clinical events:
- labevents + d_labitems
- chartevents + d_items
- diagnoses_icd + d_icd_diagnoses
- inputevents
- procedureevents

## 2) Business Objectives (QI-style)

### Primary business objective (draft)
Translate ICU care questions into measurable objectives that can support **quality improvement thinking**: identify patterns in ICU patient care and recovery that are associated with outcomes and resource utilization.

This is explicitly a **capstone / educational** analysis using a demo dataset, so the output is best framed as:
- evidence-based descriptive insights and
- defensible analytic prototypes (methods + definitions)
that could *inform* how a real ICU QI team might measure or investigate similar questions.

### Secondary objectives (draft)
- Establish a clear, reproducible definition of ICU episodes and timelines using timestamps (ICU admit → ICU discharge; transfers).
- Explore feasibility of outcome analyses given small N (e.g., LOS distributions; mortality counts if present; transfer patterns if supported).
- Explore high-level ICU “pathway” grouping as a first-pass mental model (to be verified later): **cardiac, neuro, trauma, sepsis, other**.

## 3) Business Success Criteria (what “good” looks like for this class project)

Because this is a demo dataset and not a live implementation, success is measured by producing a clear, defensible analytic narrative:

- A reproducible, well-documented analysis workflow (repo structure + notes + clear joins and grains).
- Feasibility decisions are explicit (what is analyzable vs what is not, and why).
- Outcomes and cohorts are defined in a way that is defensible for a QI-style story *without* overstating causality.
- Clear communication of limitations (small N, missingness, de-ID date shifting, measurement bias risk).
- Practical outputs suitable for a capstone submission: report sections, tables/figures, and documented decisions.

## 4) Stakeholders + Decisions (role-play, since this is a demo dataset)

Stakeholders for the narrative are framed as ICU/QI audiences who would plausibly use this style of analysis:

- ICU clinical leadership (protocol and pathway framing)
- ICU operations / bed management (resource utilization and flow)
- Hospital quality improvement team (measurement definitions, bias/assumption tracking)

**Decisions this analysis is meant to inform (draft):**
- What outcomes and operational metrics are most defensible to monitor given available data?
- How should ICU stays be grouped into coarse “pathways” without over-segmenting?
- What early-window signals are feasible to compute without leaking future information?

# Task 2 — Assess Situation

## 5) Inventory of Resources

### Data resources (available locally)
- MIMIC-IV demo CSVs: admissions, icustays, transfers, and selected events/dim tables listed above.
- Documentation sources: MIMIC table documentation and definitions (including the note that LOINC mapping is maintained in a separate code repository rather than in-table).

### Compute / workflow resources
- Local repo with version control (GitHub) and a reproducible structure (“show your work”).
- Tooling under consideration: pandas-first EDA vs loading into Postgres for repeatable SQL EDA. (Decision not finalized yet.)

### People / domain resources
- I can sanity-check the cohort mental model with :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0} at :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1} as a reality-check (not as a data source).

## 6) Requirements, Assumptions, Constraints (draft)

### Requirements
- Keep work reproducible and well-documented for capstone grading.
- Keep raw data out of Git; document how it is obtained/placed locally.
- Use clear definitions for any metric that depends on timestamps or cohort mapping.

### Constraints
- Small dataset: demo cohort is ~100 ICU patients, limiting robust modeling and subgroup analysis.
- De-identification: shifted dates preserve within-encounter intervals but limit real “calendar-time” demand analysis.
- Table sparsity/missingness likely varies across labevents/chartevents/inputevents/procedureevents.

### Assumptions (explicit, draft)
- Timestamp sequences within a stay are meaningful for interval-based analysis (durations).
- Cohort grouping using ICD codes is a reasonable first-pass approach (to validate/adjust later).
- “Early window” feature extraction (e.g., 6h/12h/24h from ICU admit) can be done without leakage if event timestamps are sufficiently dense.

## 7) Risks + Contingencies (draft)

- **Risk: too few cases per cohort** (cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/other) → contingency: reduce to fewer buckets or analyze overall cohort only.
- **Risk: event-table sparsity / missingness** blocks key features → contingency: pivot to higher-level features (diagnoses, basic demographics, LOS/transfer patterns).
- **Risk: measurement bias** (sicker patients have more labs/vitals → missingness is not random) → contingency: acknowledge bias, consider simple sensitivity checks (e.g., measurement count as proxy).
- **Risk: leakage** from using data too late in the stay → contingency: enforce an “early window” cutoff and document it.
- **Risk: throughput/demand curves not valid** due to date shifting + incomplete coverage → contingency: avoid cross-patient “real-time demand” claims; focus on within-stay timelines and distributions.

## 8) Terminology (starter list)
- **Unit of analysis:** ICU stay (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">stay_id</code>) vs hospital admission (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">hadm_id</code>) vs patient (<code class="rounded-sm bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/10 dark:bg-(--theme-user-msg-text)/15 px-1 py-0.5 text-(--theme-user-msg-text) text-sm">subject_id</code>) — not finalized.
- **Outcome:** ICU LOS, hospital LOS, in-hospital mortality, transfer patterns/bounceback — feasibility TBD.
- **Early window:** first 6h / 12h / 24h after ICU admission (candidate cutoffs).
- **Cohort / pathway:** coarse grouping of ICU stays into cardiac/neuro/trauma/sepsis/other (first-pass mental model).

## 9) Costs / Benefits (class framing)
- “Costs”: time spent on data inventory, cleaning, and documentation; scope control due to small N and missingness.
- “Benefits”: a portfolio-safe, realistic healthcare analytics project demonstrating CRISP-DM thinking, explicit assumptions, and reproducible workflow.

- Prototype “early window” features (using events within a cutoff window after ICU admit) to support later modeling **without leakage**.

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**AI use note:**</span></span></span><span> This draft was assembled with help from a generative AI assistant acting as a writing/organization aid (structuring outlines, summarizing my notes, and converting brainstormed bullets into a first draft). All project decisions, interpretations, and final wording are mine.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Executive Summary (1 paragraph “why this exists”)</span></span><span>
This case study analyzes ICU patient care patterns using the </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo**</span></span><span> (open-access subset; ~100 ICU patients) using a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**quality-improvement (QI) style**</span></span><span> framing. The practical goal is to identify </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**which ICU patient subgroups (“pathways”) consume disproportionate ICU resources**</span></span><span> (primarily ICU length-of-stay / ICU utilization time), and to surface </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**early signals**</span></span><span> that can help explain or anticipate those prolonged trajectories—without overstating causality. Because this is a demo dataset, the deliverable is a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**defensible analytic prototype**</span></span><span>: clear metric definitions, explicit assumptions, reproducible workflow, and “QI-safe” communication of results and limitations.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section"># CRISP-DM Phase 1 — Business Understanding</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Task 1 — Determine Business Objectives</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 1) Background / Context (project framing)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 1.1 Setting and narrative frame (role-play, realistic ops request)</span></span><span>
This project is framed as the type of operational request commonly seen in hospital performance improvement work: executive leadership is concerned with </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**throughput and resource utilization**</span></span><span>, and ICU clinical leadership needs a clinically credible breakdown of what drives prolonged ICU utilization.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Narrative stakeholders (for this project’s context):**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**CMO / executive sponsor:**</span></span><span> needs an executive-safe summary and defensible metrics tied to utilization.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Medical Director:**</span></span><span> cares most about ICU-specific operational success (ICU utilization time, pathway differences, and actionable levers).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**QI / operations team:**</span></span><span> needs reproducible definitions and measurement logic.

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**Draft decision posture (QI-style):**</span></span></span><span> avoid treating “LOS” as a single monolithic metric. Where feasible, break ICU utilization into </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**sub-cycle times**</span></span><span> (e.g., ventilator weaning time, time-to-procedure) to support more actionable conversations.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 1.2 Dataset and scope</span></span><span>
I am completing a capstone-style case study using the </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Patient Care Analysis**</span></span><span> option on the </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**MIMIC-IV Clinical Database Demo**</span></span><span> (open-access subset; N≈100 ICU patients). The dataset includes realistic EHR complexity (ICU stays, transfers, vitals, labs, diagnoses, inputs, procedures), but the demo subset is small and may be sparse for some event tables.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Important dataset constraint:**</span></span><span> MIMIC dates are </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**patient-shifted**</span></span><span> for de-identification. This preserves </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**durations/intervals**</span></span><span> within a patient encounter, but it limits “true calendar time” analyses across patients (e.g., genuine demand curves by hour/day across the entire cohort).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 1.3 Why data science / analytics (justification)</span></span><span>
This problem is a good fit for analytics because ICU care produces time-stamped clinical and operational events (admissions, transfers, ICU stays, labs, charted vitals, procedures, inputs). Even with a small demo subset, a careful workflow can produce:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> defensible cohort comparisons (descriptive + statistical testing),
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> interpretable “early window” predictors (only if feasible without leakage), and
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> clear documentation of what can/cannot be supported by the data (a core QI skill).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 1.4 In-scope tables (current shortlist)</span></span><span>
Hospital / core:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`admissions`</span></span><span>

ICU / flow:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`icustays`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`transfers`</span></span><span>

Clinical events:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`labevents`</span></span><span> + </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`d_labitems`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`chartevents`</span></span><span> + </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`d_items`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`diagnoses_icd`</span></span><span> + </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`d_icd_diagnoses`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`inputevents`</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`procedureevents`</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO — refine]**</span></span></span><span> Confirm which of these are sufficiently populated in the </span><span><span class="hljs-emphasis">*demo*</span></span><span> subset to support analysis; drop/replace tables if sparsity is severe.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 2) Business Objectives (QI-style)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 2.1 Primary business objective (clean “North Star” statement)</span></span><span>
Identify ICU patient subtypes (“pathways”) that show </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**meaningfully different ICU utilization patterns**</span></span><span> and determine which </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**early factors**</span></span><span> are associated with </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**disproportionate ICU resource consumption**</span></span><span>, using defensible definitions and QI-safe interpretation.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 2.2 Secondary objectives (supporting value)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Establish a reproducible definition of ICU episodes and timelines using timestamps (ICU admit → ICU discharge; transfers).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Evaluate feasibility of sub-cycle metrics that are operationally meaningful:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Ventilator weaning time**</span></span><span> (if ventilated and charting supports it).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Time-to-procedure**</span></span><span> for procedure-driven ICU stays (if procedure timestamps exist).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Evaluate “recidivism” feasibility (e.g., ICU bounceback) as an optional analysis if the demo dataset supports a defensible definition.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Prototype an “early window” feature approach (e.g., first 6h/12h/24h after ICU admit) to avoid leakage and support interpretable risk signals.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 2.3 Decisions this analysis is meant to inform (tight and explicit)</span></span><span>
This analysis is designed to inform </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**measurement and prioritization decisions**</span></span><span> (not bedside decisions):
1) </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Which ICU pathways should be prioritized for deeper QI work**</span></span><span> because they consume disproportionate ICU time/resources?
2) </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Which sub-cycle intervals (ventilation course, time-to-procedure, etc.) appear to drive prolonged ICU utilization**</span></span><span> for those pathways?
3) </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Which early signals are feasible and defensible**</span></span><span> to compute (without leakage) that could help anticipate prolonged utilization?

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO — refine]**</span></span></span><span> Reduce to 1–2 decision statements if needed for tighter grading alignment.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 3) Business Success Criteria (what “good” looks like in this class project)</span></span><span>

Because this is a demo dataset (not a live implementation), success is defined by </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**defensibility + reproducibility + correct framing**</span></span><span> more than maximum predictive performance.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 3.1 Quantitative success criteria (right-sized for N≈100)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Coverage:**</span></span><span> At least </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO]%**</span></span><span> of ICU stays have sufficient timestamp coverage to compute the primary ICU utilization metric.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Cohort feasibility:**</span></span><span> At least </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO]**</span></span><span> pathway groups have enough cases to support descriptive comparison (with transparent “N too small” handling).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Leakage control:**</span></span><span> Early-window features are explicitly bounded (e.g., first 6–24h) and audited to prevent use of “future information.”
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Stability checks:**</span></span><span> Key findings remain directionally consistent under simple sensitivity checks (e.g., alternate bucket definitions, alternate early-window cutoff), where feasible.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 3.2 Qualitative success criteria</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Reproducible workflow:**</span></span><span> repo structure, documented joins/keys/grain, and “show your work” logic.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Explicit feasibility decisions:**</span></span><span> what is analyzable vs not analyzable is clearly stated with evidence (missingness, sparsity).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**QI-safe communication:**</span></span><span> results are framed as associations + operational hypotheses; no causal overclaiming.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Clear limitations:**</span></span><span> small N, missingness, de-ID date shifting, and measurement bias are not buried.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 4) Stakeholders (who cares, what they need, and how they’ll use outputs)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**ICU Medical Director (primary decision owner):**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Needs clinically credible pathway breakdowns and levers for improvement (e.g., sub-cycle drivers).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Success lens: ICU-specific operational performance (utilization time, avoidable delays).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**CMO / executive sponsor:**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Needs an executive-safe summary with defensible metrics and constraints.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> Success lens: throughput/resource utilization and where to invest attention.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Secondary stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> ICU nursing leadership / staffing planners: prolonged ICU utilization implies staffing intensity and operational strain.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Bed management / capacity planning: pathway mix may explain utilization differences and flow constraints.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> QI team: reusable metric definitions + measurement discipline.

</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Technical stakeholders**</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Analyst / DS practitioner (me): owns pipeline, documentation, and leakage prevention.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Task 2 — Assess Situation</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 5) Inventory of resources</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 5.1 Data resources</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> MIMIC-IV demo CSVs: admissions, icustays, transfers, and selected events/dim tables listed above.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Documentation sources: MIMIC table documentation and definitions.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 5.2 Compute/workflow resources</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Local repo with version control (GitHub) and a reproducible structure.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Tooling under consideration:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**pandas-first**</span></span><span> EDA (fast iteration),
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> or </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Postgres-first**</span></span><span> (repeatable SQL EDA and cleaner joins once stable).

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO — refine]**</span></span></span><span> Commit to a workflow choice after initial table sparsity checks.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 5.3 Domain resources</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Professional ICU/throughput analytics experience informs plausible pathways and operational “sub-cycle” thinking (used as domain intuition, not as a data source).

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 6) Requirements, assumptions, constraints</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 6.1 Requirements</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Reproducible, well-documented workflow (grading + portfolio).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Raw data stays out of Git; document how it is obtained/placed locally.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Clear definitions for any metric that depends on timestamps, joins, or cohort mapping.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 6.2 Constraints</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Small dataset: demo cohort is ~100 ICU patients → limited modeling and subgroup power.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> De-identification: patient-shifted dates → avoid cross-patient calendar-time claims.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Event-table sparsity/missingness varies across </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`labevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`chartevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`inputevents`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`procedureevents`</span></span><span>.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 6.3 Assumptions (explicit, QI-style)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Within-stay timestamp sequences are meaningful for interval-based analysis (durations).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Pathway grouping is possible using diagnoses and/or interventions (definition to be validated).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> “Early window” feature extraction can be done without leakage if event timestamps are sufficiently dense.

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO — refine]**</span></span></span><span> Convert assumptions into testable checks (e.g., “X% of stays have ≥Y charted points in first 12h”).

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 7) Risks and contingencies</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk: too few cases per cohort**</span></span><span> → contingency: reduce buckets (e.g., 3 groups instead of 5) or analyze overall cohort only.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk: event-table sparsity blocks key features**</span></span><span> → contingency: pivot to higher-level features (diagnoses, basic demographics, LOS/transfer patterns).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk: measurement bias**</span></span><span> (sicker patients measured more) → contingency: acknowledge bias; consider measurement count as a proxy; keep conclusions cautious.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk: leakage**</span></span><span> from late-stay variables → contingency: enforce early-window cutoff and document it.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Risk: sub-cycle metrics not feasible**</span></span><span> → contingency: keep them as “nice-to-have,” focus on ICU utilization time and pathway differences.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 8) Terminology (starter list)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Unit of analysis:**</span></span><span> ICU stay (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span>) vs hospital admission (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`hadm_id`</span></span><span>) vs patient (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`subject_id`</span></span><span>) — not finalized.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary outcome:**</span></span><span> ICU admit → ICU discharge interval (ICU utilization time).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Secondary outcomes (optional):**</span></span><span> ventilator weaning time; time-to-procedure; ICU bounceback/recidivism (definition TBD).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Early window:**</span></span><span> first 6h / 12h / 24h after ICU admission (candidate cutoffs).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Pathway / cohort:**</span></span><span> coarse grouping of ICU stays into clinically meaningful buckets (initial mental model: cardiac, neuro, trauma, sepsis, other).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Task 3 — Determine Data Mining Goals (technical translation)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 9) Data science goals (draft, aligned with objectives)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 9.1 Technical problem framing</span></span><span>
Primary goal is a cohort-stratified analysis of ICU utilization time, plus identification of early signals associated with prolonged utilization, if feasible.

Candidate task types (final selection depends on EDA feasibility):
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Descriptive + statistical comparisons across pathways
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Optional: simple interpretable modeling (e.g., regression / binary “prolonged utilization” classification)

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 9.2 Primary and secondary outcomes (current intent)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Primary outcome:**</span></span><span> ICU utilization time (ICU admit → ICU discharge).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Secondary outcomes:**</span></span><span> ventilator weaning time (if ventilated), time-to-procedure (procedure-driven stays), recidivism/bounceback (optional).

</span><span><span class="hljs-quote">&gt; <span class="hljs-strong">**[TODO — refine]**</span></span></span><span> Operationalize each outcome definition precisely (timestamp fields, inclusion rules, censoring rules).

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### 9.3 Data mining success criteria (draft)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Reproducible cohort construction and join logic (documented keys + grain).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Missingness/coverage summary for each event table used for features.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> If modeling is attempted:
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> honest evaluation (baselines first),
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> interpretability prioritized,
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">  -</span></span><span> performance framed as exploratory given N≈100.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Task 4 — Produce Project Plan (high-level)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">### 10) Project plan (course-aligned, specific enough to execute)</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### Phase: Data Understanding</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Build a table inventory (row counts, keys, timestamp coverage).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Confirm join keys and grain across </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`admissions`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`icustays`</span></span><span>, </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`transfers`</span></span><span>.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Missingness audit for candidate feature tables in the early window.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### Phase: Data Preparation</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Choose unit of analysis (likely </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span> unless EDA disproves feasibility).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Define pathway grouping rules (start simple, validate, iterate).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Define primary outcome and early window; implement leakage checks.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Create an analysis-ready dataset at chosen grain.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### Phase: Modeling (only if justified by feasibility)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Start with descriptive + cohort comparisons.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> If feasible, build an interpretable baseline model for prolonged utilization.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### Phase: Evaluation</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Validate success criteria: coverage, leakage control, interpretability, stability checks.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Identify what breaks and rescope transparently.

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">#### Phase: “Deployment” (academic framing)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> “Deployment” = reproducible notebook + documented pipeline + clear narrative and limitations.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">-</span></span><span> Include a short “real-world translation” section: what would be needed to implement this in an actual ICU analytics environment.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## Notes / Parking Lot (things to refine in later passes)</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Open questions (highest priority):**</span></span><span>
1) Final unit of analysis (</span><span><span class="hljs-code">`stay_id`</span></span><span> vs </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`hadm_id`</span></span><span> vs </span><span><span class="hljs-code">`subject_id`</span></span><span>)
2) Pathway grouping rule: ICD-only vs intervention-based vs hybrid
3) Early window cutoff (6h vs 12h vs 24h) based on timestamp density

<li data-start="15071" data-end="15156">
<p data-start="15073" data-end="15156">Made the <strong data-start="15082" data-end="15110">“decisions this informs”</strong> section explicit (lectures really like that).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="15157" data-end="15256">

<h2 data-start="15331" data-end="15378">Next back-and-forth (pick one to answer now)</h2>
<p data-start="15379" data-end="15490">To keep this moving like a real team workflow, answer <strong data-start="15433" data-end="15451">just these two</strong> and I’ll revise the draft immediately:</p>

<li data-start="15492" data-end="15627">
